faq.a: Dense woods surround the camp, and aggressive wild bears and prowling wolves constantly menace the workers. The attacks often force the woodcutters to flee, leaving chopped timber behind and putting timber orders at serious risk of missing shipment deadlines.
faq.q: Why is the logging camp always hiring adventurers?

faq.a: Marshal Haggard is the retired former leader of the Stormwind Guard. He stepped down from service a few years ago and now resides in a peaceful estate on the bluffs overlooking the Eastvale Logging Camp.
faq.q: Who is Marshal Haggard?

faq.a: Yes. The logging camp features an active horse-breeding stable where Alliance adventurers can purchase riding horses and riding training.
faq.q: Can you buy mounts at Eastvale Logging Camp?

text.s: Eastvale Logging Camp is a vital lumber settlement tucked into the eastern woodlands of Elwynn Forest, near the border with the Redridge Mountains. The camp supplies vital timber to Stormwind and surrounding settlements, but its operations are constantly hampered by hungry predators prowling the surrounding forests.

sec.b: Orders for timber constantly stream into Eastvale Logging Camp from buyers across the Kingdom of Stormwind, but meeting these strict deadlines is a harrowing task. The dense wilderness surrounding the camp swarms with vicious wolves and prowling bears that routinely chase lumberjacks away from their worksites, leaving valuable cut timber abandoned in the woods. Under the direction of Supervisor Raelen, the camp frequently relies on wandering adventurers to cull the encroaching beasts and retrieve fallen wood before deliveries fall fatally behind schedule.

Despite its remote location, Eastvale is more than just a logging outpost. It features several residential dwellings and bustling horse stables where travelers can purchase fine mounts. The lumber trade here is closely tied to Stormwind nobility, including Lord Joran Tremaind, whose family maintains significant business interests in the camp's timber harvest. On a nearby hill overlooking the worksite sits the quiet manor of retired Marshal Haggard, the former leader of the Stormwind Guard, who withdrew to this rustic outpost to live out his retirement away from capital politics.

subzone:echo-isles.s: Islas del Eco. Las Islas del Eco son un conjunto de islas tropicales situadas justo frente a la costa suroriental de Durotar. Colonizado originalmente por los trols de Lanza Negra tras huir de sus islas ancestrales, el archipiélago se encuentra actualmente bajo el control del médico brujo renegado Zalazane, quien expulsó a su pueblo al exilio valiéndose de magia oscura y esbirros esclavizados. Tras su huida a través del Mare Magnum junto a Thrall, la tribu Lanza Negra reclamó las Islas del Eco como su nuevo hogar. Su paz se vio truncada en repetidas ocasiones: primero por las fuerzas navales del Gran Almirante Daelin Valiente durante la invasión de Durotar por parte de Kul Tiras, y más tarde desde dentro. Poco después de que los trols repelieran la flota de Valiente, uno de sus propios médicos brujos, Zalazane, recurrió a las artes oscuras para esclavizar las mentes de sus congéneres. El caudillo Vol'jin y los Lanza Negra libres se vieron obligados a abandonar las islas una vez más, buscando refugio temporal al otro lado del estrecho en el Poblado Sen'jin.

ang.faction:Horde: Securing the Echo Isles is essential for stabilizing the southern coast of Durotar, protecting Sen'jin Village, and consolidating the young Horde's borders against naval threats and rogue mystics.
ang.race:Troll: The Echo Isles represent both the promised home of the Darkspear in Kalimdor and the bitter sting of Zalazane's betrayal. Reclaiming them is a matter of tribal survival and personal honor.

faq.a: The witch doctor Zalazane betrayed the tribe, using dark magic to strip his brethren of their free will and twist them into obedient servitors. Chieftain Vol'jin ordered an evacuation to the mainland coast of Durotar, founding Sen'jin Village as a staging ground while the tribe fights to reclaim their home.
faq.q: Why don't the Darkspear trolls live here right now?

faq.a: Zalazane is a traitorous Darkspear witch doctor who turned on his tribe. Using powerful voodoo and dark magic, he placed hexes over the islands, corrupted the local wildlife, and enslaved fellow trolls into mindless thralls.
faq.q: Who is Zalazane?

faq.a: The archipelago is infested with wild raptors, tigers, and corrupted beasts, as well as Zalazane's voodoo heaps and his mind-controlled troll minions, including hexed and voodoo trolls.
faq.q: What threats are on the islands?

faq.a: After Thrall and the Horde rescued the Darkspear tribe from a sinking island and hostile naga in the Great Sea, the trolls journeyed to Kalimdor and were granted the Echo Isles to settle alongside their orc allies.
faq.q: How did the Darkspear tribe end up on these islands originally?

text.s: The Echo Isles are a cluster of tropical islands lying just off the southeastern coast of Durotar. Originally settled by the Darkspear trolls after fleeing their ancestral islands, the archipelago is currently lost to the rogue witch doctor Zalazane, who drove his people into exile with dark magic and enslaved minions.

sec.b: Following their flight across the Great Sea alongside Thrall, the Darkspear tribe claimed the Echo Isles as their new home. Their peace was repeatedly shattered: first by the naval forces of Grand Admiral Daelin Proudmoore during Kul Tiras' invasion of Durotar, and later from within. Shortly after the trolls drove back Proudmoore's fleet, one of their own witch doctors, Zalazane, seized dark arts to enslave the minds of his kin. Chieftain Vol'jin and the free Darkspears were forced to abandon the islands once more, seeking temporary refuge across the narrow strait at Sen'jin Village.

Today, the tropical cluster is overrun by aggressive predators, tainted wildlife, and the thralls of Zalazane. Using malevolent hexes, voodoo fetishes, and ju-ju heaps placed throughout the islands, the traitorous witch doctor bends beasts and captive trolls to his will. From their encampment at Darkspear Strand, Vol'jin's scouts and warriors mount frequent sorties into the islands, determined to recover the remains of their fallen and strike down the mad mystic who stole their home.

subzone:echo-ridge-mine.s: Mina del Eco. La Mina del Eco es una pequeña excavación horadada en los acantilados noroccidentales del Valle de Villanorte. Rica en piedra y mineral, recientemente ha caído en las garras de una destructiva plaga de kóbold, lo que ha paralizado las operaciones locales de Villanorte. Oculta en las colinas sobre la Abadía de Villanorte, la Mina del Eco debía abastecer al valle con piedra y metal útiles. En su lugar, oportunistas kóbold pulularon por los túneles y expulsaron a los trabajadores locales. El Alguacil McBride considera la infestación como un riesgo de seguridad inaceptable para la tranquilidad de Villanorte y los esfuerzos de reclutamiento, enviando a los nuevos reclutas directamente a los túneles para reducir sus números y recuperar el lugar.

ang.profession:Mining: The shafts of Echo Ridge are rich in early mineral deposits, though any prospector seeking ore will have to fight through hordes of candle-bearing kobolds first.
ang.race:Human: For fresh recruits answering Stormwind's call, purging Echo Ridge Mine serves as an essential trial by fire to defend Northshire Abbey.

faq.a: Kobolds are natural burrowers drawn to dark, mineral-rich tunnels. Sensing weak defenses, they overran Echo Ridge Mine to dig for treasures and claim the territory as their own.
faq.q: Why are kobolds in Echo Ridge Mine?

faq.a: Marshal McBride at Northshire Abbey oversees efforts to clear the mine. He enlists newly arrived adventurers to scout the tunnels and cull the infesting vermin before they expand further into the valley.
faq.q: Who is trying to reclaim Echo Ridge Mine?

faq.a: The mine entrance sits in the northwestern corner of Northshire Valley, carved directly into the rocky hillside just north of the abbey vineyards.
faq.q: Where is Echo Ridge Mine located?

text.s: Echo Ridge Mine is a small excavation carved into the northwestern cliffs of Northshire Valley. Rich in stone and ore, it has recently fallen into the clutches of a destructive kobold infestation, halting Northshire's local operations.

sec.b: Tucked away in the hills above Northshire Abbey, Echo Ridge Mine was meant to supply the valley with useful stone and metal. Instead, opportunistic kobolds swarmed through the tunnels, driving out the local workers. Marshal McBride views the infestation as an unacceptable security risk to Northshire's safety and recruitment efforts, directing new recruits straight into the tunnels to cull their numbers and reclaim the site.

The occupation of Echo Ridge is part of a broader pattern of kobold encroachment spreading across Elwynn Forest. If left unchecked in the northwestern ridge, these subterranean pests threaten to disrupt Northshire's peaceful training grounds and choke off crucial resources from reaching the abbey.

subzone:elder-rise.s: Alto de los Ancestros. El Alto de los Ancestros se encuentra directamente al este de la meseta central de Cima del Trueno, accesible a través de largos puentes colgantes tanto desde High Rise como desde Middle Rise. Sirve como el corazón espiritual de la capital tauren, albergando al Círculo Cenarion, a druidas y sacerdotes tauren, y al Consejo de Ancianos gobernante. Conectado a las mesetas principales por oscilantes puentes de cuerda, el Alto de los Ancestros está dedicado a la reflexión tranquila, la sabiduría sagrada y el gobierno cívico. Los druidas y sacerdotes tauren se reúnen aquí para enseñar a los acólitos los caminos de la naturaleza y la devoción espiritual. En lo alto de esta meseta reside el Archidruida Hamuul Runatótem, el venerado líder que devolvió el druidismo al pueblo tauren y forjó estrechos lazos con el Círculo Cenarion. Junto a estos santuarios salvajes se alza la Sala de los Ancianos, donde los líderes tribales se reúnen para deliberar sobre los asuntos que afronta su incipiente capital.

ang.class:Druid: Elder Rise is the paramount home for Horde druids, serving as Arch Druid Hamuul Runetotem's sanctuary and the Cenarion Circle's regional seat in Kalimdor.
ang.race:Tauren: The rise houses the Council of Elders and spiritual guides who steer your tribes through peace, tradition, and the complex realities of the Horde.

faq.a: Elder Rise serves as the center for spiritual learning and civic deliberation in Thunder Bluff. It houses the Cenarion Circle's druids, tauren priests, the governing Council of Elders, and tribal leaders.
faq.q: What is Elder Rise used for?

faq.a: Arch Druid Hamuul Runetotem resides here. A close friend and advisor to Cairne Bloodhoof, Hamuul is the highest-ranking tauren in the Cenarion Circle and trains those called to walk the path of nature.
faq.q: Who leads the druids on Elder Rise?

faq.a: Magatha Grimtotem occupies a tent situated between the bridges. As the elder crone and chieftain of the Grimtotem tribe, she attends the Council of Elders to represent her people in Thunder Bluff, despite mutual distrust between her clan and Cairne's allies.
faq.q: Why does Magatha Grimtotem stay here?

faq.a: Elder Rise lies directly east of the city's central plateau. It can be reached via large wooden rope bridges connected to both the High Rise and the lower plateau.
faq.q: How do you reach Elder Rise?

text.s: Elder Rise sits directly east of Thunder Bluff's central plateau, reachable across long suspension bridges from both the High and Middle Rises. It serves as the spiritual heart of the tauren capital, hosting the Cenarion Circle, tauren druids and priests, and the governing Council of Elders.

sec.b: Connected to the main mesas by swaying rope bridges, Elder Rise is dedicated to quiet reflection, sacred wisdom, and civic governance. Tauren druids and priests gather here to teach acolytes the ways of nature and spiritual devotion. High atop this mesa resides Arch Druid Hamuul Runetotem, the revered leader who brought druidism back to the tauren people and forged close ties with the Cenarion Circle. Alongside these wild sanctuaries stands the Hall of Elders, where tribal leaders convene to deliberate on matters facing their fledgling capital.

Despite its role as a peaceful sanctuary, political tension lingers over the rise. Magatha Grimtotem, elder matriarch of the secretive and haughty Grimtotem tribe, maintains her residence in a hut positioned between the two bridges. While Cairne Bloodhoof extends hospitality and formal council seats to all tauren lineages, her watchful presence serves as a constant reminder that not every tribe embraces the Bloodhoof's pacifist ideals or unquestioning alliance with the Horde.

subzone:engineering-labs.s: Laboratorios de Ingeniería. Los Laboratorios de Ingeniería son una instalación de investigación y manufactura de varios niveles situada en las profundidades de Gnomeregan. Conectado con la Entrada del Taller y el Hangar de Lanzamiento, este bullicioso centro de innovación gnómica fue arrasado durante el cataclismo radiactivo de la ciudad y ahora está plagado de enloquecidos gnomos parias y artefactos mecánicos descontrolados. Construidos alrededor de una estructura mecánica central, los Laboratorios de Ingeniería abarcan dos niveles principales conectados por un elevador de carga central. En el apogeo de Gnomeregan, los manitas desarrollaban aquí esquemas y perfeccionaban inventos de relojería. En la actualidad, las fugas de radiación han vuelto locos a los investigadores supervivientes, transformándolos en desquiciados gnomos parias que custodian mecánicamente maquinaria averiada junto a ensamblajes descontrolados.

ang.profession:Engineering: The Engineering Labs represent the pinnacle of fallen gnomish automation, retaining functional automated punchograph terminals and discarded schematics amid the wreckage.
ang.race:Gnome: For exiled gnomes, these laboratories are a tragic sight: once the beating heart of their race's technological triumphs, now reduced to an irradiated ruin overrun by their corrupted kin.

faq.a: Before the city fell, the Engineering Labs were dedicated to research, assembly, and testing of complex gnome contraptions and automated devices. Gnomish engineers and technicians used the vast two-level chamber to blueprint new technology.
faq.q: What were the Engineering Labs originally used for?

faq.a: Irradiated leper gnomes and haywire mechanical automatons roam both tiers of the chamber. These lingering residents were driven completely mad by the irradiated gas released during the city's fall and attack any non-irradiated intruders on sight.
faq.q: What threats roam the Engineering Labs now?

faq.a: These automated gnomish data terminals are found on the lower level of the Engineering Labs. They allow engineers and adventurers to punch encoded data cards, advancing their security clearance and deciphering technical archives preserved within the city.
faq.q: What are the Matrix Punchograph 3005-D machines?

faq.a: The upper level connects directly to the Workshop Entrance back door and passages leading to the Launch Bay. The lower level leads to the main corridors connecting the Launch Bay and Tinkers' Court.
faq.q: How does this area connect to the rest of Gnomeregan?

text.s: The Engineering Labs are a multi-tiered research and manufacturing facility deep within Gnomeregan. Connected to the Workshop Entrance and Launch Bay, this bustling center of gnome innovation was overrun during the city's radioactive cataclysm and is now swarming with crazed leper gnomes and rogue mechanical contraptions.

sec.b: Built around a central mechanical structure, the Engineering Labs span two primary tiers connected by a central cargo lift. In Gnomeregan's prime, tinkerers here developed schematics and fine-tuned clockwork inventions. Today, radiation leaks have driven the remaining researchers mad, transforming them into deranged leper gnomes who mindlessly guard malfunctioning machinery alongside rogue constructs.

Beyond its historical role as a laboratory, the chamber serves as a vital transit hub through the lower reaches of the ruined city. Passages wind toward the Launch Bay, Tinkers' Court, and the Workshop Entrance back door. The lower floor also houses the Matrix Punchograph 3005-D terminals, critical processing units required to decipher the coded punch cards carried by gnome engineers.

subzone:falfarren-river.s: Río Falfarren. El Río Falfarren fluye de noreste a suroeste por el corazón de Vallefresno; nace en las laderas del Monte Hyjal antes de deslizarse bajo tierra bajo las montañas del norte de Los Baldíos. Forma una frontera natural entre los dominios de los elfos de la noche alrededor de Astranaar, al oeste, y las avanzadas invasoras de la Horda, al este. Los viajeros deben andar con cautela, pues sus orillas sombrías y sus aguas poco profundas albergan fauna hostil y marcan el límite del conflicto abierto. Descendiendo desde el Monte Hyjal, las aguas del Falfarren caen en cascadas hacia Xavian antes de serpentear entre el Puesto del Hachazo y la Senda de la Noche. Aunque no es excepcionalmente profundo ni intransitable en condiciones climáticas normales, sirve como la línea divisoria geopolítica aproximada en el centro de Vallefresno. Al oeste se encuentran Astranaar y las posesiones principales de los Kaldorei; al este se asientan los campamentos y las operaciones madereras de la Horda. Cruzar los puentes de madera del camino principal lleva a los viajeros al disputado corazón del bosque, donde las patrullas se enfrentan a lo largo de las orillas.

ang.faction:Alliance: For the Night Elves and their allies, crossing eastward over the Falfarren signifies stepping directly into the Horde's front lines near Splintertree Post.
ang.faction:Horde: The Falfarren marks the western edge of the Horde's expansion out of Splintertree Post, beyond which lies fortified night elf territory.

faq.a: The Falfarren River starts in the heights of Mount Hyjal, cascading down waterfalls into the lake at Xavian. From there, it meanders southwest across Ashenvale before plunging underground into subterranean channels beneath the northern mountains of the Barrens.
faq.q: Where does the Falfarren River begin and end?

faq.a: It serves as the rough borderline between night elf and Horde control in central Ashenvale. Night elf territory, centered around Astranaar, lies to the west, while the orc outpost of Splintertree Post and active Horde lumbering operations lie to the east.
faq.q: Why is the Falfarren River significant to the war in Ashenvale?

faq.a: Aggressive bog beasts roam the shallows, particularly near the corrupted regions around Felfire Hill. In addition, patrols from both the Alliance and the Horde watch the bridges and crossings, making unattended river banks prime territory for skirmishes and ambushes.
faq.q: What threats should travelers expect along the riverbanks?

text.s: The Falfarren River flows northeast to southwest through the heart of Ashenvale, originating on the slopes of Mount Hyjal before slipping underground beneath the Barrens' northern mountains. It forms a natural boundary between night elven domains around Astranaar to the west and the encroaching Horde outposts to the east. Travelers must tread carefully, as its shaded banks and shallows harbor hostile wildlife and mark the edge of open conflict.

sec.b: Feeding down from Mount Hyjal, the waters of the Falfarren cascade across waterfalls into Xavian before winding between Splintertree Post and Night Run. While it is neither exceptionally deep nor impassable under ordinary weather, it serves as the rough geopolitical dividing line in central Ashenvale. To the west lie Astranaar and the core holdings of the Kaldorei; to the east sit the camps and lumber operations of the Horde. Crossing the main road's wooden bridges brings travelers into the contested heart of the forest, where patrols clash along the banks.

Beyond the tensions of warring sentinels and grunts, the river conceals natural and unnatural dangers beneath its surface. Downstream near Felfire Hill, corrupted bog beasts and aggressive water creatures prowl the muddy shallows. Rainfall can swell the currents, yet the true peril lies in the dense canopies flanking either shore, where ambushes and skirmishes routinely spill into the stream.

subzone:fallen-sky-lake.s: Lago Cielo Estrellado. El Lago Cielo Estrellado es una masa de agua aislada enclavada en las profundidades de los bosques del este de Vallefresno. Situadas entre la Avanzada Ala de Plata y el invasor Campo de trabajos forzados Grito de Guerra, sus serenas aguas ocultan peligro en forma de sombramatorral woodkin hostiles que defienden agresivamente el lago y su isla central. Escondido al sur de la Avanzada Ala de Plata y justo al oeste del Campo de trabajos forzados Grito de Guerra, el Lago Cielo Estrellado ofrece un fugaz vistazo al esplendor natural de Vallefresno antes de que las hachas orcas echaran raíces en las cercanías. Las orillas y el pequeño islote que se alza en medio del lago están habitados por shadethickets: lechúcicos corruptos o territoriales que consideran una amenaza a cualquier intruso bípedo. El corazón de la isla sirve como dominio de un poderoso Oráculo Sombramatorral, cuya presencia mantiene a los woodkin locales vinculados a la arboleda e implacablemente vigilantes contra los viajeros que pasan por allí.

ang.class:Druid: Wildkin are traditionally sacred creatures touched by Elune's grace, making the corrupted, aggressive shadethickets infesting Fallen Sky Lake an unsettling sight to behold.
ang.race:NightElf: Positioned just south of Silverwing Outpost, the lake represents yet another corner of the sacred ancestral forest where wild beasts have grown erratic amidst the gathering drums of the Horde.

faq.a: Fallen Sky Lake is located in eastern Ashenvale, directly south of Silverwing Outpost, west of the Warsong Labor Camp, and northeast of Silverwing Grove.
al: how to find fallen sky lake
faq.q: Where is Fallen Sky Lake located?

faq.a: The lake and its surrounding banks are overrun by shadethickets—aggressive wildkin creatures—led by a formidable Shadethicket Oracle who dwells on the central island.
al: what is at fallen sky lake
faq.q: What creatures live around Fallen Sky Lake?

faq.a: The Shadethicket Oracle is the matriarchal leader of the local woodkin gathered at the lake. Travelers and scouts in Ashenvale are often tasked with hunting down the oracle on her central isle to cull the hostile wildkin threat.
faq.q: Why is the Shadethicket Oracle important?

text.s: Fallen Sky Lake is a secluded body of water nestled deep within the forests of eastern Ashenvale. Situated between Silverwing Outpost and the encroaching Warsong Labor Camp, the serene waters hide danger in the form of hostile shadethicket woodkin that aggressively defend the lake and its central isle.

sec.b: Tucked south of Silverwing Outpost and just west of the Warsong Labor Camp, Fallen Sky Lake offers a fleeting glimpse of Ashenvale's natural splendor before the Orcish axes took root nearby. The shores and the small islet rising from the middle of the lake are inhabited by shadethickets—corrupted or territorial wildkin that view any two-legged intruder as a threat. The heart of the island serves as the domain of a powerful Shadethicket Oracle, whose presence keeps the local woodkin bound to the grove and relentlessly vigilant against travelers passing through.

subzone:faol-s-rest.s: Tumba de Faol. La Tumba de Faol es un sepulcro tranquilo y descuidado situado en el este de los Claros de Tirisfal, justo al suroeste del Monasterio Escarlata. Se erigió como la tumba del arzobispo Alonsus Faol, el venerado patriarca espiritual que fundó los Caballeros de la Mano de Plata. Hoy en día, descuidada bajo la bóveda arbórea asolada por la plaga, sirve como cementerio de reaparición para quienes perecen cerca del monasterio. Antes de que la Tercera Guerra devastara Lordaeron, esta vaguada apartada era un lugar de solemne peregrinaje. Alberga la tumba de piedra del arzobispo Alonsus Faol, quien guio a la Iglesia de la Luz Sagrada a través de los oscuros días de la Segunda Guerra e instituyó la orden de paladines para proteger a la humanidad. Faol falleció en paz antes de la llegada de la Plaga, librándose de la agonía mortal de ver caer su reino. En aquellos años más luminosos, los dolientes recorrían regularmente el camino desde la capital de Lordaeron para dejar ofrendas y rendir homenaje al querido patriarca.

ang.class:Paladin: Every paladin owes their calling to Archbishop Faol, who first gathered Uther and his peers to unite the martial arts with the Holy Light. Standing before his untended tomb is a sobering reminder of the order's beginnings.
ang.class:Priest: As the supreme leader of the Church of the Holy Light through the Second War, Faol was the shepherd of all priesthoods in Lordaeron; seeing his monument ruined reflects the church's tragic ruin in the north.

faq.a: Alonsus Faol was the Archbishop of the Church of the Holy Light during the Second War. Revered for his wisdom and compassion, he organized relief for refugees and founded the Knights of the Silver Hand, transforming holy priests and pious knights into humanity's first paladins, including Uther the Lightbringer and Turalyon.
faq.q: Who was Alonsus Faol?

faq.a: The grounds near the Scarlet Monastery were historically significant religious holdings of the Church of the Holy Light in northern Lordaeron. Faol was laid to rest in this tranquil corner of Tirisfal Glades before the kingdom fell, long before the scarlet-clad zealots fortified the nearby monastery.
faq.q: Why is this monument located near the Scarlet Monastery?

faq.a: No. Since the fall of Lordaeron to the Scourge, the site has been utterly neglected. The Scarlet Crusade rarely descends into the hollow to tend it, and the Forsaken have little interest in honoring the shrines of the old church, leaving the stone markers weathered and overgrown.
faq.q: Is anyone maintaining the tomb today?

faq.a: Faol's Rest functions as the local spirit graveyard for the surrounding wilderness and the Scarlet Monastery. Adventurers who perish attempting to breach the monastery or traversing eastern Tirisfal find their spirits returning to the Archbishop's quiet monument.
al: what is this place in game
faq.q: What practical purpose does Faol's Rest serve for travelers?

text.s: Faol's Rest is a quiet, neglected gravesite situated in eastern Tirisfal Glades, just southwest of the Scarlet Monastery. It was erected as the tomb of Archbishop Alonsus Faol, the revered spiritual patriarch who founded the Knights of the Silver Hand. Today, untended beneath the blighted canopy, it serves as a release graveyard for those who perish near the monastery.

sec.b: Before the Third War devastated Lordaeron, this secluded hollow was a place of solemn pilgrimage. It holds the stone tomb of Archbishop Alonsus Faol, who led the Church of the Holy Light through the dark days of the Second War and instituted the order of paladins to protect humanity. Faol passed away peacefully prior to the arrival of the Scourge, spared the mortal agony of seeing his kingdom fall. In those brighter years, mourners regularly journeyed up the road from Capital City to leave offerings and pay respects to the beloved patriarch.

When the Plague of Undeath swept across Lordaeron, Tirisfal withered, and the pilgrims vanished. Today, the monument sits abandoned and cracked in the shadows beneath the Scarlet Monastery's high bluffs. The wild brush has reclaimed the pathways, and the tomb itself lies still amid the damp mist. For adventurers striving against the zealots of the Scarlet Crusade or the lingering terrors of Tirisfal, this forgotten resting place now serves primarily as a quiet threshold where fallen spirits briefly regroup before returning to the fray.
sec.t: Desolation in the Shadow of the Monastery

subzone:far-watch-post.s: Avanzada del Puente. La Avanzada del Puente es un puesto avanzado fortificado de la Horda situado justo al oeste del puente sobre el Río Furia del Sur que conecta Durotar con Los Baldíos. Al servir como primera línea de defensa del territorio orco, el puesto protege caravanas comerciales vitales contra agresivas manadas de jabaespines y las hostiles incursiones de la Alianza. Situada al pie occidental del puente que sale de Durotar, la Avanzada del Puente es el primer bastión de la autoridad de la Horda que ven los viajeros al entrar en la vasta y árida sabana de Los Baldíos. El asentamiento es espartano pero funcional, construido para la preparación táctica más que para el confort. Cuenta con una robusta torre de vigilancia orca, un cubil y catapultas de asedio ya calibradas y orientadas hacia las polvorientas llanuras. Justo al sur del camino principal, los peones cuidan un corral de lobos de monta listos para transportar mensajeros o refuerzos. La Avanzada del Puente existe principalmente para mantener segura la ruta de suministros hacia El Cruce, inspeccionando el tráfico entrante y repeliendo los asaltos de las tribus errantes de jabaespines y de los sigilosos exploradores de la Alianza.

ang.faction:Alliance: Positioned squarely across the bridge from Durotar, Far Watch Post stands as a formidable roadblock that prevents scouting parties and saboteurs from easily approaching the orcish capital.
ang.faction:Horde: For young warriors stepping out of Durotar for the first time, Far Watch Post is the final outpost of familiar ground before venturing into the rugged, dangerous heartland of Kalimdor.

faq.a: The post acts as the primary border station between Durotar and the Barrens. Its defenders protect vital Horde supply caravans and ensure that local dangers, notably aggressive quilboar tribes and Alliance trespassers, do not cross the Southfury River into Durotar.
al: why is far watch post here
faq.q: What is the purpose of Far Watch Post?

faq.a: Far Watch Post is an active military encampment manned by the Horde. Orc grunts garrison the tower and maintain the siege engines, supported by peons overseeing riding wolves.
faq.q: Who controls this outpost?

faq.a: The post faces frequent harassment from nearby quilboar packs that contest the surrounding thorn-covered scrubland. It also stands on guard against Alliance incursions that might attempt to strike across the Barrens toward Orgrimmar.
faq.q: What threats does the outpost face?

text.s: Far Watch Post is a fortified Horde outpost situated just west of the Southfury River bridge connecting Durotar to the Barrens. Serving as the front line of defense for the orcish homeland, the post guards vital trade caravans against aggressive quilboar packs and hostile Alliance incursions.

sec.b: Located at the western foot of the bridge out of Durotar, Far Watch Post is the first bastion of Horde authority travellers see when entering the vast, arid savannah of the Barrens. The settlement is Spartan but functional, built for tactical readiness rather than comfort. It features a sturdy orcish watchtower, a burrow, and pre-sighted siege catapults trained toward the dusty plains. Directly south of the main road, peons tend a pen of riding wolves ready to bear messengers or reinforcements. Far Watch Post exists primarily to keep the supply road to Crossroads secure, screening incoming traffic and repelling raids from roaming quilboar tribes and stealthy Alliance scouts.

subzone:fargodeep-mine.s: Mina Abisal. Mina Abisal es una mina de oro abandonada situada en el centro del Bosque de Elwynn, al sur de Villadorada. Antaño una productiva fuente de riqueza para el Reino de Ventormenta, hace poco ha sido invadida por un clan beligerante de kóbolds. Mina Abisal proporcionaba antes un flujo constante de oro al tesoro de Ventormenta, pero la menguante presencia militar del reino en Elwynn ha dejado vulnerables los recursos periféricos. Los kóbolds no tardaron en abarrotar los oscuros túneles, estableciendo una bulliciosa madriguera bajo las colinas. El Alguacil Dughan y las autoridades locales de Villadorada ven la infestación con profunda preocupación, no solo por el mineral perdido, sino porque estas envalentonadas criaturas amenazan ahora granjas cercanas como las tierras de los Stonefield y los Maclure.

ang.faction:Alliance: Clearing the vermin out of Fargodeep Mine is vital for securing the supply lines and farmlands immediately surrounding Goldshire.
ang.profession:Mining: Though infested with pests, the rocky tunnels of Fargodeep remain rich in accessible copper veins for fledgling miners.

faq.a: The mine was neglected as Stormwind's military stretched thin across southern lands. With town guards focused on protecting Goldshire and the main roads, the subterranean dig site was left unguarded, allowing kobolds to move in and fortify the tunnels.
faq.q: Why did Stormwind abandon Fargodeep Mine?

faq.a: Fargodeep Mine lies right between the Stonefield and Maclure family farms. The kobolds venture out from the tunnels to steal livestock, tools, and personal belongings, harassing anyone who wanders near the mine's entrance.
faq.q: Why are the kobolds here so dangerous to local farmers?

faq.a: Goldtooth is a prominent kobold who nests deep within the lower shafts of Fargodeep Mine. He is notorious for snatching Auntie Bernice Stonefield's prized family necklace.
faq.q: Who is Goldtooth?

faq.a: Local merchants and townsfolk see opportunity in clearing the pests: Remy 'Two Times' buys up salvaged gold dust, the alchemist William Pestle uses kobold candle wax for reagents, and Marshal Dughan needs the infestation monitored to safeguard Elwynn.
faq.q: Why do people in Goldshire want items from the mine?

text.s: Fargodeep Mine is an abandoned gold mine nestled in central Elwynn Forest, south of Goldshire. Once a productive source of wealth for the Kingdom of Stormwind, it has recently been overrun by a belligerent clan of kobolds.

sec.b: Fargodeep Mine once provided steady gold to Stormwind's treasury, but the Kingdom's dwindling military presence in Elwynn has left outlying resources vulnerable. Kobolds quickly swarmed into the dark tunnels, establishing a bustling warren beneath the hills. Marshal Dughan and the local authorities in Goldshire view the infestation with deep concern, not only because of lost ore, but because the emboldened creatures now threaten nearby farmsteads like the Stonefield and Maclure holdings.

The mine spans multiple levels, with the lower shafts winding deep beneath the forest floor. Kobold laborers and vermin scurry along the wooden scaffolds, fiercely guarding their scavenged wax and gold dust. Deeper within lurks Goldtooth, a particularly cunning kobold leader known for hoarding trinkets pilfered from unwary travelers and surrounding residents.

subzone:fel-rock.s: Roca Mácula. Roca Mácula es una caverna asolada oculta en los bosques justo al norte de Dolanaar, sobre las ramas de Teldrassil. En el pasado fue una hondonada tranquila, pero ha caído en la corrupción bajo la influencia del sátiro Lord Melenas y su horda de viles grells. Escondida en las colinas boscosas al norte de Dolanaar, Roca Mácula fue antaño una caverna ordinaria y apacible excavada en la madera y la piedra de Teldrassil. Hoy en día, se alza como un inquietante recordatorio de la corrupción invasora que amenaza al Árbol del Mundo. Raíces retorcidas y sombras antinaturales dominan el interior de la caverna, infestada por enjambres de grells salvajes y parientes de grell.

ang.class:Druid: Druids of the Cenarion Circle view Fel Rock as a festering wound on the young world tree, requiring immediate purging before demonic corruption spreads.
ang.race:NightElf: For the Kaldorei, the presence of a satyr like Lord Melenas so close to Dolanaar is an alarming affront to Teldrassil that demands swift retribution.

faq.a: Fel Rock is located in central Teldrassil, tucked into the hills directly north of the settlement of Dolanaar.
faq.q: Where is Fel Rock located?

faq.a: The cavern is commanded by Lord Melenas, a vile satyr who has made Fel Rock his lair and gathered a host of grells to do his bidding.
faq.q: Who rules Fel Rock?

faq.a: The presence of a satyr and fel-tainted grells within the world tree's boughs poses an immediate threat to the natural balance of Teldrassil. Druids like Tallonkai Swiftroot dispatch adventurers to cut down Lord Melenas and stem the corruption.
faq.q: Why are druids concerned about Fel Rock?

faq.a: Inside Fel Rock, you will encounter aggressive grells, grellkin, and their dark master, the satyr Lord Melenas.
faq.q: What creatures dwell inside the cavern?

text.s: Fel Rock is a blighted cavern hidden within the woods just north of Dolanaar on the boughs of Teldrassil. Once a tranquil hollow, it has fallen into corruption under the influence of the satyr Lord Melenas and his horde of vicious grells.

sec.b: Tucked away in the forested hills north of Dolanaar, Fel Rock was once an ordinary, peaceful cavern carved into the wood and stone of Teldrassil. Today, it stands as an unsettling reminder of the creeping taint encroaching on the world tree. Twisted roots and unnatural shadows dominate the cavern interior, overrun by swarms of wild grells and grellkin.

The corruption within Fel Rock stems from the presence of Lord Melenas, a wicked satyr who has claimed the hollow as a stronghold. From deep within the cave, he orchestrates the spread of malevolent corruption right under the watchful gaze of the night elf sentinels. Druids from Dolanaar, particularly Tallonkai Swiftroot, actively enlist capable defenders to cleanse the cave and slay Melenas before his foul blight can spread further into the surrounding woodlands.

subzone:felfire-hill.s: Cerro Lumbrevil. Cerro Lumbrevil es una colina marchita e infestada de demonios ubicada en el este de Vallefresno. Azotada por la caída de infernales durante la Tercera Guerra, su tierra corrupta aún arde con poder demoníaco. La Horda mantiene puestos de guardia fortificados en los puentes que conducen a la colina para proteger sus asentamientos cercanos. Durante la invasión cataclísmica de la Tercera Guerra, cayeron meteoros llameantes por todo Kalimdor mientras la Legión Ardiente desataba a sus temibles infernales. Varios de esos colosos ardientes se estrellaron contra esta cresta en Vallefresno, arrasando los bosques ancestrales y corrompiendo la propia tierra. Hoy en día, el paisaje abrasado sigue saturado de energía vil y acechado por demonios rezagados que sobrevivieron a la derrota de la Legión en el Monte Hyjal.

ang.class:Warlock: The raw fel energies lingering where the Legion's infernals made landfall make this scarred ridge an object of dangerous curiosity for practitioners of dark magic.
ang.faction:Horde: The Horde holds the fortified bridges around Felfire Hill to safeguard the transit road connecting Splintertree Post with the Warsong Lumber Camp against demonic raids.

faq.a: During the Third War, Burning Legion infernals rained down from the sky and slammed into this hill. The impact and subsequent fel contamination burned away the pristine elven forest, leaving behind scarred rock and corrupting demonic energies that never dispersed.
faq.q: Why is Felfire Hill corrupted?

faq.a: The hill is occupied by surviving demons and infernal constructs left over from the Legion's invasion during the Third War. They remain hostile to all mortals who wander near their corrupted perimeter.
faq.q: What creatures live on Felfire Hill?

faq.a: Felfire Hill lies directly between Splintertree Post and the Warsong Lumber Camp. Horde commanders fortified both bridges to ensure the roaming demons cannot break out and overrun their nearby camps, supply convoys, and lumber operations.
al: why are orcs guarding felfire hill
faq.q: Why did the Horde fortify the bridges here?

faq.a: Though the hill itself was once part of Ashenvale's sacred forest, it now sits menacingly northeast of the Dor'Danil Barrow Den. The creeping demonic taint and roaming fiends pose an enduring danger to the nearby slumbering grounds and the surrounding wildlands.
faq.q: Is Felfire Hill connected to the night elves?

text.s: Felfire Hill is a blighted, demon-infested rise nestled in eastern Ashenvale. Struck by falling infernals during the Third War, its corrupted soil still burns with demonic power. The Horde maintains fortified guard posts on the bridges leading into the hill to safeguard their nearby settlements.

sec.b: During the cataclysmic invasion of the Third War, flaming meteors fell across Kalimdor as the Burning Legion unleashed its dread infernals. Several of those fiery behemoths struck this ridge in Ashenvale, scouring away the ancient woodlands and corrupting the earth itself. Today, the scorched landscape remains saturated with fel energy and prowled by lingering demons who survived the Legion's defeat at Mount Hyjal.
sec.t: A Scar of the Burning Legion

sec.b: Situated southeast of Splintertree Post and southwest of the Warsong Lumber Camp, Felfire Hill sits uncomfortably close to vital Horde operations. Because the demonic remnants threaten to spill out into the surrounding forest, Horde forces have erected fortified barricades and guard towers at both bridges approaching the hill, containing the foul creatures within their blighted haven.

subzone:fenris-keep.s: Castillo de Fenris. El Castillo de Fenris es una fortaleza de piedra aislada situada en lo alto de la Isla de Fenris, en el corazón del Lago Lordamere. Antaño un bastión estratégico que albergaba tropas de Lordaeron, ha caído en manos de la Plaga bajo el mando del mago renegado Thule Corvozarpa. Antes de la Tercera Guerra, el Castillo de Fenris tenía una gran importancia estratégica para el Reino de Lordaeron, albergando un contingente considerable de tropas para proteger el Lago Lordamere. Cuando la Plaga de los no-muertos asoló la región, la fortaleza insular fue arrasada junto con el resto del reino. En lugar de desmoronarse en una ruina olvidada, fue tomada por Thule Corvozarpa, un antiguo mago traidor del Kirin Tor. Corvozarpa se alió con la Plaga, subyugó a los gnolls locales con vil nigromancia para crear la voraz jauría de los Podrepiel y se atrincheró en lo más profundo de las salas de piedra del castillo.

ang.class:Mage: The master of Fenris Keep, Thule Ravenclaw, represents a grim betrayal of the Kirin Tor's teachings, having twisted Dalaran's arcane knowledge into the dark arts of the Scourge.
ang.faction:Horde: For the Horde—and the Forsaken in particular—Fenris Keep represents a lingering Scourge stronghold that must be eradicated to safeguard Silverpine Forest and the waterways of Lordamere Lake.

faq.a: Fenris Keep is a fortified stone castle situated on Fenris Isle in Lordamere Lake. Formerly a military stronghold for the fallen kingdom of Lordaeron, it is currently held by the undead Scourge.
faq.q: What is Fenris Keep?

faq.a: The keep is ruled by Thule Ravenclaw, a former Kirin Tor mage who betrayed the living to serve the Scourge. He commands an army of undead-tainted Rot Hide gnolls from within the fortress.
faq.q: Who rules Fenris Keep right now?

faq.a: The local gnoll population was subjugated by Thule Ravenclaw through dark magic and disease, twisting them into the Rot Hide gnolls. They serve as Ravenclaw's loyal shock troops and guards throughout the castle and the surrounding island.
faq.q: Why are there gnolls inside Fenris Keep?

faq.a: Fenris Keep provides the Scourge with a defensible base on Lordamere Lake, directly menacing Forsaken movements through eastern Silverpine Forest and Tirisfal Glades. Sylvanas's forces cannot leave an active Scourge commander unchecked so close to their borders.
faq.q: Why do the Forsaken care about Fenris Keep?

text.s: Fenris Keep is an isolated stone fortress situated atop Fenris Isle in the heart of Lordamere Lake. Once a strategic stronghold housing Lordaeron troops, it has fallen into the hands of the Scourge under the rogue mage Thule Ravenclaw.

sec.b: Before the Third War, Fenris Keep held strategic importance for the Kingdom of Lordaeron, stationing a sizable contingent of troops to safeguard Lordamere Lake. When the undead Scourge swept across the land, the island fortress was overwhelmed along with the rest of the realm. Rather than crumbling into forgotten ruin, it was seized by Thule Ravenclaw, a traitorous former wizard of the Kirin Tor. Ravenclaw allied himself with the Scourge, subjugated the resident gnolls with foul necromancy to create the ravenous Rot Hide pack, and entrenched himself deep inside the keep's stone halls.

Today, Fenris Keep serves as the seat of Ravenclaw's power and an imminent threat to the Forsaken securing Silverpine Forest. From this bastion, Thule directs legions of Rot Hide gnolls that violently assail anyone daring to set foot on the isle. Because Fenris Isle sits mere miles across the water from the Tirisfal border, the Forsaken of the Sepulcher and Undercity actively dispatch champions to batter down the keep's defenses and put an end to the rogue necromancer.

subzone:field-of-giants.s: Tierra de Gigantes. La Tierra de Gigantes es una extensa llanura que cubre el sur de Los Baldíos entre el Campamento Taurajo y las ciénagas del Marjal Revolcafango. Bautizada así por los imponentes kodos, lagartos del trueno y enormes bestias que pastan en sus áridos matorrales, la región se ha vuelto recientemente mucho más peligrosa debido a una creciente plaga de silítidos. Extendiéndose a lo largo del tramo sur del Camino del Oro, la Tierra de Gigantes es remota, escarpada y apenas está defendida en comparación con Los Baldíos del norte. Aunque las atalayas de madera del camino se encuentran prácticamente abandonadas, la propia tierra rebosa vida. Enormes manadas de la megafauna de Kalimdor deambulan por las vastas llanuras, atrayendo tanto a cazadores como a naturalistas. Sin embargo, la seguridad es esquiva aquí: los excavadores enanos de Bael Modan cavan agresivamente hacia el sur, y una amenaza mucho más siniestra ha comenzado a excavar bajo la tierra.

ang.class:Hunter: The roaming herds of thunder lizards and massive kodo make the Field of Giants one of the premier hunting grounds in the Barrens for those seeking formidable beasts.
ang.faction:Horde: The emergence of silithid hives so close to the road between Camp Taurajo and Dustwallow Marsh threatens travel lines, prompting leaders across the Barrens to call for scouts.

faq.a: The plain earns its name from the sheer scale of the wildlife roaming it. Great herds of towering kodo beasts and thunder lizards graze here, dominating the landscape alongside massive Kalimdorean wildlife.
faq.q: Why is it called the Field of Giants?

faq.a: Those are silithid mounds. These insectoid predators have tunneled up from deep underground, creating the northernmost hives discovered in Kalimdor. Their sudden presence poses a dire threat to passing travelers and local wildlife.
faq.q: What are those bug mounds in the ground?

faq.a: The plain itself has few settlements, but prominent figures watch its borders. The tauren shaman Brine lives on a southern ridge, while the displaced exile Gann Stonespire watches from nearby, plotting against the dwarven excavation at Bael Modan.
faq.q: Who lives near the Field of Giants?

faq.a: The Horde's military presence is concentrated heavily along the northern Gold Road around the Crossroads. The southernmost reaches receive far fewer patrols, leaving these towers neglected amidst the creeping threats of silithid and aggressive wildlife.
faq.q: Why are the watchtowers along the road abandoned?

text.s: The Field of Giants is an expansive plain covering the southern Barrens between Camp Taurajo and the marshes of Dustwallow. Named for the towering kodo, thunder lizards, and massive beasts that graze its arid scrub, the region has recently grown far more perilous due to an encroaching silithid infestation.

sec.b: Stretching along the southern span of the Gold Road, the Field of Giants is remote, rugged, and lightly defended compared to the Barrens to the north. While the road's wooden watchtowers stand largely abandoned, the land itself thrums with life. Tremendous herds of Kalimdor's megafauna wander the vast flats, drawing hunters and naturalists alike. However, safety is elusive here: dwarven excavators from Bael Modan dig aggressively to the south, and a far more sinister menace has begun burrowing beneath the earth.
sec.t: A Wild Frontier in the South

sec.b: In recent times, insectoid silithid hives have erupted from the ground across the Field of Giants, marking the northernmost known sighting of these ravenous creatures in Kalimdor. These strange mounds and aggressive swarms have alarmed the Horde. Scouts such as the troll Korran from the Crossroads and tauren warriors like Ruga Ragetotem at Camp Taurajo urge adventurers to probe the hives, seeking to uncover what draws these subterranean horrors so far from the deep deserts.

subzone:fire-scar-shrine.s: Santuario de la Escara. El Santuario de la Escara es un santuario de los elfos de la noche profanado, enclavado en los bosques del suroeste de Vallefresno. Antaño un sereno lugar de culto, ha sido corrompido por fuerzas demoníacas y transformado en una ampolla de energía vil a las mismas puertas de Astranaar. Situado al suroeste de Astranaar y al oeste de Las ruinas del Polvo Estelar, el Santuario de la Escara se erige como un lúgubre recordatorio del veneno persistente de la Legión Ardiente en Vallefresno. El santuario ha sucumbido a la corrupción demoníaca, alimentada por los siervos del sombrío Culto de la Facción Oscura y el Consejo de la Sombra. La magia vil ha retorcido la tierra circundante convirtiéndola en roca calcinada, donde demonios errantes se reúnen ahora en abierto desafío a los defensores del bosque.

ang.class:Warlock: The fel scarring and wild demonic summons here bear the clear signature of the Shadow Council's subtle infiltrations throughout Kalimdor.
ang.race:NightElf: The desecration of Fire Scar Shrine is a bitter affront so near to Astranaar, demanding swift retribution against any demonic trespassers who sully the forest.

faq.a: Fire Scar Shrine is situated in southwestern Ashenvale, directly southwest of the night elf hub of Astranaar, south of the Shrine of Aessina, and just west of the Ruins of Stardust.
faq.q: Where is Fire Scar Shrine located?

faq.a: The shrine was infiltrated and corrupted by agents of the Shadow Council and the Cult of the Dark Strand, notably the orc warlock Ilkrud Magthrull. Their dark rituals summoned demons and infused the sacred ground with lingering fel taint.
faq.q: Why are there demons at Fire Scar Shrine?

faq.a: Akkrilus is a formidable doomguard that occasionally manifests around Fire Scar Shrine, drawn to the potent demonic energies that pool around the corrupted stones.
faq.q: Who is Akkrilus?

faq.a: The orc warlock who operated here, Ilkrud Magthrull, served Athrikus Narassin, the leader of the Cult of the Dark Strand. They leveraged the shrine as a foothold for their demonic summoning and dark ambitions within Ashenvale.
al: cult of the dark strand fire scar
faq.q: What connection does this place have to the Cult of the Dark Strand?

text.s: Fire Scar Shrine is a despoiled night elf shrine nestled in the southwestern forests of Ashenvale. Once a serene place of worship, it has been corrupted by demonic forces and turned into a blister of fel energy right on Astranaar's doorstep.

sec.b: Located southwest of Astranaar and west of the Ruins of Stardust, Fire Scar Shrine stands as a grim reminder of the Burning Legion's lingering poison in Ashenvale. The shrine has fallen under the sway of demonic corruption, nurtured by servants of the shadowy Cult of the Dark Strand and the Shadow Council. Fel magic has twisted the surrounding earth into scorched rock, where roaming demons now gather in open defiance of the forest's defenders.

The shrine's descent into darkness was spearheaded by agents like the orcish warlock Ilkrud Magthrull, operating under the orders of Athrikus Narassin. Though mortal sorcerers brought the corruption to bear, summoned fiends now patrol the altar stones unchecked. The localized tear in the veil occasionally draws greater horrors, including the towering doomguard Akkrilus.

subzone:forest-s-edge.s: Linde del bosque. Linde del bosque es una cuña boscosa de tierra a lo largo de la frontera suroeste de Bosque de Elwynn, flanqueada por ríos que conducen hacia Páramos de Poniente. Custodiada al norte por Cuartel Arroyoeste, esta zona salvaje ha sido peligrosamente invadida por gnolls zarparrío bajo el mando del infame Hogger. Ubicada al suroeste de Ciudad de Ventormenta, entre Vergel del Lago Espejo y los ríos que bordean Páramos de Poniente, Linde del bosque forma una península natural de bosque. A pesar de su proximidad a Cuartel Arroyoeste, las mermadas filas del ejército de Ventormenta han dejado la zona vulnerable a bestias salvajes y partidas de saqueadores. Jabalíes errantes merodean entre los árboles y a lo largo de las orillas del río, pero la verdadera amenaza es la concentración de gnolls zarparrío que han convertido estos bosques en su base de operaciones.

ang.faction:Alliance: For recruits stationed in Elwynn Forest, clearing Forest's Edge and defeating Hogger is one of the first major trials proving their combat readiness to the crown.
ang.profession:Herbalism: The quiet riverbanks and shaded groves of Forest's Edge yield common woodland herbs, though gathering them often requires dodging aggressive gnoll patrols.

faq.a: Forest's Edge is located in the southwestern corner of Elwynn Forest. It sits south of Westbrook Garrison, bordered by Mirror Lake Orchard and the waterways that lead into Westfall.
faq.q: Where exactly is Forest's Edge?

faq.a: A large and aggressive pack of Riverpaw gnolls has claimed the woods, threatening travel along the southwestern border. The biggest threat is their chieftain, Hogger, an exceptionally vicious gnoll who prowls these woods.
faq.q: Why is this area so dangerous?

faq.a: Hogger is a notorious, powerful gnoll leader responsible for violent attacks on Elwynn's borders. The Stormwind Army has posted a generous bounty for proof of his death, warning adventurers not to face him alone.
faq.q: Who is Hogger?

faq.a: Stormwind's military is stretched remarkably thin across the kingdom. With unrest in Westfall and threats encroaching on all sides, the garrison lacks the manpower to clear the gnoll camps, leaving the task to volunteer adventurers.
faq.q: Why hasn't Westbrook Garrison cleared the area?

text.s: Forest's Edge is a wooded wedge of land along the southwestern frontier of Elwynn Forest, flanked by rivers leading toward Westfall. Guarded to the north by Westbrook Garrison, this untamed area has become dangerously overrun by riverpaw gnolls under the command of the notorious Hogger.

sec.b: Tucked southwest of Stormwind City between Mirror Lake Orchard and the rivers bordering Westfall, Forest's Edge forms a natural peninsula of woodland. Despite its proximity to Westbrook Garrison, the Stormwind army's thin ranks have left the area vulnerable to wild beasts and raiding parties. Wandering boars roam among the trees and along the riverbanks, but the true menace is the concentration of Riverpaw gnolls who have made these woods their staging ground.

The woods of Forest's Edge are the hunting grounds of Hogger, a massive and brutal gnoll chieftain. With a sizable bounty placed on his head by the Stormwind Army, Hogger directs his pack in harassing travelers and raiding nearby farms, turning what could be a peaceful timberland into a lethal proving ground for young Alliance adventurers.

subzone:forest-song.s: Canción del Bosque. Canción del Bosque es una antigua ruina de los elfos de la noche ubicada en el noreste de Vallefresno, cerca de los bosques corruptos de Satyrnaar y del gran portal de Talloumbrío. En la actualidad, se encuentra prácticamente desierta, a excepción del vigilante druida Kayneth Ventoleve, quien custodia la frontera oriental frente a las amenazas emergentes. Escondida en los densos bosques del noreste de Vallefresno, Canción del Bosque fue antaño un elegante asentamiento de los kaldorei. Hoy en día, sus columnas de piedra blanca y arcos en ruinas están cubiertos de hiedra y helechos silvestres. Situadas al noreste de Satyrnaar y justo al norte del invasivo Aserradero Grito de Guerra, las ruinas ofrecen un mirador tranquilo y estratégico a lo largo de los senderos orientales hacia Azshara y Talloumbrío. Aunque los bosques que la rodean están plagados de corrupción demoníaca e incursiones de la Horda, la ruina en sí conserva una sobrecogedora y sosegada quietud.

ang.class:Druid: The quiet presence of Kayneth Stillwind underscores the Cenarion Circle's solitary vigil in corrupted borderlands, situated right beneath the shadowed canopy near the Great Tree of Bough Shadow.
ang.faction:Alliance: Forest Song serves as a vital solitary outpost for Alliance adventurers cutting across northeastern Ashenvale toward Azshara or Felwood.

faq.a: Currently, Forest Song is inhabited by the night elf druid Kayneth Stillwind, who stands watch alone amidst the ancient ruins.
faq.q: Who lives at Forest Song?

faq.a: The ruins lie perilously close to Satyrnaar to the southwest, crawling with corrupted satyrs, and the Warsong Lumber Camp to the south. To the northeast lies Bough Shadow, where the green dragonflight guards a Great Tree leading into the Emerald Dream.
faq.q: What threats are near Forest Song?

faq.a: Kayneth monitors hostile movements throughout the eastern forests, directing allies against regional dangers—including sinister ventures and diseases spread by the Forsaken operating in the area.
faq.q: Why is Kayneth Stillwind stationed here?

faq.a: No. Unlike Astranaar, Forest Song is largely an unfortified ruin without an active garrison, vendors, or military infrastructure, maintained only as a lone forward lookout post.
faq.q: Is Forest Song a major Alliance settlement?

text.s: Forest Song is an ancient night elf ruin nestled in northeastern Ashenvale, near the tainted woods of Satyrnaar and the great portal at Bough Shadow. At present, it stands largely deserted save for the vigilant druid Kayneth Stillwind, who watches over the eastern border against emergent threats.

sec.b: Tucked away in the dense woodlands of northeastern Ashenvale, Forest Song was once an elegant settlement of the kaldorei. Today, white stone columns and crumbling archways are overgrown with ivy and wild ferns. Located northeast of Satyrnaar and just north of the encroaching Warsong Lumber Camp, the ruins hold a quiet, strategic overlook along the eastern trails toward Azshara and Bough Shadow. While the woods around it are plagued by demonic corruption and Horde incursions, the ruin itself maintains a haunting, tranquil stillness.
sec.t: A Lonely Vigil in Eastern Ashenvale

sec.b: Forest Song is currently manned solely by the druid Kayneth Stillwind. From this crumbling outpost, Stillwind keeps a watchful eye on the dark designs of enemies entering the wilderness, including the unsettling presence of the Forsaken in the eastern forests. Though isolated far from Astranaar and lacking garrison fortifications, the sanctuary serves as an important rallying point for Alliance travelers venturing toward the northern road into Felwood or investigating the corruptions seeping across the canopy.

subzone:forlorn-rowe.s: Loma Inhóspita. La Loma Inhóspita es una colina lúgubre y sombría situada en el límite septentrional del Cementerio del Cerro del Cuervo, en el Bosque del Ocaso. Es tristemente célebre por ser la oscura morada de Morbent Vil, un nigromante cuya magia malévola reanima a los muertos inquietos por todo el bosque. Elevándose a lo largo del extremo norte del Cementerio del Cerro del Cuervo, la Loma Inhóspita se halla perpetuamente envuelta en penumbra. En lo alto de esta elevación se encuentra el hogar de Morbent Vil, el nigromante similar a un liche responsable de gran parte de los muertos vivientes que acechan las tierras salvajes circundantes. Atado por viles encantamientos arcanos, el señor de la colina dirige a sus sirvientes esqueléticos desde esta atalaya, haciendo que todo el rincón noroccidental del Bosque del Ocaso sea peligroso para los viajeros.

ang.class:Paladin: The dark rites woven at the Forlorn Rowe represent an affront to the Holy Light, requiring consecrated relics and righteous wrath to pierce the necromancer's wards.
ang.faction:Alliance: Rooting out Morbent Fel from the Forlorn Rowe is critical for restoring a semblance of safety to Duskwood's western border.

faq.a: The Forlorn Rowe is situated in northwestern Duskwood, resting directly on the northern ridge overlooking the sprawling Raven Hill Cemetery.
faq.q: Where is the Forlorn Rowe located?

faq.a: It is the lair of Morbent Fel, a powerful and malevolent necromancer who uses dark arcane rites to raise and command the legions of undead wandering Duskwood.
faq.q: Who lives at the Forlorn Rowe?

faq.a: Morbent Fel shields himself with foul sorcery, rendering mundane attacks almost useless until he is stripped of his dark protections by a consecrated relic crafted to dispel his magic.
faq.q: Why is Morbent Fel so hard to fight here?

faq.a: Yes, it stands as an elevated bluff along the northern boundary of the Raven Hill Cemetery, directly overlooking the graves and crypts below.
faq.q: Is the Forlorn Rowe part of the cemetery?

text.s: The Forlorn Rowe is an ominous, shadowy hill perched on the northern boundary of the Raven Hill Cemetery in Duskwood. It is infamous as the dark abode of Morbent Fel, a necromancer whose malevolent magic animates the restless dead throughout the forest.

sec.b: Rising along the northern edge of the Raven Hill Cemetery, the Forlorn Rowe is perpetually cloaked in gloom. Atop this rise sits the home of Morbent Fel, the lich-like necromancer responsible for much of the walking dead haunting the surrounding wilderness. Bound by foul arcane enchantments, the master of the hill directs his skeletal servants from this vantage, rendering the entire northwestern corner of Duskwood perilous for travelers.

Morbent Fel's grasp on the Forlorn Rowe cannot be broken by ordinary steel alone. His dark enchantments protect his physical form from mortal weapons until he is weakened by specialized relics of holy power. Bringing down the necromancer and breaking his hold over the woods requires adventurers to secure consecrated armaments, striking at the heart of the curse smothering the cemetery grounds.

subzone:freewind-post.s: Poblado Viento Libre. El Poblado Viento Libre es el principal puesto de avanzada de la Horda en Las Mil Agujas, encaramado en lo alto de una de las impresionantes mesetas de piedra del cañón. Accesible principalmente mediante un ascensor tauren y serpenteantes puentes de cuerda, sirve como refugio defensivo frente a las partidas de guerra centauro y como un enclave fronterizo vital. Construido directamente sobre las mesetas del cañón, el Poblado Viento Libre confía en el ingenio y la altura para proteger a su gente. Los centauros Galak dominan el árido fondo del cañón que se extiende abajo, pero no pueden escalar con eficacia los imponentes acantilados ni franquear los pesados montacargas de madera que suben a los viajeros de la Horda hacia el cielo. Un laberinto de puentes de cuerdas y tablones conecta Viento Libre con las agujas vecinas, conformando un nido seguro. Más allá de mantener a raya a las partidas de saqueo centauro, el puesto de avanzada también ayuda a controlar a las chillonas arpías que anidan a lo largo de los riscos y atiende los cercanos terrenos de dracoleones en Nido Alto, donde se recolectan huevos salvajes para criarlos como leales monturas de jinete del viento para la Horda.

ang.faction:Horde: Freewind Post is the sole major Horde sanctuary and flight connection between the Southern Barrens and Tanaris, providing essential logistical support across central Kalimdor.
ang.race:Tauren: Freewind Post displays the architectural ingenuity of the shu'halo, adapting mesa heights to shut out traditional centaur marauders while tending the ancestral wyverns of the bluffs.

faq.a: The vertical layout keeps the settlement safe from the hostile Galak centaur warbands patrolling the canyon bottom. Centaur excel on flat terrain but cannot scale sheer cliff faces or easily breach the mechanical wooden lifts used by the tauren.
al: why is freewind post in the sky
faq.q: Why is Freewind Post built so high up on a mesa?

faq.a: Most travelers use the large mechanical wooden lifts stationed at the base of the main mesa. There is also a back route consisting of a precarious series of rope bridges and wooden ramps winding between neighboring rock pillars, though a careless step can mean a lethal plunge to the canyon floor.
al: how to get up freewind post
faq.q: How do you get up and down from the post?

faq.a: Relations are deeply strained. The Grimtotem occupying Darkcloud Pinnacle northwest of Freewind Post are accused of murders, kidnappings, and unprovoked hostility toward other tauren, leaving the outpost's defenders in a state of quiet vigilance against their neighboring kin.
faq.q: What is the relationship between Freewind Post and the Grimtotem?

faq.a: Highperch is an ancestral nesting ground for wild wyverns just across the canyon. The tauren of Freewind Post monitor these beasts and cull eggs from their nests, which are then nurtured and raised to serve as wind rider mounts throughout the Horde.
faq.q: What importance does Highperch have to the post?

text.s: Freewind Post is the primary Horde outpost in Thousand Needles, perched high atop one of the canyon's dramatic stone mesas. Accessible primarily by tauren lift and winding rope bridges, it serves as a defensive refuge against centaur warbands and a vital frontier staging ground.

sec.b: Built directly upon the canyon mesas, Freewind Post relies on ingenuity and height to safeguard its people. The Galak centaur dominate the arid canyon floor below, but they cannot effectively scale the towering cliffs or breach the heavy wooden elevators that haul Horde travelers up into the sky. A labyrinth of rope and plank bridges connects Freewind to neighboring spires, forming a secure aerie. Beyond keeping centaur raiding parties at bay, the outpost also helps manage the screeching harpies nesting along the bluffs and tends to the nearby wyvern grounds at Highperch, where wild eggs are culled and trained as loyal wind rider mounts for the Horde.

Despite its impregnable height, Freewind Post faces growing tension with its neighbors to the northwest: the Grimtotem tribe stationed at Darkcloud Pinnacle. Once tolerated as stubborn traditionalists, the Grimtotem under Chieftain Arnak have increasingly turned to violence, kidnapping, and murder. Suspicious rituals and whispers of dark power surround the nearby peaks. The local tauren watch the skies and rope bridges with growing dread, conscious that their most dangerous enemies do not prowl the salt flats below, but sit entrenched across the canyon winds.

subzone:frostmane-hold.s: Poblado Peloescarcha. Poblado Peloescarcha es un campamento fortificado y un complejo de cavernas reclamado por los trols de hielo Peloescarcha en el oeste de Dun Morogh. Escondido entre los riscos al sur de Gnomeregan, sirve como base de operaciones central para los asaltantes trols que invaden el territorio enano. La Guardia de Forjaz vigila de cerca el poblado para calibrar la creciente amenaza trol. Esculpido en los gélidos acantilados del oeste de Dun Morogh, Poblado Peloescarcha está formado por toscas estructuras al aire libre y un sinuoso sistema de cuevas. Para la tribu Peloescarcha, funciona como su fortaleza principal, fuertemente custodiada por despellejadores y cazadores de cabezas. Desde aquí, los trols lanzan incursiones hacia los valles circundantes, poniendo a prueba las defensas de asentamientos cercanos como Kharanos y amenazando a los viajeros a lo largo de los pasos de montaña.

ang.race:Dwarf: The Frostmane have contested Dun Morogh for centuries, and clearing out Frostmane Hold is a rite of passage for mountaineers seeking to safeguard Ironforge's snowy heartland.
ang.race:Gnome: Nestled just south of Gnomeregan, the hold represents yet another dangerous hostile front bordering the embattled former gnome capital.

faq.a: The stronghold is occupied by the Frostmane tribe of ice trolls, specifically their hunters, hideskinners, and headhunters, along with their chieftains and raiders.
faq.q: Who lives in Frostmane Hold?

faq.a: It lies in the western mountains of Dun Morogh, situated south of the industrial ruins of Gnomeregan and west of Kharanos.
faq.q: Where is Frostmane Hold located?

faq.a: Dwarven leaders in Kharanos fear that the Frostmane are massing in numbers large enough to stage serious raids on settlements, prompting military leaders to send scouts to map the caves and thin their ranks.
faq.q: Why are the dwarves interested in this cave?

faq.a: No. In the present era, the stronghold belongs firmly to the Frostmane ice trolls. Trogg activity in Dun Morogh remains primarily centered around their own dens and the ruins of Gnomeregan.
faq.q: Are there troggs in Frostmane Hold?

text.s: Frostmane Hold is a fortified encampment and cavern complex claimed by the Frostmane ice trolls in western Dun Morogh. Tucked into the crags south of Gnomeregan, it serves as a central staging ground for troll raiders encroaching on dwarven territory. The Ironforge Guard keeps a close watch on the hold to gauge the growing troll threat.

sec.b: Carved into the freezing cliffs of western Dun Morogh, Frostmane Hold consists of rough outdoor structures and a winding cave system. For the Frostmane tribe, it functions as a primary stronghold, densely guarded by hideskinners and headhunters. From here, the trolls launch raids into the surrounding valleys, testing the defenses of nearby settlements like Kharanos and menacing travelers along the mountain passes.
sec.t: A Troll Bastion in the Snows

sec.b: As tensions in Dun Morogh mount, dwarven commanders in Kharanos have grown increasingly concerned about the scale of the Frostmane buildup. Young mountaineers and adventurers are routinely dispatched to scout the interior caverns, map out the defenses, and cull the warbands before the tribe can muster an organized assault against dwarven outposts.

subzone:frostmane-hovel.s: Cobertizo Peloescarcha. Cobertizo Peloescarcha es una guarida en una cueva escarpada escondida en los riscos meridionales del Valle de Crestanevada, en Dun Morogh. Sirve como refugio atrincherado para los agresivos troles Peloescarcha que presionan directamente los campos de entrenamiento de los enanos. Excavado en las montañas del sur que flanquean el Valle de Crestanevada, Cobertizo Peloescarcha da cobijo a troles Peloescarcha autóctonos que se niegan a ceder las nieves perpetuas a Forjaz. Operando desde cavernas rudimentarias como esta, los troles organizan continuos ataques contra los campamentos enanos locales e interrumpen las líneas de suministro hacia el valle.

ang.faction:Alliance: The persistent Frostmane presence right outside Anvilmar highlights how even the heartland of Ironforge must constantly defend itself against local adversaries.
ang.race:Dwarf: For young Bronzebeard recruits training in Coldridge Valley, securing the perimeter against the hostile Frostmane tribe in caves like this is an essential rite of passage.

faq.a: The Frostmane Hovel is a natural cavern in southern Coldridge Valley used as a foul-weather encampment by indigenous Frostmane trolls encroaching on dwarven territory.
faq.q: What is the Frostmane Hovel?

faq.a: The Frostmane tribe has inhabited the snowy peaks of Dun Morogh for generations. Bitter rivals of the Bronzebeard dwarves, they constantly push inward from the high ridges to raid supply paths and challenge dwarven settlements.
faq.q: Why are there trolls in Coldridge Valley?

faq.a: The cave is occupied by raiding Frostmane trolls who use the sheltered crevice to stage incursions across the southern shelf of the valley.
faq.q: Who controls this cave?

text.s: Frostmane Hovel is a rugged cave den tucked into the southern crags of Coldridge Valley in Dun Morogh. It serves as an entrenched shelter for aggressive Frostmane trolls pressing directly into dwarven training grounds.

sec.b: Carved into the southern mountains flanking Coldridge Valley, the Frostmane Hovel shelters indigenous Frostmane trolls who refuse to yield the high snows to Ironforge. Operating out of crude caverns like this, the trolls mount continuous raids against local dwarven camps and disrupt supply lines into the valley.
sec.t: A Troll Den in the Valley

subzone:galardell-valley.s: Valle de Galardell. El Valle de Galardell es un cañón escarpado y peligroso enclavado en las alturas del noreste de las Montañas Crestagrana. El desfiladero está infestado de agresivas manadas de gnomos y se alza bajo la sombra de la infame Torre de Ilgalar. Esculpido en los acantilados del noreste de Crestagrana, el Valle de Galardell ha escapado por completo al control de los defensores de Villa del Lago. Fieros gnomos de Crestagrana merodean por las tierras bajas y acampan a lo largo del fondo del cañón, organizados bajo brutales líderes de manada como el teniente Fangore. Elevándose por encima de los barrancos se encuentra la oscura aguja de la Torre de Ilgalar, el bastión del mago renegado Morganth, lo que convierte a todo el valle en una fuente constante de pavor para los asentamientos cercanos.

ang.faction:Alliance: Lakeshire's overwhelmed town guard cannot secure the northeast road as long as gnoll packs and Morganth's dark presence hold Galardell Valley.

faq.a: Galardell Valley is situated in the far northeastern corner of the Redridge Mountains, tucked behind the high crags beyond the roads leading north from Lake Everstill.
faq.q: Where is Galardell Valley located?

faq.a: The valley is overrun by bloodthirsty gnoll packs who patrol the trails in dense clusters, led by dangerous brutes like Lieutenant Fangore.
faq.q: What creatures live in the valley?

faq.a: That is the Tower of Ilgalar, an imposing stone structure that serves as the base of operations for the rogue sorcerer Morganth.
faq.q: What is the dark tower overlooking the valley?

faq.a: Lieutenant Fangore is a formidable gnoll leader stationed within the valley. Known for his cunning and ferocity, he will howl for aid from nearby gnoll packs when challenged, quickly overwhelming unwary travelers.
faq.q: Who is Lieutenant Fangore?

text.s: Galardell Valley is a rugged, dangerous canyon nestled in the northeastern heights of the Redridge Mountains. The gorge is overrun by aggressive gnoll packs and sits beneath the shadow of the infamous Tower of Ilgalar.

sec.b: Carved into the northeastern cliffs of Redridge, Galardell Valley has fallen completely out of the control of Lakeshire's defenders. Fierce Redridge gnolls prowl the lowlands and camp along the canyon floor, organized under brutal pack leaders such as Lieutenant Fangore. Towering high above the ravines stands the dark spire of the Tower of Ilgalar, the stronghold of the renegade mage Morganth, making the entire valley a persistent source of dread for the surrounding settlements.
sec.t: A Den of Beasts and Shadow

subzone:gallows-end-tavern.s: Mesón La Horca. El Mesón La Horca es la posada principal de Rémol y el corazón de la hospitalidad de los Renegados en los Claros de Tirisfal. Más allá de ofrecer cobijo y licores a los viajeros agotados, sirve como un centro esencial para mentores de clase, instructores de profesión e interrogatorios encubiertos. Erigido de forma prominente junto al camino en Rémol, el Mesón La Horca sirve como el principal punto de encuentro para los Renegados recién despertados que parten de Camposanto y viajan hacia el sur, rumbo a Entrañas. A pesar de su condición de no-muertos, los Renegados siguen frecuentando sus salas en busca de camaradería, comercio y refugio. La posada alberga a varios instructores de clase —que guían a jóvenes guerreros, sacerdotes, magos, pícaros y brujos—, así como a vendedores y profesionales de la medicina.

ang.faction:Alliance: Beneath the taproom floors, the Forsaken keep captured Alliance scouts and Scarlet Crusade zealots detained for intelligence and interrogation.
ang.race:Undead: As the first major inn encountered outside Deathknell, Gallows' End Tavern serves as the cultural and functional crossroads for newly awakened Forsaken entering the wider world.

faq.a: It is located in the center of Brill, the main Forsaken settlement just north of the Undercity in Tirisfal Glades.
faq.q: Where is the Gallows' End Tavern located?

faq.a: While the Forsaken do not require sleep or mortal sustenance to survive, taverns like Gallows' End maintain social bonds and cultural habits from their past lives. It also acts as a secure civic center for training, commerce, and official business.
faq.q: Why do the undead need an inn or tavern?

faq.a: In the cellars beneath the tavern, the Forsaken hold captive enemies including a Scarlet Zealot from the hostile Scarlet Crusade and an Alliance Dwarven Mountaineer.
faq.q: Who is imprisoned in the basement?

faq.a: The tavern features instructors for warriors, priests, mages, rogues, and warlocks, along with first aid and enchanting trainers, general trade vendors, and an innkeeper.
faq.q: What services and trainers can be found here?

text.s: Gallows' End Tavern is the principal inn of Brill and the heart of Forsaken hospitality in Tirisfal Glades. Beyond offering shelter and spirits to weary travelers, it serves as an essential hub for class mentors, trade instructors, and covert interrogations.

sec.b: Standing prominently along the road in Brill, Gallows' End Tavern serves as the primary gathering place for newly awakened Forsaken leaving Deathknell and journeying south toward the Undercity. Despite their undead condition, Forsaken still frequent its halls for fellowship, trade, and refuge. The inn houses various class instructors—guiding young warriors, priests, mages, rogues, and warlocks—as well as vendors and medical practitioners.
sec.t: A Gathering Place for the Dead

sec.b: Beneath the creaking floorboards and tavern laughter lies a far grimmer purpose. Down in the cellars, the Forsaken keep prisoners of war bound and guarded away from public view. Among them are a captured Scarlet Zealot and a Dwarven Mountaineer, held beneath the tavern for interrogation and experimentation as the Forsaken fight to secure their borders against both zealous crusaders and Alliance scouts.

subzone:gates-of-ironforge.s: Puertas de Forjaz. Las Puertas de Forjaz sirven como la monumental entrada principal que conduce a los viajeros desde los valles montañosos y nevados de Dun Morogh hasta la capital enana. Talladas directamente en la escarpada roca de la montaña, en su interior están custodiadas por una estatua colosal del rey supremo Modimus Yunquemar. Al aproximarse subiendo por la rampa serpenteante y fortificada que asciende desde el centro de Dun Morogh, las Puertas de Forjaz presentan una fachada imponente visible desde gran parte de las llanuras nevadas.
