Arathi is a fiercely contested crossroads. In the northeast, the Horde converted an abandoned human internment camp into Hammerfall, named in honor of the legendary Warchief Orgrim Doomhammer, using it as an anchor to secure their northern holdings and safeguard allies in Hillsbrad. Meanwhile, the Witherbark troll tribe seeks vengeance against their ancient human persecutors, and the Argus Wake pulls strings behind the Syndicate's occupation. At the center of the plateau lie ancient Circles of Binding, where bound elementals restrain an enigmatic, ancient power buried beneath the stone.

zone:ashenvale.s: Vallefresno. Vallefresno es el ancestral bosque de los elfos de la noche, empapado por la lluvia y considerado sagrado bajo la protección de las Centinelas y el semidiós Cenarius. Limita con Los Baldíos al sur y Costa Oscura al norte, y se ha convertido en una enconada zona de guerra mientras la Horda tala madera para construir su joven nación. Árboles milenarios y tranquilos pozos de la luna comparten dosel con reductos demoníacos, hombres bestia hostiles y puntos de conflicto a lo largo de la disputada frontera. Extendiéndose bajo el Monte Hyjal, Vallefresno ha perdurado durante milenios bajo la custodia de los kaldorei y los hijos de Cenarius. Inmensos árboles se entrelazan en un denso dosel que transforma la lluvia diaria en una suave bruma y sume el suelo del bosque en un crepúsculo eterno. Antiguas ruinas de la civilización élfica asoman entre el musgo, custodiadas por ancestros caminantes y dríades. Durante miles de años, los elfos de la noche no construyeron verdaderas ciudades aquí, prefiriendo cazar con moderación y preservar el dominio salvaje en un equilibrio prístino.

ang.class:Druid: The balance of nature here is under siege on multiple fronts. Between the lumber operations, corrupted furbolg dens, and the nightmare-haunted portal at Bough Shadow, Ashenvale desperately needs Cenarion restoration.
ang.profession:Herbalism: Fed by ancient magical leyways and perpetual rainfall, Ashenvale is one of Kalimdor's richest foraging zones for Briarthorn, Stranglekelp, Kingsblood, and rare Gromsblood around demonic scars.
ang.race:NightElf: Ashenvale is your spiritual backyard and the legacy of Cenarius. Defending its groves against Warsong axes and weeding out satyr corruption from its moonwells is a matter of primal kaldorei honor.
ang.race:Orc: This timber fuels the very walls and siege towers of Orgrimmar. It is also sacred ground where Grommash Hellscream shed blood to redeem the orcish race from demonic servitude.

faq.a: The orcs of Durotar have virtually no timber in their dry homeland and desperately need Ashenvale's lumber to build Orgrimmar and fuel their young nation. To the night elves, Ashenvale is a sacred ancestral homeland protected by nature deities. The Silverwing Sentinels view the Warsong clan's clear-cutting operations as intolerable desecration, sparking constant skirmishes and the pitched struggle in Warsong Gulch.
faq.q: Why are the Horde and Alliance fighting in Ashenvale?

faq.a: During the Third War, Grommash Hellscream led the Warsong clan into Ashenvale to gather timber. Cenarius attacked the orcs to defend the sacred grove. Desperate to defeat the demigod, Grommash and his clan drank from a fountain tainted by the pit lord Mannoroth, gaining demonic fury and slaying Cenarius. Although Grom later broke the curse by slaying Mannoroth at Demon Fall Canyon, the elves have not forgotten the murder of their patron demigod.
faq.q: What happened to Cenarius in this forest?

faq.a: Blackfathom Deeps is a sunken temple complex situated beneath the Zoram Strand along Ashenvale's northwestern coastline. Formerly an ancient kaldorei temple dedicated to Elune, it collapsed into the sea during the Great Sundering. It is now overrun by savage naga, Twilight's Hammer cultists, and aquatic beasts who revere the ancient hydra Aku'mai.
faq.q: What is Blackfathom Deeps?

faq.a: Bough Shadow is home to one of four Great Trees planted by the Cenarion Circle thousands of years ago to anchor conduits into the Emerald Dream and contain saronite corruption. It serves as an active gateway between Azeroth and the Dream. Green dragonspawn guard the area, though a sinister taint within the Dream occasionally drives monstrous Nightmare Dragons through the portal.
faq.q: What is the Great Tree at Bough Shadow?

faq.a: While the night elves maintained peaceful alliances with the furbolgs for centuries, the demonic taint left by the Burning Legion's invasion shattered their minds. Residual fel magic radiating from places like Felwood, Satyrnaar, and Demon Fall Canyon drove tribes like the Thistlefur into violent insanity, turning them hostile to outsiders and kin alike.
faq.q: Why are the furbolgs in Ashenvale hostile?

faq.a: Demon Fall Canyon is the battlefield where Grommash Hellscream and Thrall confronted the pit lord Mannoroth. Grom struck down the demon lord with a fatal blow, freeing the orcish race from the demonic blood curse at the cost of his own life. Mannoroth's shattered armor remains mounted on a stone monument there in memorial to Hellscream's sacrifice.
faq.q: Who is buried at Demon Fall Canyon?

faq.a: Alliance travelers generally enter through the northern mountain pass from Auberdine in Darkshore, following the highway east toward Astranaar. Horde adventurers march north out of the Barrens through the fortified Mor'shan Rampart toward Splintertree Post or west to Zoram'gar Outpost on the Zoram Strand. Both factions maintain flight masters at their major fortresses.
faq.q: How do I travel through Ashenvale?

text.s: Ashenvale is the ancient, rain-drenched ancestral forest of the night elves, held sacred under the protection of the Sentinels and the demigod Cenarius. Bordering the Barrens to the south and Darkshore to the north, it has erupted into a bitter war zone as the Horde harvests timber to build its young nation. Ancient trees and tranquil moonwells share canopy with demonic holdouts, hostile beastmen, and clash points along the contested frontier.

sec.b: Stretching beneath Mount Hyjal, Ashenvale has stood for millennia under the stewardship of the kaldorei and the children of Cenarius. Immense trees knit together into a dense canopy that turns daily rain into a gentle mist and casts the forest floor in eternal twilight. Ancient ruins of elven civilization poke through the moss, guarded by walking ancients and dryads. For thousands of years, the night elves built no true cities here, preferring to hunt lightly and preserve the wild domain in pristine balance.

The peace shattered during the Third War when Grommash Hellscream and the Warsong clan penetrated the forest for lumber, slaying Cenarius after falling to demonic bloodlust. Today in 25 ADP, the struggle has become a full-scale territorial war. From Splintertree Post and the southern Mor'shan Rampart, the Warsong Outriders drive axes and shredders into the eastern woods to supply Orgrimmar. The Silverwing Sentinels, based in the sanctuary town of Astranaar, have sworn to expel every last orcish logger from the sacred grove.

The lumber war is far from Ashenvale's only peril. The Burning Legion left scarred blights at Felfire Hill and Demon Fall Canyon, where Mannoroth met his end. Cruel satyrs operate out of ruins like Satyrnaar and Xavian, corrupting waterways and wildlife. Furbolg tribes, once friends of the elves, have largely succumbed to dark madness. Meanwhile, mysterious worgen stalk the northern shrine near Felwood, and cursed dragonkin prowl Bough Shadow, guarding a portal into the troubled Emerald Dream.

zone:azshara.s: Azshara. Azshara es una costa escarpada y azotada por el viento en el noreste de Kalimdor, cubierta por un vibrante y perpetuo follaje otoñal. Antaño parte de la gloriosa capital de los elfos de la noche antes de que el Gran Cataclismo la arrojara al mar, sigue siendo un territorio salvaje y peligroso sembrado de ruinas antiguas, nagas taciturnos y practicantes de la magia aislados. Tanto la Horda como la Alianza mantienen precarios puestos de avanzada a lo largo de sus fronteras, cautelosos ante los fantasmas inquietos y los horrores oceánicos que acechan en su interior. Hace diez mil años, esta costa era el corazón palpitante de la civilización kaldorei, rodeando la capital real de Zin-Azshari. Cuando la reina Azshara y su corte de Altonato atrajeron a la Legión Ardiente a Azeroth, la consiguiente Guerra de los Ancestros culminó en el catastrófico colapso del Pozo de la Eternidad. El mar se precipitó tierra adentro con gran estruendo, devorando la mayor parte de la magnífica ciudad y dejando a su paso acantilados fracturados, traicioneros arrecifes de coral y agujas anegadas. Los supervivientes rebautizaron el paisaje en ruinas con el nombre de su monarca caída, marcándolo como un monumento maldito al orgullo y a la traición catastrófica.

ang.class:Mage: The shattered stones of Eldarath still crackle with forgotten Highborne sorcery, and high above the cliffs, the reclusive Archmage Xylem tests those seeking mastery of arcane teleportation and spellcraft.
ang.profession:Herbalism: Azshara's perpetual autumn climate sustains rare and potent herbs, including Dreamfoil, Golden Sansam, Mountain Silversage, and Purple Lotus among the ruins.
ang.profession:Mining: The steep coastal cliffs and jagged ridges of Azshara are rich in precious mineral veins, containing abundant deposits of Mithril, Truesilver, and Thorium.
ang.race:NightElf: Every drowned pillar and wailing Highborne shade in Azshara serves as a grim, haunting testament to Queen Azshara's reckless arrogance and the cataclysmic ruin of the ancient kaldorei civilization.

faq.a: Azshara is cloaked in a perpetual autumn. The vibrant orange, gold, and red canopy never sheds its leaves, giving the coastal woods a strikingly beautiful yet melancholy atmosphere that has persisted for thousands of years.
faq.q: Why are all the trees red and orange here?

faq.a: This coastline once formed the outskirts of the kaldorei capital, Zin-Azshari. During the War of the Ancients, the Well of Eternity imploded during the Great Sundering, sundering the continent and sending vast portions of the city tumbling into the sea.
faq.q: How did Azshara become a ruin?

faq.a: No single faction holds dominion over the territory. The Alliance maintains a small watch at Talrendis Point near Ashenvale, while the Horde operates out of the encampment of Valormok. The surrounding land is dominated by dangerous Spitelash naga, violent satyrs, and untamed monsters.
faq.q: Who rules Azshara today?

faq.a: Archmage Xylem is an eccentric human sorcerer residing in a remote cliffside tower overlooking Azshara. Unaligned with regional politics, he aids visiting mages and rogues in unlocking unique martial and arcane potential through challenging trials.
faq.q: Who is Archmage Xylem?

faq.a: The great blue dragon Azuregos and his brood watch over the ancient ruins of Eldarath. He fiercely protects the powerful Highborne magical artifacts still buried in the rubble from being plundered by mortal hands.
faq.q: What is the blue dragon doing in the ruins?

faq.a: The kaldorei consider Azshara cursed because it bears the name and architectural legacy of their treacherous Queen Azshara, whose pact with the Burning Legion shattered their empire and brought ruin to the world.
al: why do night elves hate azshara
faq.q: Why do the night elves consider this land cursed?

text.s: Azshara is a rugged, windswept coastline in northeastern Kalimdor cloaked in vibrant, perpetual autumn foliage. Once part of the glorious night elven capital before the Great Sundering shattered it into the sea, it remains a dangerous wilderness littered with ancient ruins, brooding naga, and isolated practitioners of magic. Both the Horde and the Alliance maintain precarious outposts along its borders, wary of the restless ghosts and ocean horrors lurking within.

sec.b: Ten thousand years ago, this coast was the beating heart of the kaldorei civilization, surrounding the royal capital of Zin-Azshari. When Queen Azshara and her Highborne court drew the Burning Legion into Azeroth, the resulting War of the Ancients culminated in the catastrophic collapse of the Well of Eternity. The sea thundered inward, swallowing most of the magnificent city and leaving behind fractured cliffs, treacherous coral reefs, and waterlogged spires. The survivors renamed the ruined landscape after their fallen monarch, branding it as a cursed monument to pride and catastrophic betrayal.

Azshara is famous for its stunning crimson, orange, and gold canopy, giving the impression of an eternal autumn unbroken by changing seasons. Beneath this tranquil canopy, however, lies an inhospitable expanse. Corrupted satyrs practice dark rituals in forested hollows, lingering Highborne apparitions haunt drowned foundations, and Spitelash naga prowl the shallow reefs of the Coral Sea. Ferocious beasts, giant hydras, and mountain giants roam unchecked across the highlands and ivory beaches.

Because of its isolation and harsh terrain, Azshara draws recluse figures pursuing forgotten crafts or watching over dangerous powers. The enigmatic Archmage Xylem inhabits a secluded tower perched high above the cliffs, testing promising spellcasters and cunning rogues alike. Farther along the coast, the demon hunter Loramus Thalipedes watches the waves from a barren isle, while the immense sea giant Lord Arkkoroc demands blood sacrifices from his temple overlooking the churning waters.
sec.t: A Realm of Exiles and Outcasts

zone:badlands.s: Tierras Inhóspitas. Tierras Inhóspitas es una extensión árida y castigada por el sol, repleta de tierra agrietada, tormentas de polvo y cañones rocosos, enclavada entre Loch Modan y La Garganta de Fuego. A pesar de encontrarse en las profundidades del Khaz Modan enano, sirve como una frontera inestable dominada por enanos Hierro Negro, troggs, ogros Rotapolvo y dracónidos negros anidando. También alberga las ruinas titánicas de Uldaman y el bastión de la Horda de Kargath, lo que la convierte en un punto de paso estratégico crucial. Situada al sur de las verdes colinas de Loch Modan, Tierras Inhóspitas se transforma rápidamente en una cuenca sofocante de llanuras yermas y barrancos escarpados. Sobrevivir aquí exige enfrentarse a coyotes despiadados, pumas, buitres y feroces tormentas de arena que oscurecen el horizonte. Dispersos por las mesetas se encuentran los toscos campamentos de los ogros Rotapolvo, mientras que el sombrío clan Hierro Negro fortifica la Fortaleza de Angor y choca con cualquiera que traspase su territorio.

ang.faction:Horde: Kargath serves as your sole military sanctuary deep in Khaz Modan, acting as the frontline against the Dark Horde occupying Blackrock Mountain.
ang.profession:Mining: The arid landscape is rich in iron, gold, truesilver, and mithril, including rare Indurium deposits found within Uldaman and the surrounding terrain.
ang.race:Dwarf: The Badlands holds the answers to your very ancestry within Uldaman, where the discovery of the titan-forged earthen reshaped dwarven understanding of history.

faq.a: The outpost of Kargath was established by the Kargath Expeditionary Force on orders from Warchief Thrall. Stationed under Warlord Goretooth, the encampment provides the Horde a vital staging ground to strike against Rend Blackhand and his renegade Blackrock clan entrenched within Blackrock Mountain.
faq.q: Why is the Horde stationed in the Badlands?

faq.a: Alliance travelers can walk directly south from Loch Modan through the Maker's Terrace pass. Horde travelers face a longer trek on foot through the southern hills of Loch Modan or through Searing Gorge via the western mountain pass before unlocking Kargath's flight master.
faq.q: How do you get to the Badlands?

faq.a: Uldaman is a massive underground vault built by the ancient titans and their earthen servants. Though recently excavated by dwarven prospectors seeking the secrets of dwarven origins, the dig awoke buried earthen constructs and primitive Stonevault troggs, turning the ruin into a lethal battleground.
faq.q: What is Uldaman?

faq.a: Lethlor Ravine serves as an eastern breeding and nesting canyon for the black dragonflight. Guarded by drakes and whelps, the clutch maintains a dangerous presence near the mountains, preying upon wanderers and guarding the eastern reaches from trespassers.
faq.q: What are the black dragons doing in Lethlor Ravine?

faq.a: Angor Fortress is held by the hostile Dark Iron clan. Situated south of Uldaman, the fortress serves as a regional base where the Dark Irons conduct reconnaissance, contest the titan digsites, and battle neighboring ogres and surface explorers.
faq.q: Who controls Angor Fortress?

faq.a: No. The Badlands has no fortified Alliance settlements or flight masters. Ironforge prospectors and solitary hermits maintain scattered, fragile camps near the digsites, but Alliance adventurers must rely on bases in Loch Modan or Searing Gorge for extensive supplies.
faq.q: Are there any friendly settlements for Alliance players here?

text.s: The Badlands is an arid, sun-baked expanse of cracked earth, dust storms, and rocky canyons nestled between Loch Modan and Searing Gorge. Despite being deep within dwarven Khaz Modan, it serves as a volatile frontier dominated by Dark Iron dwarves, troggs, Dustbelcher ogres, and nesting black dragonkin. It also houses the titan ruins of Uldaman and the Horde stronghold of Kargath, making it a critical strategic waypoint.

sec.b: Wedged south of Loch Modan's verdant hills, the Badlands quickly turns into a sweltering basin of barren flats and rugged ravines. Surviving here requires contending with merciless coyotes, cougars, vultures, and fierce sandstorms that obscure the horizon. Scattered across the plateaus are the crude encampments of the Dustbelcher ogres, while the brooding Dark Iron clan fortifies Angor Fortress and clashes with anyone trespassing on their territory.

In the northern bluffs lies Uldaman, an ancient subterranean complex carved out by the titan-forged earthen. Recently uncovered by Ironforge prospectors, the excavation unearthed monumental secrets regarding the ancient ancestry of the dwarven race. However, digging into the subterranean vaults awoke hordes of vicious Stonevault troggs and animated earthen guardians, slaughtering archaeological teams and turning the digsites outside into bloody skirmish grounds.

The Badlands is one of the Horde's most precarious footholds in the southern Eastern Kingdoms. Established in the northwest, the fortress of Kargath gives Warchief Thrall's forces a base of operations to keep watch on the rogue Dark Horde in nearby Blackrock Mountain. Meanwhile, to the far east lies Lethlor Ravine, a treacherous chasm where black whelps and dangerous black dragonkin guard their brooding grounds under the shadow of the mountains.
sec.t: The Shadows of Kargath and Lethlor

zone:barrens.s: Los Baldíos. Los Baldíos son una vasta sabana abrasada por el sol que sirve como el palpitante corazón geográfico y logístico de la Horda en el centro de Kalimdor. Antaño un frondoso bosque antes del Gran Cataclismo, hoy son una llanura árida de polvo rojo, matorrales resistentes y fauna errante. Centrada en torno al enclave estratégico de El Cruce, esta tierra permanece sumida en una lucha constante contra las tribus de jabaespines, los asaltantes centauros y una corrupción insidiosa. Durante incontables generaciones, los tauren nómadas cazaron kodos y cebras a lo largo de estas llanuras mientras libraban una guerra cíclica y defensiva contra los merodeadores centauros Kolkar. Cuando Thrall guio a los orcos a Kalimdor durante la Tercera Guerra, ayudó a Cairne Pezuña de Sangre a repeler a los centauros y a cruzar la sabana hasta Mulgore. En la actualidad, Los Baldíos conectan Durotar, Mulgore y Vallefresno. Puestos avanzados como El Cruce y Campamento Taurajo aseguran el comercio a lo largo del Camino del Oro, mientras que los asentamientos orcos desafían el clima árido para forjar un hogar duradero.

ang.class:Druid: The twisted waters flowing from the Wailing Caverns represent a profound tragedy, where Naralex's noble attempt to restore the Barrens succumbed to the nightmare.
ang.class:Shaman: The arid plains test your connection to the elements, from the dry earth spirits of the plains to the enchanted, altered waters that bubble up in isolated oases.
ang.faction:Horde: The Barrens is the logistical backbone of your realm; securing the Crossroads and defending supply convoys across the Gold Road ensures the survival of Orgrimmar and Thunder Bluff.
ang.race:Tauren: Before the orcs landed on Kalimdor, your nomadic ancestors wandered these savannas for generations, hunting sacred game and fighting for survival against the ruthless Kolkar centaur.

faq.a: The sudden pools—such as the Forgotten Pools and Lushwater Oasis—are fed by underground springs flowing out of the Wailing Caverns. The night elf druid Naralex tapped into the Emerald Dream to channel spring waters and regreen the arid land, but the venture went awry, saturating the northern Barrens with potent, volatile natural magic.
al: why is there water in barrens
faq.q: Why are there lush oases in the middle of a desert?

faq.a: The Crossroads is garrisoned by the Horde, primarily orc and tauren warriors serving Warchief Thrall. Because it sits at the intersection of the primary trade routes linking Durotar, Mulgore, and Ashenvale, it serves as the Horde's chief strategic military and transit hub in central Kalimdor.
faq.q: Who controls the Crossroads?

faq.a: The quilboar consider the Barrens their ancestral birthright, believing the colossal brambles sprouted from the blood of their demigod, Agamaggan, during the War of the Ancients. They view both the arriving Horde and the native tauren as trespassers stealing their sacred foraging grounds and hunting territory.
faq.q: Why are the quilboar attacking everyone?

faq.a: The Alliance maintains a presence along the edges of the savanna. Northwatch Hold is garrisoned by human troops from Theramore keeping watch over Horde movements, while the dwarves of Bael Modan and Bael'dun Keep are deeply invested in excavating ancient titan artifacts buried in the southern hills.
faq.q: Why are Alliance soldiers in the Barrens?

faq.a: No. Ratchet is an independent goblin port run by Gazlowe. It maintains strict neutrality, acting as a gateway for maritime trade, smugglers, and adventurers of both the Horde and the Alliance, provided everyone respects goblin commerce and keeps weapons sheathed in town.
faq.q: Is Ratchet part of the Horde?

faq.a: Insectoid creatures called silithid have emerged from earthen hives in the southern Barrens, particularly around the Field of Giants. Their sudden appearance and rapid colony growth pose an escalating threat to travelers and local outposts, prompting the Horde to investigate their origins.
faq.q: What is going on with the silithid in the south?

text.s: The Barrens is an expansive, sun-baked savanna that serves as the beating geographical and logistical heart of the Horde in central Kalimdor. Once a verdant forest prior to the Great Sundering, it is now an arid plain of red dust, hardy scrub, and wandering wildlife. Centered around the strategic hub of the Crossroads, the land remains locked in constant struggle against quilboar tribes, centaur raiders, and creeping corruption.

sec.b: For countless generations, nomadic tauren hunted kodo and zhevra across these plains while waging a defensive, cyclical war against marauding Kolkar centaur. When Thrall led the orcs to Kalimdor during the Third War, he aided Cairne Bloodhoof in repelling the centaur and traversing the savanna into Mulgore. Today, the Barrens connects Durotar, Mulgore, and Ashenvale. Outposts like the Crossroads and Camp Taurajo secure trade along the Gold Road, while orcish homesteads brave the arid climate to forge a lasting home.

Despite Horde dominance, control over the savanna is hotly contested. Porcupine-like Razormane quilboar aggressively raid farms and supply lines from their thorn-choked redoubts, backed by the looming dens of Razorfen Kraul to the south. Along the eastern coast, Theramore forces garrison Northwatch Hold, while dwarven prospectors dig into the titan complex of Bael Modan. Meanwhile, the goblins of Ratchet enforce an uneasy mercantile neutrality, welcoming any traveler with coin.

Several oases punctuate the northern plains, their waters unnaturally surging with life-giving vigor. This surge originates from the Wailing Caverns, where the night elf druid Naralex attempted to tap into the Emerald Dream to restore the Barrens to its ancient, forested glory. Instead, a nightmare twisted Naralex's vision. Corrupted water now seeps across the Forgotten Pools and Stagnant Oasis, spawning bizarre deviate flora, unnatural beasts, and the rogue Druids of the Fang.

zone:blackfathom.s: Cavernas de Brazanegra. Cavernas de Brazanegra es un complejo de templos subterráneos inundados situado a lo largo de La Ensenada de Zoram, en el noroeste de Vallefresno. Antaño un santuario dedicado a Elune, la diosa de la luna de los elfos de la noche, este recinto sumergido ha sido tomado por el Martillo Crepuscular, traicioneros naga y sátiros. Se reúnen en sus oscuras aguas para venerar y alimentar a Aku'mai, una mascota primordial y heraldo de los Dioses Antiguos. Mucho antes de que el Gran Cataclismo destrozara el antiguo Kalimdor, este complejo era conocido como Lathar'Lazal, un espléndido templo dedicado a Elune. Los canteros altonato erigieron puentes incrustados de gemas mientras la Reina Azshara dominaba las aguas circundantes, separando los mares salados y los arroyos de montaña alrededor de una poza de la luna sagrada. Cuando el Cataclismo desgarró el mundo hace diez mil años, el templo se hundió en las profundidades costeras del Mar Velado. Durante milenios permaneció imperturbable bajo las olas, hasta que viles susurros comenzaron a filtrarse desde la oscuridad subterránea.

ang.class:Shaman: Shaman answering the call of Je'neu and the Earthen Ring must plunge into the watery dark to halt the corruption of the elements and banish the chaotic taint of the Old Gods.
ang.faction:Alliance: Alliance heroes enter to rescue Scout Thaelrid, recover lost Highborne knowledge, and aid the night elves in cleansing their sacred homeland from cultist terror.
ang.faction:Horde: Operating out of Zoram'gar Outpost, the Horde seeks to secure the northern coast of Ashenvale from encroaching naga aggression and prevent the dark rituals within the deeps from threatening their outposts.
ang.race:NightElf: For night elves, the deeps represent a heartbreaking desecration of their heritage, as an ancient shrine of Elune and its sacred moonwell have been befouled by void cultists and monstrous aberrations.

faq.a: Originally named Lathar'Lazal, it was a magnificent night elven temple dedicated to the moon goddess Elune. It featured crystal-clear pools, gemmed bridges, and a blessed moonwell, all overseen by Queen Azshara before the Great Sundering broke the temple and cast it beneath the sea.
faq.q: What was Blackfathom Deeps before it fell into darkness?

faq.a: Drawn by nightmare visions and whispering voices from beneath Azeroth, the cultists came to worship the Old Gods. Under Twilight Lord Kelris, they took over the sunken ruins to nurture Aku'mai, offering living sacrifices in hopes of hastening the return of their chaotic masters.
faq.q: Why are the Twilight's Hammer cultists here?

faq.a: Twilight Lord Kelris is the leader of the Twilight's Hammer cell within Blackfathom Deeps. Convinced that the awakening of Aku'mai will grant him eternal life and bring about the reign of the Old Gods, he orchestrates the cult's sacrifices and oversees the desecration of the temple.
faq.q: Who is Twilight Lord Kelris?

faq.a: Both the naga and satyrs were lured to the drowned temple by lingering ancient magical energies. The naga, led by Lady Sarevess, formed a pact with the Twilight's Hammer: the cultists feed her captives and dark knowledge, and in return, her sea witches provide magical shielding against the horrors lurking in the deep.
faq.q: What are the naga and satyr doing in the ruins?

faq.a: The Argent Dawn sent Scout Thaelrid to investigate suspicious alliances between the naga and cultists, uncovering proof of their murderous rituals. Meanwhile, the Earthen Ring rushed to Ashenvale because the invocation of Old Gods threatens the elemental balance and safety of the entire world.
faq.q: Why do the Earthen Ring and Argent Dawn care about this place?

faq.a: Slaying Aku'mai severs the immediate physical foothold of the Old Gods within Ashenvale. It thwarts Twilight Lord Kelris's plot to unleash an ancient, flesh-devouring herald upon Kalimdor, striking a major blow against the Twilight's Hammer cult and cleansing a fragment of the dark taint infecting the ruined moonwell.
al: what happens when you kill aku'mai
faq.q: What happens when Aku'mai is defeated?

text.s: Blackfathom Deeps is a flooded subterranean temple complex situated along the Zoram Strand in northwestern Ashenvale. Once a shrine dedicated to the night elven moon goddess Elune, the sunken sanctuary has been overtaken by the Twilight's Hammer cult, treacherous naga, and satyrs. They gather in its dark waters to venerate and nurture Aku'mai, a primordial pet and herald of the Old Gods.

sec.b: Long before the Great Sundering shattered ancient Kalimdor, this complex was known as Lathar'Lazal, a splendid temple dedicated to Elune. Highborne masons raised gem-encrusted bridges while Queen Azshara commanded the surrounding waters, partitionining salt seas and mountain streams around a sacred moonwell. When the Sundering tore the world apart ten thousand years ago, the temple sank into the coastal depths of the Veiled Sea. For millenia, it sat undisturbed beneath the waves—until foul whispers began seeping upward from the subterranean dark.

Drawn by mad dreams and dark portents, the Twilight's Hammer cult converged on the sunken ruins. Within, they forged an unholy truce with coastal naga led by Lady Sarevess and prowling satyrs. Together, they desecrated the moonwell and enslaved local life. They drove the giant sea turtle Ghamoo-ra mad through years of torment, allowed the brutal murloc Gelihast to erect a blood shrine, and stocked cavernous depths with fresh sacrifices. Under the leadership of Twilight Lord Kelris, the cultists turned the ruins into a staging ground for the Old Gods' impending return.

At the deepest heart of the sunken temple lies Aku'mai, an ancient three-headed hydra carrying a spark of the Old Gods' primordial power. Twilight Lord Kelris believes this devourer is the herald of his dark masters and his personal ticket to immortality. Rather than a wild beast, the cult treats Aku'mai as a cherished divine pet, feeding her subjects and captives to nurture her strength. Striking down Kelris and extinguishing the cult's foul braziers breaks the wards binding her lair, allowing champions to slay the beast before its insatiable hunger is unleashed across Kalimdor.

zone:burningsteppes.s: Las Estepas Ardientes. Las Estepas Ardientes son un páramo volcánico y calcinado que flanquea la base sur de la Montaña Roca Negra. Formado por la catastrófica invocación de Ragnaros hace siglos, este traicionero territorio alberga el principal paso terrestre entre Ventormenta y Khaz Modan. En la actualidad, está plagado de orcos Roca Negra rebeldes, ogros Pirontraña, enanos Hierro Negro y crías del Vuelo Negro. Hace mucho tiempo, estas colinas no eran más que la extensión norte de las Montañas Crestagrana. Durante la Guerra de los Tres Martillos, el clan Hierro Negro exiliado estableció aquí su reino y erigió su capital, Thaurissan. Al verse al borde de la derrota absoluta a manos de los clanes Barbabronce y Martillo Salvaje, el desesperado Thane hechicero Thaurissan intentó conjurar fuerzas elementales. En su lugar, resquebrajó la tierra e invocó a Ragnaros el Señor del Fuego en Azeroth. La violenta explosión pulverizó las montañas circundantes, abrió ríos de lava e hizo brotar el colosal volcán conocido como la Montaña Roca Negra, dejando las estepas carbonizadas y yermas para siempre.

ang.faction:Alliance: The Burning Steppes are a somber, dangerous frontier where Supreme Commander Anduin Lothar fell; Marshal Maxwell at Morgan's Vigil continually seeks brave champions to counter the threats encroaching toward Redridge.
ang.faction:Horde: Thrall's New Horde watches Flame Crest with deep concern, determined to curb the dangerous, unrepentant Blackrock clan whose warmongering stains the honor of orckind.
ang.profession:Mining: The volcanic landscape is rich in rare minerals, making it one of the select open-air regions on Azeroth to harvest valuable Dark Iron deposits alongside veins of rich thorium.
ang.race:Dwarf: Every stone in the steppes bears witness to the Dark Iron clan's folly during the War of the Three Hammers, culminating in the shattering of their capital and the summoning of Ragnaros.

faq.a: Centuries ago, the Dark Iron Sorcerer-Thane Thaurissan attempted to summon an elemental minion to rescue his clan from defeat in the War of the Three Hammers. His spell mistakenly breached the Elemental Plane and summoned Ragnaros the Firelord, ripping open the earth, creating the massive Blackrock volcano, and reducing the northern Redridge Mountains to a charred wasteland.
al: why is blackrock mountain a volcano
faq.q: Why is the ground charred and covered in lava?

faq.a: No. The orcs in the Burning Steppes are remnants of the Blackrock clan who refuse to join Thrall's New Horde. They do not honor the armistice with the Alliance and remain dedicated to the savage, warmongering traditions of the First and Second Wars, serving Blackrock Spire and the black dragonflight.
faq.q: Do the orcs here belong to Thrall's Horde?

faq.a: Anduin Lothar was slain by Warchief Orgrim Doomhammer at the foot of Blackrock Mountain in the Burning Steppes near the end of the Second War. Lothar's demise spurred his second-in-command, Turalyon, and the Alliance forces into a furious counterattack that shattered the Horde's lines.
faq.q: Where did Anduin Lothar die?

faq.a: Alliance soldiers and travelers base themselves at Morgan's Vigil, an elevated outpost in the southeastern foothills of the zone. Marshal Maxwell commands the station, watching over the northern pass and monitoring enemy troop movements around the mountain.
faq.q: Where can the Alliance find shelter in the steppes?

faq.a: Horde adventurers report to Flame Crest, an elevated camp located along the northeastern ridge. From here, emissaries watch the rival Blackrock clan and maintain flight connections back to the Badlands, the Swamp of Sorrows, and Searing Gorge.
faq.q: Where does the Horde stage operations here?

faq.a: The Ruins of Thaurissan are the remnants of the grand city built by the Dark Iron clan after their exile from Ironforge. When Thane Thaurissan summoned Ragnaros, the raw elemental blast destroyed his capital and enslaved his surviving people to the Firelord's will.
al: what is the destroyed dwarf city
faq.q: What are the Ruins of Thaurissan?

text.s: The Burning Steppes are a scorched, volcanic wasteland flanking the southern base of Blackrock Mountain. Formed by the catastrophic summoning of Ragnaros centuries ago, this treacherous territory holds the primary overland passage between Stormwind and Khaz Modan. Today, it crawls with rogue Blackrock orcs, Firegut ogres, Dark Iron dwarves, and broodlings of the black dragonflight.

sec.b: Long ago, these foothills were simply the northern reaches of the Redridge Mountains. During the War of the Three Hammers, the exiled Dark Iron clan established their kingdom here, raising their capital city of Thaurissan. Facing total defeat at the hands of the Bronzebeard and Wildhammer clans, the desperate Sorcerer-Thane Thaurissan attempted to conjure elemental forces. Instead, he shattered the earth and summoned Ragnaros the Firelord into Azeroth. The violent explosion pulverized the surrounding mountains, tore open rivers of lava, and birthed the colossal volcano known as Blackrock Mountain, leaving the steppes forever charred and barren.

During the Second War, the Old Horde claimed Blackrock Spire as its foremost seat of power. At the climax of the conflict, the Grand Alliance of Lordaeron pushed deep into the Burning Steppes to lay siege to the mountain. It was at the foot of Blackrock Mountain that Warchief Orgrim Doomhammer clashed with Lord Anduin Lothar, striking down the human champion. Rather than breaking the Alliance's resolve, Lothar's death galvanized the Allied armies to rout the orcs, sealing the victory of the Second War and leaving behind an enduring valley of ash and rusted steel.

Though Thrall established a New Horde in distant Kalimdor, the Blackrock clan remaining in the steppes maintains the bloodthirsty cruelty of the Old Horde. Operating from Blackrock Stronghold, these orcs openly ally with the black dragonflight and local Firegut ogres rather than honor any truce. Meanwhile, Dark Iron dwarves and elemental servitors lurk among the fiery ruins, all while black drakes and wyrmkin prey upon unwary travelers attempting to use the thoroughfare to cross between Stormwind and the northern kingdoms.
sec.t: A Den of Monsters and Dragons

zone:darkshore.s: Costa Oscura. Costa Oscura es una fría franja costera envuelta en niebla que bordea el noroeste de Kalimdor, salpicada de antiguas ruinas kaldorei y fauna perturbada. Con el pueblo portuario de Auberdine de la Alianza como eje central, sirve como la principal puerta de entrada continental para los viajeros que llegan desde Teldrassil y los Reinos del Este. Más allá del camino patrullado, los cultos demoníacos, los invasores naga y una corrupción que repta desde las tierras altas amenazan el delicado equilibrio de la región. Extendiéndose bajo las sombras occidentales del Monte Hyjal y Frondavil, Costa Oscura se caracteriza por sus pinares, niebla marina y playas rocosas azotadas por olas frías. Hace milenios, esta costa albergó las prósperas ciudades gemelas kaldorei de Ameth'Aran y Bashal'Aran. Destrozadas durante el Gran Cataclismo, sus pilares esqueléticos y arcos de mármol yacen ahora medio sumergidos en el oleaje o cubiertos de raíces, atormentados por inquietos espíritus Altonato e invadidos por múrlocs carroñeros y voraces naga.

ang.class:Druid: Darkshore serves as the front line for Cenarion Circle initiates answering summons from Moonglade to diagnose tainted waterways and brew cleansers for sick forest creatures.
ang.faction:Alliance: Auberdine represents the Alliance's primary trade nexus in northern Kalimdor, maintaining the direct maritime link connecting Stormwind and Ironforge to the night elf capital of Darnassus.
ang.faction:Horde: A remote, heavily patrolled Alliance bastion, Darkshore sits directly north of Horde encampments in Ashenvale, offering a treacherous coastline prowled by hostile sentinels and dangerous cults.
ang.race:NightElf: For young night elves leaving Teldrassil, Darkshore is their first step onto mainland Kalimdor, confronting the painful ruins of their ancient civilization and the spreading corruption of the wild.

faq.a: Alliance players can take a boat directly to Auberdine from either Rut'theran Village at the base of Teldrassil or from Menethil Harbor in the Wetlands. Horde travelers journeying north must walk through Ashenvale, following the main road northeast from Zoram'gar Outpost up across the border.
faq.q: How do I get to Darkshore?

faq.a: Rivers running out of the tainted heights of Felwood, such as the Cliffspring River, wash demonic pollution straight down into Darkshore's water table. Drinking from these foul streams has driven the native furbolg tribes feral and infected the local deer and predators with disease and aggression.
faq.q: What is wrong with the local wildlife and furbolgs?

faq.a: They were prosperous twin Kaldorei cities destroyed ten thousand years ago during the Great Sundering. Their ruler, Athrikus Narassin, claimed he would rescue his people from the cataclysm, but he instead bound their souls into gems to preserve them as eternal power sources for himself, leaving the ruins full of weeping ghosts.
faq.q: What happened to Ameth'Aran and Bashal'Aran?

faq.a: Located in southern Darkshore, the Master's Glaive is a massive petrified skull impaled by an enormous stone weapon. It is an ancient relic associated with the primordial Old Gods and their servitors, and it currently attracts dangerous cultists from the Twilight's Hammer.
faq.q: What is the Master's Glaive?

faq.a: That is Onu, a wise and venerable Ancient of Lore. Resting in his tranquil grove south of Auberdine, he ponders the disturbing encroachment of the Twilight's Hammer cult and assists travelers in investigating disturbances throughout the forest.
faq.q: Who is the giant tree in the Grove of the Ancients?

faq.a: The tower is occupied by the Dark Strand, a vicious cult practicing dark sorcery and summoning demonic entities. Their cabal actively ambushes unwary travelers along the northern reaches of the coastal woods.
faq.q: Who lives in the Tower of Althalaxx?

text.s: Darkshore is a cold, mist-shrouded strip of coast lining northwestern Kalimdor, dotted with ancient Kaldorei ruins and troubled wildlife. Anchored by the Alliance harbor town of Auberdine, it serves as the primary continental gateway for travelers arriving from Teldrassil and the Eastern Kingdoms. Beyond the patrolled road, demonic cults, encroaching naga, and a creeping corruption from the highlands threaten the region's delicate balance.

sec.b: Stretching beneath the western shadows of Mount Hyjal and Felwood, Darkshore is characterized by pine groves, sea fog, and rocky beaches beaten by cold waves. Millennia ago, this coast was home to the flourishing Kaldorei twin cities of Ameth'Aran and Bashal'Aran. Shattered during the Great Sundering, their skeletal pillars and marble arches now lie half-drowned in the surf or overgrown with roots, haunted by restless Highborne spirits and overrun by scavenger murlocs and invasive naga.
sec.t: A Land of Mist and Memory

sec.b: Following the Third War and the planting of Teldrassil, the night elves established Auberdine as a bustling maritime haven amidst the wilderness. Featuring wooden piers that welcome regular vessels from Rut'theran Village and Menethil Harbor in the distant Wetlands, Auberdine is the lifeline linking night elf territory to the rest of the Alliance. Sentinels diligently patrol the trade highway south toward Ashenvale, though their small garrison struggles to police the deep wilds beyond the path.

Despite its shelter against the eastern mountains, Darkshore suffers from a slow, malignant rot. Corrupted run-off trickling down from Felwood poisons sources like Cliffspring Falls, fouling the water table and driving the local bears, stags, and furbolgs of Blackwood Den into violent madness. Worse still, sinister organizations have established footholds in the shadows: the Dark Strand and Twilight's Hammer cultists perform foul rituals at the Tower of Althalaxx and convene around the terrifying, ancient monument known as the Master's Glaive.

faq.a: La suma sacerdotisa Tyrande Susurravientos gobierna Darnassus y a los kaldorei desde el gran Templo de la Luna. El archidruida Fandral Corzocelada lidera a los druidas del Círculo Cenarion desde el Enclave Cenarion, actuando como la autoridad druídica de facto mientras Malfurión Tempestira continúa perdido en El Sueño Esmeralda.

Darnassus fue fundada poco después de la Tercera Guerra. Cuando los elfos de la noche sacrificaron su inmortalidad para derrotar a Archimonde en el Monte Hyjal, Fandral Corzocelada impulsó el crecimiento del nuevo Árbol del Mundo, Teldrassil, para recuperar su antiguo estado. Darnassus fue esculpida en sus ramas como su nuevo refugio.

Malfurión Tempestira está desaparecido, con su espíritu atrapado dentro del Sueño Esmeralda. En su ausencia, el archidruida Fandral Corzocelada gobierna a los druidas de Teldrassil, mientras que Tyrande Susurravientos busca continuamente una manera de despertar y recuperar a su amado compañero.

La ciudad está dividida en bancales especializados. El Bancal del Artesano alberga disciplinas de recolección y sastrería junto con una posada, mientras que el Bancal de los Mercaderes cuenta con puestos comerciales y la Casa de Subastas. Los instructores de herrería y marciales residen en el Bancal del Guerrero, y el banco de la ciudad se encuentra en la isla central de Los Jardines del Templo.

Tras la devastación de la Tercera Guerra, los elfos de la noche se enfrentaron a la creciente presión de la Horda, en particular a las expediciones de tala orcas en Vallefresno. Al reconocer la necesidad de aliados frente a estas incursiones y otras amenazas emergentes por todo Kalimdor, Darnassus estableció lazos diplomáticos y se unió a la Gran Alianza.

zone:darnassus.s: Darnassus. Darnassus es la serena capital al aire libre de los elfos de la noche, erigida entre las ramas del recién plantado Árbol del Mundo, Teldrassil. Gobernada por la suma sacerdotisa Tyrande Susurravientos junto a los druidas del Enclave Cenarion, sirve como un apacible santuario para un pueblo ancestral que se adapta a la mortalidad. Extendida por amplios bancales que rodean un lago cristalino, se alza como el corazón de la sociedad de los elfos de la noche y su puente hacia la Alianza. A diferencia de la densa mampostería de Ventormenta o los túneles de piedra tallada de Forjaz, Darnassus es amplia, tranquila y está íntimamente abierta a la naturaleza salvaje. En el dosel superior de Teldrassil, frente a la costa norte de Kalimdor, las elegantes estructuras de madera y los sinuosos senderos de la capital rodean un apacible lago central. Elegantes puentes conectan bancales dedicados a mercaderes, artesanos, centinelas y druidas, creando una atmósfera que equilibra el gobierno civil con una profunda reverencia por la naturaleza.

ang.class:Druid: The Cenarion Enclave serves as the nexus of druidic training in Teldrassil, overseen by the demanding and uncompromising Archdruid Fandral Staghelm.
ang.class:Priest: The grand Temple of the Moon is the holy center of the Sisters of Elune, presided over by High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind herself.
ang.faction:Alliance: Darnassus acts as the westernmost stronghold of the Alliance, providing critical naval and strategic shelter on the continent of Kalimdor.
ang.race:NightElf: As the heart of your sovereign civilization, Darnassus is your sanctuary as you navigate the unprecedented trials of mortal existence.

faq.a: Because Teldrassil is an island isolated off Kalimdor's northwest coast, travelers must reach Rut'theran Village at the foot of the tree by boat or flight. From the village docks, a glowing magical portal takes travelers directly up into the city boughs.
faq.q: How do you travel to Darnassus from the mainland?

faq.a: High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind rules Darnassus and the kaldorei from the grand Temple of the Moon. Archdruid Fandral Staghelm leads the druids of the Cenarion Circle from the Cenarion Enclave, acting as the de facto druidic authority while Malfurion Stormrage remains lost in the Emerald Dream.
faq.q: Who rules Darnassus?

faq.a: Darnassus was founded shortly after the Third War. When the night elves sacrificed their immortality to defeat Archimonde at Mount Hyjal, Fandral Staghelm pushed to grow the new World Tree, Teldrassil, to reclaim their former state. Darnassus was carved into the boughs as their new refuge.
faq.q: Why was the city founded so recently?

faq.a: Malfurion Stormrage is missing, his spirit trapped within the Emerald Dream. In his absence, Archdruid Fandral Staghelm governs the druids of Teldrassil, while Tyrande Whisperwind continually seeks a way to awaken and recover her beloved mate.
faq.q: Where is Archdruid Malfurion Stormrage?

faq.a: The city is divided into specialized terraces. The Craftsmen's Terrace hosts gathering and tailoring disciplines along with an inn, while the Tradesmen's Terrace houses trade stalls and the Auction House. Blacksmithing and martial trainers reside on the Warrior's Terrace, and the city bank rests upon the central island of the Temple Gardens.
faq.q: Where are the profession trainers and shops located?

faq.a: After the devastation of the Third War, the night elves faced mounting pressure from the Horde, particularly orcish logging expeditions into Ashenvale. Recognizing the need for allies against these incursions and other rising threats across Kalimdor, Darnassus opened diplomatic ties and joined the Grand Alliance.
faq.q: Why did the night elves join the Alliance?

text.s: Darnassus is the serene, open-air capital city of the night elves, built amidst the branches of the newly planted World Tree, Teldrassil. Governed by High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind alongside the druids of the Cenarion Enclave, it serves as a tranquil sanctuary for an ancient people adapting to mortality. Sheltered across vast terraces surrounding a crystalline lake, it stands as the heart of night elf society and their bridge to the Alliance.

sec.b: Unlike the dense masonry of Stormwind or the carved stone tunnels of Ironforge, Darnassus is broad, quiet, and intimately open to the wilderness. Formed upon the upper canopy of Teldrassil off northern Kalimdor's coast, the capital's graceful wooden structures and winding pathways encircle a tranquil central lake. Elegant bridges connect terraces dedicated to tradesmen, craftsmen, sentinels, and druids, creating an atmosphere that balances civic governance with profound reverence for nature.
sec.t: A Crown High in the Branches

sec.b: Darnassus is remarkably young for a civilization thousands of years old. Following the Third War and the sacrifice of Nordrassil at Mount Hyjal, the kaldorei suddenly faced the perils of aging and sickness. Seeking a renewal of their lost vitality, Archdruid Fandral Staghelm and his followers planted Teldrassil in defiance of missing Archdruid Malfurion Stormrage's warnings. Darnassus was founded among its immense boughs as an asylum and monument to their survival, though shadows of malaise already whisper among its roots.

Though peaceful on its surface, Darnassus balances on a delicate political divide. From the towering colonnades of the Temple of the Moon, High Priestess Tyrande Whisperwind guides the spiritual life and military defense of her people through the vigilant Sentinels. Across the waterways in the Cenarion Enclave, Archdruid Fandral Staghelm commands the druids in Malfurion's continuing absence. While both leaders present a united front to their newfound Alliance partners, friction between the priestesses and the druidic circle lingers throughout the city.

zone:deadmines.s: Las Minas de la Muerte. En las profundidades del polvoriento pueblo agrícola de Arroyo de la Luna se encuentran Las Minas de la Muerte, un enorme complejo subterráneo que antaño suministraba un tercio de las reservas de oro de Ventormenta. Abandonados durante la Primera Guerra y considerados embrujados durante mucho tiempo, estos laberínticos túneles han sido tomados en secreto por la Hermandad Defias como su base de operaciones definitiva. Aquí, Edwin VanCleef y sus ingenieros goblins reclutados a la fuerza trabajan lejos de los ojos del reino para construir una máquina de venganza contra la corona. Antes de la Primera Guerra, Las Minas de la Muerte eran celebradas como el mayor centro productor de oro de las tierras humanas, financiando la prosperidad de Ventormenta. Cuando la Horda orca arrasó el reino y redujo a cenizas la capital, las minas fueron apresuradamente abandonadas a la oscuridad. Durante aquellos años turbulentos, figuras legendarias recorrieron estas profundidades: Sir Anduin Lothar fue encarcelado por ogros subterráneos durante veinte meses mientras recuperaba el sagrado Libro de la Divinidad, y la rebelde hija del Jefe de Guerra Puño Negro, Griselda, huyó a los pasadizos inferiores junto al ogro Turok antes de que ambos encontraran su final. Consideradas malditas y pobladas únicamente por no-muertos errantes y alimañas subterráneas al acecho, las profundidades permanecieron intactas durante décadas.

ang.class:Paladin: These desecrated shafts are a test of valor and faith, echoing the historic trials of Sir Anduin Lothar and the lost miners whose restless dead still wander the outer tunnels.
ang.faction:Alliance: The Deadmines represent the gravest internal threat to the kingdom of Stormwind; bringing down VanCleef is the defining victory that restores hope to the besieged farmers of Westfall.
ang.profession:Engineering: The Goblin Foundry and Sneed's mechanical workshop offer an inside look at cutting-edge steam shredders, remote-controlled golems, and specialized ordnance.
ang.profession:Mining: Once supplying a third of the capital's wealth, the rocky tunnels remain rich in veins of copper, tin, and precious silver.

faq.a: The entrance is hidden inside a derelict barn in the ruined town of Moonbrook, located in southwestern Westfall. Winding tunnels pass through an outer complex of Defias diggers and undead miners before reaching the locked instance threshold.
faq.q: Where is the entrance to the Deadmines located?

faq.a: Adventurers frequently refer to the dungeon as 'VC' after its master, Edwin VanCleef. This shorthand is used to avoid confusing the Deadmines with Dire Maul, an ancient elven complex in Feralas that shares the initials 'DM'.
faq.q: Why does everyone call the Deadmines 'VC'?

faq.a: Edwin VanCleef was the brilliant guildmaster of the Stonemasons who oversaw the majestic reconstruction of Stormwind City after the First War. When the House of Nobles refused to honor their debts, VanCleef formed the Defias Brotherhood to exact restitution through rebellion and open brigandage.
faq.q: Who is Edwin VanCleef?

faq.a: The Defias have contracted goblin engineers to assemble a massive ironclad juggernaught. Armed with heavy ordnance and sturdy timber, the warship is designed to sail out of the cove's sea gate and raid the trade that feeds the capital.
faq.q: What is being built in Ironclad Cove?

faq.a: Foreman Thistlenettle and his crew were sent to legally reopen the mines for the kingdom. When the Defias stormed the works, a devastating tunnel collapse trapped the miners in the dark, where they starved and eventually rose as mindless, restless undead.
faq.q: What happened to the Miners' League workers outside the instance?

faq.a: Cookie serves as the bizarre ship's cook aboard VanCleef's dreadnaught. While defeating VanCleef cuts off the head of the rebellion, slaying Cookie cleans out the remaining crew lingering in the ship's galley, utterly breaking the crew's presence in Ironclad Cove before adventurers escape out the coastal passage.
faq.q: What does defeating Cookie the murloc mean for the Defias ship?

faq.a: Following the natural tunnel out behind the dreadnaught brings adventurers to an exit along the coastal bluffs of the Dagger Hills, looking out toward the ocean and the Westfall Lighthouse.
faq.q: Where does the exit tunnel lead when leaving the dungeon?

text.s: Deep beneath the dusty farm town of Moonbrook lies the Deadmines, an enormous subterranean complex that once supplied a third of Stormwind's gold reserves. Abandoned during the First War and long considered haunted, these labyrinthine tunnels have secretly been overtaken by the Defias Brotherhood as their ultimate staging ground. Here, Edwin VanCleef and his conscripted goblin engineers labor away from the eyes of the realm to build an engine of vengeance against the kingdom.

sec.b: Before the First War, the Deadmines were celebrated as the greatest gold-producing center in human lands, financing the prosperity of Stormwind. When the Orcish Horde swept through the kingdom and razed the capital, the mines were hastily abandoned to the dark. During those turbulent years, legendary figures walked these depths: Sir Anduin Lothar was imprisoned by subterranean ogres for twenty months while recovering the sacred Tome of Divinity, and Warchief Blackhand's rebellious daughter Griselda fled into the lower passages alongside the ogre Turok before both met their ends. Believed to be cursed and populated only by shambling undead and lurking subterranean vermin, the depths lay untouched for decades.
sec.t: A Legacy of Gold and Ruin

sec.b: When the Stonemasons' Guild was cast out of Stormwind without payment for rebuilding the city, Edwin VanCleef reorganized the disenfranchised artisans into the Defias Brotherhood. Seeking a secure headquarters safe from Gryan Stoutmantle's People's Militia, the thieves established their central redoubt within the abandoned tunnels. They drove out the legitimate Miners' League—leaving Foreman Thistlenettle's doomed workers to perish and rise as undead ghouls—and converted the shafts into an industrial war camp. Guarded by lumbering ogres, seasoned brigands, and mechanical constructs, the lower mines echo once again with picks, fires, and illicit industry.

Beyond the sweltering Goblin Foundry and the timber-strewn Mast Room lies Ironclad Cove, a vast subterranean grotto hollowed out beneath the Dagger Hills. In this hidden harbor, VanCleef has employed goblin shipbuilders and tinkerers to construct a colossal ironclad dreadnaught. Commanded by Captain Greenskin and First Mate Mr. Smite, this warship is engineered to sail through an underwater sea gate leading out toward the ocean, where the Defias Brotherhood means to prey on the sea trade that keeps Stormwind rich.

zone:desolace.s: Desolace. Desolace es un desierto inhóspito y azotado por el viento en la costa occidental de Kalimdor, caracterizado por una tierra gris agrietada, cielos tormentosos constantes y los huesos de bestias caídas. Es la cuna ancestral de la despiadada raza centauro y un páramo disputado, marcado por antiguas ruinas de los Altonato, cultos demoníacos invasores y una cruenta guerra tribal. Tanto la Horda como la Alianza mantienen precarios asentamientos entre el polvo, buscando afianzar su influencia mientras frenan la corrupción que se expande. Desolace no siempre fue una árida extensión de ceniza y charcas amarillentas. Hace más de un milenio, era Mashan'she, una pradera exuberante cuidada por chamanes tauren. Ese paraíso se desmoronó cuando la elemental de tierra Princesa Theradras despertó bajo el suelo, absorbiendo la fuerza vital circundante para regenerar su forma. La calamidad atrajo a Zaetar, hijo de Cenarius, pero en lugar de someterla, tomó a la princesa como compañera. De su antinatural unión surgieron los primeros centauros. Llenos de vergüenza e ira sanguinarias, los recién nacidos asesinaron a su padre, arrasaron las verdes llanuras y expulsaron a los tauren, dejando tras de sí el desolado páramo que se conoce hoy en día.

ang.class:Druid: Cenarion Circle druids view Desolace as a horrifying scar upon the natural order, where Zaetar met his tragic demise and elemental decay chokes the earth.
ang.class:Warlock: The arid plains and demonic sites like Mannoroc Coven draw dark practitioners seeking the secrets of felsteeds, majestic wild horses twisted into fire-breathing horrors through forbidden Shadow Council rites.
ang.faction:Alliance: Operating out of Nijel's Point, the Alliance monitors both the treacherous centaur tribes and the suspicious spread of Horde settlements like Shadowprey Village alongside demonic cults.
ang.faction:Horde: The Horde strives to secure the coastline at Shadowprey Village and protect the kodo herds at Ghost Walker Post, while fighting relentlessly to crush the Burning Blade and prove the modern Horde is free of demonic influence.
ang.race:Tauren: For the tauren, Desolace is sacred and tragic ground. Once known as Mashan'she, it was the nomadic home of your ancestors before the awakening of Theradras and the scourge of the centaur drove your people onto the brink of extinction.

faq.a: Centuries ago, the land was a fertile meadow called Mashan'she. Tauren shaman accidentally roused the slumbering earth elemental Princess Theradras, who consumed the vitality of the region to rebuild her physical form. The birth and violent expansion of the centaur shortly after destroyed whatever plant life survived, leaving only gray dust and ash.
faq.q: Why is Desolace such a dead wasteland?

faq.a: The centaur are the offspring of Zaetar, son of the demigod Cenarius, and the elemental Princess Theradras. Disgusted and enraged by their own twisted appearance, the first khans slew their father immediately after birth and multiplied across the plains in a frenzy of brutality.
faq.q: Where did the centaur come from?

faq.a: Yes. Adventurers can earn reputation with either the Gelkis or the Magram tribe by slaying members of their rival clan. Gaining enough standing with one unlocks access to their village, tribal quests, and peace within their territory, though it makes the opposing tribe permanently hostile.
faq.q: Can I ally with the centaur tribes here?

faq.a: Maraudon is the sacred ancestral burial ground of the centaur race, hidden deep within the twisting western cliffs of Desolace. It serves as both the tomb of Zaetar and the subterranean lair of Princess Theradras, who continues to channel dark elemental corruption through its cavernous halls.
faq.q: What is Maraudon?

faq.a: That is Rexxar, the Champion of the Horde, accompanied by his loyal bear companion Misha. The Mok'Nathal wanderer patrols the dusty highways of Desolace and the Stonetalon Mountains, keeping a watchful eye on the wilderness and assisting those on vital Horde business.
al: who is the orc with a bear
faq.q: Who is the wanderer roaming Desolace with a bear?

faq.a: The Burning Blade cult has taken over strongholds like Thunder Axe Fortress to summon demons and bind felsteeds. The demons and satyrs it calls up threaten a region-wide demonic infestation, a danger both the Horde and the Alliance must answer.
faq.q: Why are the Alliance and Horde fighting the Burning Blade here?

text.s: Desolace is a bleak, windswept desert on Kalimdor's western coast, defined by cracked gray earth, constant stormy skies, and the bones of fallen beasts. It is the ancestral cradle of the vicious centaur race and a contested wasteland scarred by ancient Highborne ruins, encroaching demonic cults, and bitter tribal warfare. Both the Horde and Alliance maintain precarious footholds amidst the dust, each seeking to carve out influence while warding off spreading corruption.

sec.b: Desolace was not always a barren expanse of ash and yellowed pools. Over a millennium ago, it was Mashan'she—a lush meadowland tended by tauren shaman. That paradise unraveled when the earth elemental Princess Theradras awakened from beneath the soil, draining the surrounding life force to regenerate her form. The calamity summoned Zaetar, son of Cenarius, but rather than subduing her, he took the princess as his mate. From their unnatural union sprang the first centaur. In shame and bloodthirsty wrath, the newborn race murdered their father, overran the verdant plains, and drove the tauren away, leaving behind the scarred wasteland known today.

The interior of Desolace echoes with the thunder of thousands of hooves as four splintered centaur tribes wage endless war against all interlopers and each other. The Kolkar roam the eastern cliffs, the Magram hold crude yurts around brackish sinkholes, the Gelkis dwell behind rope bridges in deep southern ravines, and the fanatical Maraudine defend the approach to Maraudon itself. Travelers venturing across the wastes frequently find themselves drawn into this ancient blood feud, forced to slaughter one tribe to gain safe passage and tenuous parley with another.

Beyond the warring centaur, darker perils fester along the borders. The Burning Blade cult operates freely out of Thunder Axe Fortress and Shadowbreak Ravine, summoning demons and satyrs that threaten to drown the region in fel fire. Along the stormy shoreline, naga creep onto the beaches of Ethel Rethor, while Darkspear trolls spear fish from the stilted platforms of Shadowprey Village. Tucked high in the northern crags, the Alliance watches from Nijel's Point, suspicious of the Horde's expansion and ever wary of the demonic taint spreading from Mannoroc Coven.

faq.a: Tanto los enanos como los gnomos inician aquí sus viajes, en el Valle de Crestanevada, una cuenca resguardada en el suroeste de Dun Morogh, antes de aventurarse a través del Desfiladero de Crestanevada hacia Kharanos y el resto de la zona.

Durante la Tercera Guerra, una raza subterránea conocida como troggs invadió Gnomeregan en tropel. En un intento por purgar a los invasores, el Manitas Mayor Gelbin Mekkatorque liberó gas radiactivo en los niveles inferiores. El plan fracasó de forma catastrófica, matando a miles y convirtiendo a muchos gnomos en gnomos parias desquiciados debido a la radiación, lo que obligó a los supervivientes sanos a huir a Forjaz.

Dun Morogh está amurallado por altas crestas montañosas. Para viajar a pie hacia el este, rumbo a Loch Modan, toma los caminos que conducen al Paso de la Puerta Norte o al Paso de la Puerta Sur en las montañas del noreste. También puedes viajar directamente a Ciudad de Ventormenta a través del Tren subterráneo que hay dentro de Forjaz.

El único maestro de vuelo de la Alianza operativo en la zona se encuentra dentro de la Gran Fundición, en Forjaz, y conecta a los viajeros con emplazamientos de Khaz Modan, Ventormenta y los puestos avanzados del norte de la Alianza.

Los Peloescarcha son una tribu de trolls de hielo que gobernó Dun Morogh mucho antes de que los enanos emergieran de Uldaman. Aunque fueron derrotados y arrojados a los riscos hace generaciones, siguen siendo acérrimos enemigos de Forjaz y asaltan con frecuencia granjas y caminos enanos desde refugios como el Poblado Peloescarcha.

Kharanos es el asentamiento enano principal del centro de Dun Morogh. Alberga la Destilería Cebatruenos, instructores y suministros, y sirve como centro de operaciones principal para los jóvenes aventureros y montañeros que lidian con los problemas locales de trolls y fauna salvaje.

zone:dunmorogh.s: Dun Morogh. Dun Morogh es una meseta montañosa azotada por la nieve y situada en el corazón de Khaz Modan. Sirve como punto de partida ancestral y hogar compartido para los enanos de Forjaz y los gnomos desplazados de Gnomeregan. Aunque está protegido por imponentes picos y pasos fortificados, este reino nevado se enfrenta a crecientes amenazas internas procedentes de los troggs, los trolls Peloescarcha y los gnomos parias irradiados. Dun Morogh ocupa los picos más altos de los Reinos del Este, una extensión alpina rodeada de cumbres escarpadas que la protegen de La Garganta de Fuego al sur y de Los Humedales al norte. Estas montañas nevadas alimentan los ríos que fluyen a través de Khaz Modan y proporcionan vetas prácticamente ilimitadas de cobre y hierro. El acceso está sumamente restringido a túneles de montaña como el Paso de la Puerta Norte y el Paso de la Puerta Sur, vigilados de cerca por los montañeros enanos. En el corazón de la región se asienta Forjaz, una antigua maravilla subterránea y capital del reino del Rey Magni Barbabronce, comunicada directamente con Ventormenta mediante la maravilla del Tren subterráneo.

ang.profession:Cooking: Local hunters and innkeepers in Kharanos and Brewnall Village make hearty use of boar meat, bear ribs, and dwarven stout to ward off the biting mountain frost.
ang.profession:Mining: The mountain crags of Dun Morogh are rich with surface deposits of Copper Veins, particularly around the quarry at Gol'Bolar and along the snowy rock faces.
ang.race:Dwarf: This is your ancestral homeland. From the hearthfires of Anvilmar to the blazing core of the Great Forge in Ironforge, defending these peaks from trolls and troggs is your duty to King Magni.
ang.race:Gnome: Your lost home, Gnomeregan, lies irradiated in the western valley. Dun Morogh serves as your base in exile alongside your dwarven cousins while you fight back against troggs and rogue leper gnomes.

faq.a: Both dwarves and gnomes begin their journeys here in Coldridge Valley, a sheltered basin in southwestern Dun Morogh, before venturing out through Coldridge Pass into Kharanos and the wider zone.
faq.q: What races start in Dun Morogh?

faq.a: During the Third War, a subterranean race called troggs swarmed Gnomeregan. In an attempt to purge the invaders, High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque released radioactive gas into the lower levels. The plan failed catastrophically, killing thousands and irradiating many gnomes into crazed leper gnomes, forcing the healthy survivors to flee to Ironforge.
faq.q: What happened to Gnomeregan?

faq.a: Dun Morogh is walled in by high mountain ridges. To travel eastward into Loch Modan on foot, take the roads leading to North Gate Pass or South Gate Pass in the northeastern mountains. You can also travel directly to Stormwind City via the Deeprun Tram inside Ironforge.
faq.q: How do you leave Dun Morogh on foot?

faq.a: The only functional Alliance flight master in the zone is located inside the Great Forge of Ironforge, connecting travelers to locations across Khaz Modan, Stormwind, and the northern Alliance outposts.
faq.q: Where is the flight master in Dun Morogh?

faq.a: The Frostmane are a tribe of ice trolls who ruled Dun Morogh long before the dwarves emerged from Uldaman. Though defeated and driven into the crags generations ago, they remain bitter enemies of Ironforge, routinely raiding dwarven farms and roads from retreats like Frostmane Hold.
al: why are there trolls in dun morogh
faq.q: Who are the Frostmane trolls?

faq.a: Kharanos is the primary dwarven settlement in central Dun Morogh. It houses the Thunderbrew Distillery, trainers, and supplies, serving as the central operational hub for young adventurers and Mountaineers tackling local troll and wildlife problems.
faq.q: What is Kharanos?

text.s: Dun Morogh is a snow-swept mountain highland situated at the heart of Khaz Modan. It serves as the ancestral starting ground and shared homeland for the dwarves of Ironforge and the displaced gnomes of Gnomeregan. Though guarded by towering peaks and fortified passes, the snowy realm faces rising internal threats from troggs, Frostmane trolls, and irradiated leper gnomes.

sec.b: Dun Morogh occupies the highest peaks in the Eastern Kingdoms, an alpine expanse ringed by jagged summits that shield it from Searing Gorge to the south and the Wetlands to the north. These snowy mountains feed the rivers flowing across Khaz Modan and provide near-limitless veins of copper and iron. Access is heavily restricted to mountain tunnels like North Gate Pass and South Gate Pass, watched closely by dwarven Mountaineers. At the heart of the region sits Ironforge, an ancient subterranean wonder and the capital of King Magni Bronzebeard's realm, linked straight to Stormwind by the marvel of the Deeprun Tram.

Centuries ago, the dwarves drove the native Frostmane ice trolls into the crags, carving out room for themselves alongside their brilliant gnome allies. The two races flourished in neighboring mountain halls until the recent catastrophe in Gnomeregan during the Third War. A horrific trogg invasion and a catastrophic radioactive venting ruined the technological wonder, turning its defenders into mindless leper gnomes and driving High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque and his surviving folk into exile. Now, the gnomes dwell as guests inside Ironforge, while leper gnomes and surviving troggs spill out into Chill Breeze Valley.

Life in the drifts is far from quiet. The Frostmane tribe has grown emboldened, establishing heavily armed encampments from Shimmer Ridge down to Coldridge Valley. Meanwhile, primitive troggs have clawed their way out of ancient subterranean fissures into Gol'Bolar Quarry, threatening the region's mining operations. Between prowling wendigos, wild boars, infiltrating Dark Iron dwarven agents, and toxic fallout spreading from the ruins of Gnomeregan, the dwarven Mountaineers are stretched thin maintaining order from Kharanos to the border gates.

zone:duskwood.s: Bosque del Ocaso. Antaño una extensión soleada del sur de Elwynn conocida como Brightwood, el Bosque del Ocaso es ahora una floresta maldita atrapada bajo una penumbra antinatural y perpetua. Abandonados por las autoridades de Ventormenta, sus asediados habitantes humanos luchan por sobrevivir en Villa Oscura bajo la atenta protección de la milicia local, la Guardia Nocturna. Por sus oscuras arboledas y túmulos embrujados merodean necrófagos carnívoros, arañas venenosas gigantescas, ogros saqueadores y salvajes y misteriosos huargen. Antes de que descendiera la oscuridad, esta provincia se conocía como Brightwood, una rica franja agrícola del Reino de Ventormenta que contaba con asentamientos prósperos como Grand Hamlet y Cerro del Cuervo. La tragedia de la región comenzó cuando el Guardián Medivh cayó en Karazhan durante la Primera Guerra, desatando oleadas de magia vil corrompida que retorcieron la serena floresta hasta convertirla en un lodazal nudoso y sombrío. Las arañas mutaron en aterradoras bestias depredadoras, mientras que los lobos que huían se extendieron al norte hacia el Bosque de Elwynn. Con el tiempo, Grand Hamlet pasó a llamarse Villa Oscura, y sus aterrorizados habitantes quedaron prácticamente abandonados a su suerte mientras la guarnición real se replegaba para defender la capital.

ang.class:Druid: The Twilight Grove cradles an ancient Great Tree with deep ties to the Emerald Dream, making Duskwood a focal point for druids investigating the world's slumbering magic.
ang.class:Paladin: The desecrated barrows of Raven Hill and the sinister necromancy of Morbent Fel make Duskwood an urgent testing ground for holy crusaders wielding the Light.
ang.faction:Alliance: Though technically an Alliance holding, Duskwood receives zero official troop support from Stormwind, relying purely on heroic adventurers and the Night Watch to stave off annihilation.
ang.profession:Herbalism: The haunted barrows and cursed soil yield rare flora like Grave Moss and Kingsblood, drawing gatherers willing to braving restless undead in the cemeteries.

faq.a: The land was once Brightwood, a vibrant southern province of Elwynn. When the Guardian Medivh was slain in nearby Karazhan during the First War, volatile fel energies washed over the forest, choking out the sunlight, twisting the flora, and giving rise to the name Duskwood.
faq.q: Why is it called Duskwood instead of Brightwood?

faq.a: The night elf Velinde Starsong brought the mystical Scythe of Elune into the region and perished near Roland's Doom. Years later, a frightened worker named Jitters disturbed the scythe in the mine, unwittingly opening tears that summoned the savage wolf-men into the forest.
faq.q: Where did the worgen come from?

faq.a: Raven Hill Cemetery served as the resting place for countless souls lost to famine, beasts, and war. The vile necromancer Morbent Fel established his lair on Forlorn Rowe, using dark sorcery to animate the graves into ghouls, skeletons, and abominations.
faq.q: Why are there so many undead in Raven Hill?

faq.a: With King Varian Wrynn missing and resources stretched thin, Stormwind's regency has pulled its military back to protect Elwynn and the throne. Darkshire is left entirely to its own devices, defended solely by the volunteer militia known as the Night Watch.
faq.q: Why hasn't Stormwind sent soldiers to help Darkshire?

faq.a: The Dark Riders are mysterious hooded horsemen originating from Deadwind Pass near Karazhan. Drawn by the release of the Scythe of Elune, they swept into Duskwood, ruthlessly slaughtering Sven Yorgen's family while hunting for the artifact.
faq.q: Who are the Dark Riders stalking the woods?

faq.a: The crater is the Twilight Grove, home to a Great Tree grown thousands of years ago from a branch of Nordrassil planted by Fandral Staghelm. It contains a portal to the Emerald Dream and maintains a calm, mystical twilight distinct from the cursed dark of the forest.
faq.q: What is the massive tree in the center crater?

text.s: Once a sunlit expanse of southern Elwynn known as Brightwood, Duskwood is now a cursed woodland trapped beneath an unnatural, perpetual gloom. Abandoned by the authorities in Stormwind, its besieged human inhabitants cling to survival in Darkshire under the watchful protection of the local Night Watch militia. Across its darkened groves and haunted barrows roam flesh-eating ghouls, gigantic venomous spiders, raiding ogres, and savage, mysterious worgen.

sec.b: Before the darkness descended, this province was known as Brightwood, a rich agricultural tract of the Kingdom of Stormwind boasting prosperous settlements like Grand Hamlet and Raven Hill. The region's tragedy began when Guardian Medivh fell at Karazhan during the First War, unleashing waves of corrupted fel magic that twisted the serene woodland into a gnarled, shadowy morass. Spiders mutated into terrifying predatory beasts, while fleeing wolves spilled north into Elwynn Forest. Over time, Grand Hamlet was rechristened Darkshire, its terrified townsfolk left largely to fend for themselves as the realm's royal garrison withdrew to defend the capital.

The land's modern nightmare deepened with the arrival of a night elf priestess named Velinde Starsong, who carried an otherworldly artifact known as the Scythe of Elune. When she vanished within the disused mine called Roland's Doom, the relic was eventually unearthed by a prospecting laborer named Jitters. The careless handling of the weapon unleashed ravenous, bipedal wolf-beasts known as worgen into the woods. Clad in perpetual mist and bloodlust, these extradimensional predators tore through the western groves, compounding the miseries of a region already groaning under undead curses.

Today, Darkshire survives only through the vigilance of Commander Althea Ebonlocke and her volunteer militia, the Night Watch, while Lord Ello Ebonlocke attempts to govern the crumbling settlement. Beyond the town's lantern-lit perimeter lies utter peril: the massive Raven Hill Cemetery churns with restless dead raised by the necromancer Morbent Fel, the Vul'Gol ogres have migrated from Deadwind Pass to claim the south, and sinister Dark Riders stalk the crossroads in relentless search of the lost Scythe.

Near the center of Duskwood lies a deep, ancient crater that defies the surrounding corruption: the Twilight Grove. Long before human kingdoms walked these lands, the archdruid Fandral Staghelm planted a bough from Nordrassil here to contain foul saronite growths. The branch blossomed into a Great Tree hosting a dormant portal into the Emerald Dream. Bathed in a soft, ethereal twilight, the grove remains an unearthly sanctuary in an otherwise dying land, watched over by sleeping druidic energies.

zone:dustwallow.s: Marjal Revolcafango. Marjal Revolcafango es un vasto y sofocante pantano en el centro de Kalimdor, atrapado entre las áridas llanuras de Los Baldíos y el Mare Magnum. Alimentadas por perpetuos manantiales subterráneos, sus traicioneras ciénagas albergan peligrosos depredadores, escaramuzas encubiertas entre facciones y la acechante presencia del Vuelo Negro. Sirve de hogar a la isla-fortaleza de la Alianza de Theramore en el este y a los ogros Quebrantarrocas del Poblado Murohelecho, aliados de la Horda, al noroeste.
