faq.a: Slaying Bazzalan and Jergosh breaks the active leadership of the Searing Blade cultists lurking under Orgrimmar. Their deaths demonstrate the Horde's resilience and allow Thrall to thwart a demon-worshiping cell right beneath his throne.
faq.q: What does killing Bazzalan and Jergosh accomplish for the story?

faq.a: Physically, any adventurer can walk through the portal, but reaching the Cleft of Shadow deep inside Orgrimmar as an Alliance member requires evading high-level Horde guards and hostile defenders throughout the city.
faq.q: Can Alliance adventurers enter Ragefire Chasm?

faq.a: Thrall tolerates the practitioners of dark magic who gather in the Cleft of Shadow, preferring to keep them close and under his watchful eye rather than drive them out of sight.
faq.q: Why doesn't Thrall simply execute Neeru Fireblade?

text.s: Ragefire Chasm is a network of winding volcanic tunnels situated directly beneath the orcish capital of Orgrimmar. Entered through the dark hollows of the Cleft of Shadow, the chasm is overrun by savage troggs and a demonic sect of cultists known as the Searing Blade. Left unchecked, the dark powers and subterranean swarms festering below threaten the very foundation of the young Horde nation.

sec.b: Beneath the dust and red rocks of Orgrimmar lies a blistering maze of volcanic corridors and lava pits. While orcish builders forged their new home above, aggressive Ragefire troggs began erupting from deep below the surface. Magatha Grimtotem sought to open diplomatic channels with the brutes on behalf of Thunder Bluff, but her envoy Maur Grimtotem was slaughtered, proving the troggs will yield only to force.

Far more dangerous than simple troggs is the presence of the Searing Blade, a fanatical cell loyal to the Shadow Council. Operating from the dark caverns alongside the magma streams, this demonic cult plots the utter ruin of the fledgling Horde. They are led by the warlock Jergosh the Invoker, a cunning satyr named Bazzalan, and the vicious felguard Taragaman the Hungerer, who presides over an altar in the lava lake.

Neeru Fireblade, an ostensible warlock trainer dwelling beside the chasm's entrance in the Cleft of Shadow, secretly serves as the local leader of the Burning Blade. Neeru sends Horde adventurers into the depths under the guise of loyalty tests, hoping to cull weak cultists and eliminate Thrall's supporters. However, Thrall is fully aware of Neeru's deception. The Warchief uses these forays to eliminate dangerous cult leaders like Jergosh and Bazzalan while letting Neeru remain in place to monitor the Shadow Council's broader schemes.

zone:razorfenkraul.s: Horado Rajacieno. Escondido en el extremo sur de Los Baldíos, Horado Rajacieno es el corazón ancestral de los jabaespines de Kalimdor. Estas feroces tribus veneran el denso laberinto de zarzas gigantes como el sagrado lugar de descanso de su progenitor, el semidiós caído Agamaggan. En la actualidad, el Horado se ha vuelto agresivamente hostil bajo la tiranía de la matriarca jabaespín Charlga Filonavaja, cuyos oscuros tratos amenazan a toda la región. Hace diez mil años, durante la apocalíptica Guerra de los Ancestros, el colosal dios salvaje Agamaggan se lanzó a la lucha contra la Legión Ardiente. El gran jabalí acabó muriendo en combate, pero su sacrificio preservó la vida en Azeroth. Cuenta la leyenda que allí donde su sangre se filtró en la tierra brotaron enormes enredaderas cubiertas de espinas, formando densos laberintos defensivos por las llanuras del sur. Los jabaespines, que veneraban a Agamaggan como su antepasado divino, reclamaron estas colosales espesuras como sus tierras sagradas y convirtieron la mayor de ellas en Rajacieno.

ang.class:Shaman: Quilboar geomancy twists the earth and elements around the blood of Agamaggan, providing a stark look at primal shamanistic powers wielded with savage intent.
ang.faction:Horde: Neutralizing the aggression within the Kraul is essential to protecting supply wagons and fledgling settlements across the southern expanses of the Barrens.
ang.race:Tauren: The quilboar have long contested Mulgore's borders, and their desecration of the earth through dark alliances makes the cleansing of the Kraul a vital matter of tribal defense.
ang.race:Undead: Apothecaries from the Undercity take an acute interest in the bizarre reagents, bat guano, and rumors of Scourge incursions found within the briars.

faq.a: Razorfen Kraul is an ancient subterranean network of massive thorny vines in the southern Barrens. It serves as the spiritual heartland and stronghold of the quilboar race, who consider the tangled labyrinth their ancestral home.
faq.q: What is Razorfen Kraul?

faq.a: The enormous brambles sprouted from the earth ten thousand years ago during the War of the Ancients, springing forth directly from the blood spilled by the fallen boar demigod Agamaggan.
al: where did the brambles come from
faq.q: How were the giant thorns created?

faq.a: The Kraul is ruled by Charlga Razorflank, a ruthless quilboar crone and shaman who commands the Razorfen tribe and orchestrates attacks on neighboring villages and travelers.
al: who is the boss of rfk
faq.q: Who rules Razorfen Kraul?

faq.a: Beyond constant quilboar raids on nascent settlements in the Barrens, Horde scouts have spotted undead skulking around the thickets, raising terrifying concerns that Charlga is aligning with the Scourge.
faq.q: Why is the Horde concerned about Razorfen Kraul?

faq.a: The aggressive expansion of Charlga's tribe threatens outposts near Feralas and the Thousand Needles, prompting Alliance commanders and scouts at Thalanaar to seek the crone's demise to stabilize the border.
faq.q: Why are Alliance forces interested in the Kraul?

faq.a: Defeating Earthcaller Halmgar, a rare and influential geomancer deep within the thickets, strikes a blow against the quilboar's earth-shaping priesthood. Stripping the Kraul of such powerful elemental summoners disrupts Charlga Razorflank's defensive fortifications and hinders the quilboar's ability to manipulate the sacred brambles of Agamaggan.
al: what happens after earthcaller halmgar dies
faq.q: What does defeating Earthcaller Halmgar mean for the story?

text.s: Tucked away in the far south of the Barrens, Razorfen Kraul is the ancestral heartland of Kalimdor's quilboar. These ferocious tribes revere the dense labyrinth of giant brambles as the sacred resting place of their progenitor, the fallen demigod Agamaggan. Today, the Kraul has grown aggressively hostile under the tyranny of the quilboar matriarch Charlga Razorflank, whose dark dealings threaten the entire region.

sec.b: Ten thousand years ago during the apocalyptic War of the Ancients, the colossal wild god Agamaggan threw himself into the fight against the Burning Legion. The great boar was eventually slain in battle, yet his sacrifice preserved life on Azeroth. Legends tell that wherever his blood seeped into the earth, massive thorn-covered vines erupted, forming thick, defensive labyrinths across the southern plains. The quilboar, venerating Agamaggan as their divine ancestor, claimed these colossal thickets as their holy lands, establishing the greatest of them as the Razorfen.

Razorfen Kraul is ruled with an iron tusk by the elder crone Charlga Razorflank. Under her despotic guidance, the shamanistic quilboar have abandoned their traditional territorial skirmishes to wage aggressive, coordinated war upon rival tribes, regional trade routes, and young Horde settlements. Far worse, troubling whispers and scout reports tell of undead fiends prowling near the brambles. It is feared that Charlga has begun negotiating with emissaries of the dreaded Scourge, seeking to harness forbidden necromancy to bolster her tribe's savagery.

zone:riverglades.s: Clarofluvial. Clarofluvial es un valle fluvial en disputa situado al este de Las Estepas Ardientes y Tierras Inhóspitas, reclamado históricamente por el Reino de Ventormenta. Invadida por la Horda Antigua durante la Primera Guerra y abandonada en gran medida por la corona, la región sigue siendo un campo de batalla mientras los leales humanos locales se enfrentan a los puestos de avanzada de la Horda moderna y a la fauna local. Limita con las Montañas Crestagrana al suroeste, el Pantano de las Penas al sur y mira hacia Tanaris al otro lado del mar. Históricamente parte del Reino de Ventormenta, Clarofluvial quedó en ruinas durante la Primera Guerra cuando la Horda Antigua arrasó la región. Su asentamiento central, Clarosol, fue saqueado por los orcos, quienes perdonaron su torre de magos únicamente para estudiar la hechicería humana antes de esclavizar a los aldeanos supervivientes. Aunque los soldados de Ventormenta hicieron un esfuerzo por liberar a los cautivos y reconstruir, el reino finalmente dio por perdido todo el valle y desvió recursos para defender los territorios centrales. Durante años, la región permaneció prácticamente aislada del apoyo formal de la corona.

ang.faction:Alliance: Alliance soldiers find old wounds laid bare in the Riverglades, where remnants of the Brotherhood of the Horse continue an unsung crusade to take back land Stormwind abandoned during the First War.
ang.faction:Horde: For the Horde, establishing outposts like Rog'mar ensures a secure coastal foothold and keeps pressure on old human strongholds lingering east of Redridge.
ang.race:Human: Human travelers witness a tragic chapter of their own heritage in Sunnyglade, a reminder of the First War's heavy toll on the eastern frontier of their kingdom.

faq.a: The Riverglades is a contested region lying east of the Badlands and Burning Steppes, fronting the Forbidding Sea. Once a flourishing territory of Stormwind, it is now an active frontier contested by the Alliance at Farholde Keep and the Horde at Rog'mar.
faq.q: What is the Riverglades?

faq.a: Sunnyglade was raided and destroyed by the Old Horde during the First War. The orcs captured the surviving villagers as slaves and kept a local mage tower intact to decipher human magic. Although Stormwind soldiers freed the captives and tried to rebuild, the kingdom ultimately abandoned the area to focus on its western borders.
faq.q: What happened to Sunnyglade?

faq.a: Farholde Keep is held by Alliance loyalists led by Knight Commander Demar Brant of the Brotherhood of the Horse. His forces have spent years fighting to reclaim the Riverglades after Stormwind originally wrote the territory off as lost.
faq.q: Who controls Farholde Keep?

faq.a: A coastal boat runs regularly between Powderfuse Port on the eastern shore of the Riverglades and Steamwheedle Port in Tanaris, offering a direct naval link across the sea.
faq.q: How do you reach Tanaris from the Riverglades?

faq.a: You can travel southwest through Redridge Pass to reach the Redridge Mountains, or cross south directly toward the Swamp of Sorrows. To the west, Blackrock Pass leads past the Bristle Hills to the Burning Steppes, while the trails north of Twilight's Shroud run directly into the Badlands.
faq.q: What passes lead into other zones?

faq.a: Krol'dok Stronghold is a fortified dungeon complex in the Riverglades, representing a major seat of hostile power in the contested territory.
faq.q: What is Krol'dok Stronghold?

text.s: The Riverglades is a contested river valley east of the Burning Steppes and Badlands, historically claimed by the Kingdom of Stormwind. Overrun by the Old Horde during the First War and largely abandoned by the crown, the region remains a battleground as local human loyalists clash with modern Horde outposts and local wildlife. It borders Redridge Mountains to the southwest, Swamp of Sorrows to the south, and faces Tanaris across the sea.

sec.b: Historically part of the Kingdom of Stormwind, the Riverglades fell into ruin during the First War when the Old Horde swept through the region. Its central settlement, Sunnyglade, was sacked by the orcs, who spared its mage tower solely to study human sorcery before enslaving the surviving townsfolk. Though Stormwind soldiers mounted an effort to liberate the captives and rebuild, the kingdom eventually deemed the entire valley lost and diverted resources toward defending the core homelands. For years, the region remained largely cut off from formal crown support.

Despite being left behind by Stormwind's higher leadership, the human defenders never fully surrendered their homeland. Under Knight Commander Demar Brant of the legendary Brotherhood of the Horse, the remaining loyalists hold Farholde Keep as a bastion against the wilderness and hostile invaders. Meanwhile, the modern Horde maintains their own strong presence nearby at outposts like Rog'mar and Bolder'ok, ensuring that the ancient conflict over the glades continues to smolder.

Stretching along the coast of the Forbidding Sea, the Riverglades is flanked by mountainous terrain and winding waterways. Travelers on foot can cross west through Blackrock Pass to the Burning Steppes, wind southwest through Redridge Pass toward the Redridge Mountains, navigate south into the Swamp of Sorrows, or trek northwest past Twilight's Shroud into the Badlands. On the coast, Powderfuse Port provides sea passage connecting directly across the ocean to Steamwheedle Port in Tanaris.

zone:ruinsoflordaeron.s: Ruinas de Lordaeron. Encaramadas directamente sobre la subterránea Entrañas, las Ruinas de Lordaeron son los restos desolados del que fuera el poderoso reino septentrional de la humanidad. Caídas ante la Plaga y el príncipe Arthas durante la Tercera Guerra, por las calles de la superficie y las plazas resquebrajadas merodean ahora monstruosidades errantes, espectros vengativos y viles experimentadores. Tanto la Alianza como la Horda envían expediciones a esta ciudadela asolada para recuperar reliquias del pasado caído o purgar los horrores que acechan sobre la capital de los Renegados. La capital de Lordaeron fue en su momento la joya de la corona de los Reinos del Este, la sede del rey Terenas Menethil II y el corazón palpitante de la civilización humana. Cuando el príncipe Arthas regresó de Rasganorte, asesinó a su padre en la sala del trono y desató a los no-muertos sobre los ciudadanos. Hoy, mientras los Renegados habitan en las catacumbas de Entrañas abajo, las ruinas de la superficie siguen siendo una zona en penumbra abandonada a su suerte. Los arcos derruidos y los adoquines cubiertos de maleza cobijan a bestias ferales como Witherfang y a trastornados vestigios del pasado.

ang.class:Paladin: Lordaeron was the cradle of the Knights of the Silver Hand; walking its desecrated halls to purge horrors and lay restless captains to rest is a solemn duty of the Light.
ang.faction:Alliance: Venturing into Lordaeron allows the Alliance to strike at the threshold of the Forsaken capital while bringing justice and peace to the spirits of their slaughtered northern brothers.
ang.race:Human: Human adventurers view the ruined capital as hallowed ground stolen by betrayal, seeking to reclaim lost heirlooms and honor fallen kin.
ang.race:Undead: For the Forsaken, the ruins above are their former home and eternal graveyard. Clearing it secures their front door and supplies the apothecaries with components to develop the New Plague.

faq.a: The dungeon is situated directly on the surface levels of Capital City in Tirisfal Glades, sitting right above the entrance network that leads down into the Forsaken capital of the Undercity.
faq.q: Where is the Ruins of Lordaeron dungeon located?

faq.a: For the Alliance, venturing into Lordaeron is a sacred pilgrimage to recover lost family heirlooms, collect royal crests, and grant final peace to fallen ancestors. For the Horde, particularly the Forsaken, clearing out the upper ruins is essential for securing the perimeter of the Undercity and acquiring research samples for the Royal Apothecary Society's new plague.
faq.q: Why are both the Horde and Alliance interested in this place?

faq.a: Viktor the Vile is one of the malevolent figures taking advantage of the ruins' lawlessness, operating foul experiments and contributing to the festering corruption that keeps the upper capital infested with twisted abominations.
faq.q: Who is Viktor the Vile?

faq.a: The Abandoned is a grotesque undead monstrosity left behind in the ruins. Like many patchwork horrors created during and after the Scourge's conquest, it wanders the derelict chambers aimlessly, attacking anything it encounters.
faq.q: What is 'The Abandoned' encountered in the ruins?

faq.a: Defeating the spectral Lordaeron Captain releases a high-ranking royal defender from a perpetual, maddening duty. Bound by honor since the Scourge's initial massacre, the Captain has spent years guarding a destroyed kingdom against all who approach. Laying the Captain to rest breaks an agonizing cycle of phantom servitude and allows their bloodied insignia to be reclaimed.
faq.q: What does defeating the Lordaeron Captain mean for the story?

faq.a: Yes. While the Forsaken make their home in the Undercity caverns below, the surface ruins are an active combat zone overrun with restless ghosts, feral predators, and experimental threats that the Forsaken have not fully eradicated.
faq.q: Is the Ruins of Lordaeron separate from the Undercity?

text.s: Perched directly above the subterranean Undercity, the Ruins of Lordaeron are the hollow remains of humanity's once-mighty northern kingdom. Fallen to the Scourge and Prince Arthas during the Third War, the surface streets and cracked plazas now crawl with wandering monstrosities, vengeful specters, and vile experimenters. Both the Alliance and the Horde dispatch ventures into this blighted citadel to reclaim relics of the fallen past or purge the horrors lurking above the Forsaken capital.

sec.b: Capital City was once the crown jewel of the Eastern Kingdoms, the seat of King Terenas Menethil II and the beating heart of human civilization. When Prince Arthas returned from Northrend, he slew his father in the throne room and unleashed the undead upon the citizenry. Today, while the Forsaken dwell in the catacombs of the Undercity below, the surface ruins remain a forsaken twilight zone. Broken archways and weed-choked cobbles shelter feral beasts like Witherfang and deranged remnants of the past.

The dangers within the ruined grounds go beyond restless dead. Apothecaries and sinister figures like Viktor the Vile work on testing new plagues among the shadows, while twisted experiments like The Abandoned roam freely. Wrathful spirits such as Rath'mael and cursed retainers like The Baron haunt the collapsed hallways, locked in unending torment and striking out against any living or undead trespassers who cross their paths.

Among the most poignant hazards in the upper ruins are the spectral remnants of the city's defenders, culminating in the appearance of a ghostly Lordaeron Captain. Still clinging to their shattered oaths, these apparitions perceive anyone approaching the throne as invaders. Putting the Captain and their soldiers to rest brings a bittersweet closure to an unbroken vigil that has lasted since the day the capital fell.

zone:scarlet.s: Monasterio Escarlata. Encaramado en las colinas del noreste de Claros de Tirisfal, el Monasterio Escarlata fue en su día un apacible santuario y centro de conocimiento para la Iglesia de la Luz Sagrada. Tras la caída de Lordaeron, la Cruzada Escarlata se apoderó de él y lo fortificó con celo para convertirlo en su principal base avanzada en el oeste. En la actualidad se erige como una extensa fortaleza dividida en cuatro alas, donde fanáticos devotos entrenan, torturan a cautivos y libran una guerra despiadada contra todo forastero. Antes de la Tercera Guerra, el monasterio sirvió como orgullosa sede del clero de Lordaeron y seminario para los incipientes paladines de la Mano de Plata, un lugar muy querido en su momento por el mismísimo arzobispo Alonsus Faol. Tras la devastación de la Plaga, los cruzados supervivientes purgaron las estancias de los no-muertos y arañas rezagados, transformando los tranquilos archivos y patios en una guarnición fortificada. Consumida por la paranoia y el dolor, la Cruzada Escarlata pasó a considerar a todo extraño —vivo o no-muerto, humano o de cualquier otra raza— como un portador de la peste al que se debía purificar con fuego.

ang.class:Mage: The Library wing houses rare historical and theological tomes guarded by Arcanist Doan, a former Dalaran scholar who defected to the Crusade's cause.
ang.class:Paladin: The monastery once served as a sacred seminary where the first paladins of the Silver Hand trained and prayed, making its descent into crimson zealotry a tragic reminder of how devotion can curdle into madness.
ang.class:Priest: Originally dedicated to Archbishop Alonsus Faol and the Church of the Holy Light, its grand chapels demonstrate how holy power can still be wielded by mortals twisted by hatred and vengeance.
ang.race:Undead: Perched on the border of Tirisfal Glades, the Scarlet Monastery represents an existential threat to the Forsaken, staging spies into Deathknell and torturing captured undead within its dungeons.

faq.a: The Crusade has succumbed to extreme madness and paranoia. In their eyes, anyone who does not wear their crimson tabard is a potential carrier of the Scourge plague. They no longer make distinctions between friend or foe, viewing all outsiders as tainted beings who must be purged before they can spread corruption.
faq.q: Why is the Scarlet Crusade hostile to living Alliance adventurers?

faq.a: Defeating High Inquisitor Whitemane decapitates the Scarlet Crusade's western military leadership. As the spiritual leader of the monastery, her miraculous resurrection powers maintained troop morale and kept Commander Mograine fighting at her side. Her death removes the Crusade's most potent priestess in Tirisfal Glades, leaving the garrison disordered and severely diminishing their threat to the surrounding region.
faq.q: What happens when you defeat High Inquisitor Whitemane?

faq.a: The Scarlet Key is held deep within the Library wing of the monastery, kept inside Arcanist Doan's strongbox behind his personal study. Possessing this key is necessary to unlock the outer gates of both the Armory and the Cathedral wings.
al: how to unlock armory and cathedral
faq.q: What is the Scarlet Key and where is it found?

faq.a: Arcanist Doan was a gifted human wizard from Dalaran who abandoned his fellow Kirin Tor magi to align with the Scarlet Crusade. Seeking seclusion to study rare manuscripts and master powerful fire and arcane magic, he took control of the monastery's extensive Library wing.
faq.q: Why is Arcanist Doan in the Scarlet Monastery?

faq.a: Alexandros Mograine, the famed Ashbringer and former leader of the Silver Hand in Lordaeron, prayed and trained at the monastery during his youth. After the Third War, he made it a forward staging ground against the undead; his son Renault now commands the Cathedral alongside High Inquisitor Whitemane.
faq.q: Who was Alexandros Mograine and how is he connected here?

faq.a: While the rest of the monastery maintains an outward appearance of pristine devotion, the Graveyard is where the Crusade's fanaticism rots from within. It holds their brutal torture chambers run by Interrogator Vishas, while neglected crypts and restless dead are harvested or manipulated by fallen casters like Bloodmage Thalnos.
faq.q: What makes the Graveyard wing so different from the rest of the monastery?

text.s: Perched in the northeastern hills of Tirisfal Glades, the Scarlet Monastery was once a peaceful sanctuary and center of learning for the Church of the Holy Light. Following the fall of Lordaeron, it was seized and heavily fortified by the Scarlet Crusade as their primary forward base in the west. Now, it stands as a sprawling stronghold divided into four wings, where fanatical zealots train, torture captives, and wage an uncompromising war against all outsiders.

sec.b: Before the Third War, the monastery served as a proud seat of Lordaeron's priesthood and a seminary for fledgling paladins of the Silver Hand, once cherished by Archbishop Alonsus Faol himself. Following the Scourge's devastation, surviving crusaders purged the halls of lingering undead and spiders, transforming the tranquil archives and courtyards into a fortified garrison. Driven by paranoia and grief, the Scarlet Crusade came to view all outsiders—living or undead, human or otherwise—as carriers of the plague who must be cleansed with fire.

Past the monastery's Grand Vestibule lie four distinct quarters. The Graveyard is an unhallowed open-air terrace where fallen crusaders rise as undead abominations and torturers pry confessions from prisoners. The Library preserves precious theological texts and historical tomes, guarded by the renegade mage Arcanist Doan and his hounds. The Armory serves as a training ground where Scarlet weaponmasters like Herod drill fanatic recruits into ironclad warriors. Deepest within stands the Cathedral, the grand heart of the stronghold where the Crusade's leadership directs their crusade across the blighted north.

The inner sanctum of the Cathedral is commanded by Scarlet Commander Mograine and the monastery's true master, High Inquisitor Sally Whitemane. Defeating Whitemane strikes a critical blow to the Crusade's operational command in Tirisfal Glades. Her ability to channel blinding Holy Light and resurrect fallen champions made the garrison seem invincible to its devotees. Slaying her shatters the aura of divine mandate that fueled the monastery's zealotry, exposing the Crusade's leadership as mortal and severely weakening their campaign against the Forsaken and the neighboring lands.
sec.t: The Fall of the High Inquisitor

zone:searinggorge.s: La Garganta de Fuego. La Garganta de Fuego es un cañón calcinado y desolado situado en el sur de Khaz Modan, que limita al sur con la Montaña Roca Negra. En su día fue una verde extensión de las Montañas Crestagrana, pero quedó devastada hace más de dos siglos por la apocalíptica invocación de Ragnaros, el Señor del Fuego. En la actualidad, la garganta está intensamente explotada por el clan Hierro Negro, cuyas extensas minas con esclavos en La Caldera están estrechamente vigiladas por la escindida Hermandad del torio. Antes de la Guerra de los Tres Martillos, el territorio que hoy conforma La Garganta de Fuego era una región montañosa, verde y ondulada, unida a la cordillera de Crestagrana. Ese exuberante paisaje dejó de existir hace más de doscientos treinta años, cuando el señor feudal hechicero Thaurissan, desesperado por cambiar el rumbo de la derrota, invocó a Ragnaros desde las profundidades del mundo. El cataclísmico surgimiento del Señor del Fuego desgarró la tierra, alzó la Montaña Roca Negra, redujo la gran ciudad de Thaurissan de los Hierro Negro a ruinas humeantes y convirtió el valle septentrional en una extensión resquebrajada de ceniza, azufre y vidrio volcánico.

ang.class:Rogue: Rogues with seasoned lockpicking skill are valued travelers here, as they can bypass the locked Stonewrought Pass gate connecting Loch Modan directly to the gorge.
ang.faction:Alliance: The Alliance keeps the gate at Stonewrought Pass locked to isolate the Dark Irons from peaceful dwarven settlements in Loch Modan, though courageous adventurers are sanctioned to strike into the gorge.
ang.faction:Horde: Using Kargath as a staging base, the Horde cut an overland approach into the gorge to gather intelligence on Blackrock Mountain and disrupt Dark Iron operations in Khaz Modan.
ang.profession:Mining: The volcanic landscape and deep excavations in the Slag Pit make Searing Gorge one of the primary hunting grounds for rich veins of mithril, truesilver, and coveted Dark Iron ore.
ang.race:Dwarf: For dwarves of Ironforge, Searing Gorge is a bitter reminder of the War of the Three Hammers and the catastrophic folly of the Dark Iron clan, whose excavations now threaten Khaz Modan's southern approaches.

faq.a: Over two hundred and thirty years ago, during the War of the Three Hammers, the Dark Iron Sorcerer-Thane Thaurissan attempted to summon a supernatural power to avoid defeat. Instead, he summoned Ragnaros the Firelord. The cataclysmic eruption shattered the southern Redridge range, created the volcano of Blackrock Mountain, and incinerated the surrounding valleys into Searing Gorge and the Burning Steppes.
faq.q: Why is the Searing Gorge burned and covered in ash?

faq.a: They belong to the Thorium Brotherhood, an independent faction of Dark Iron dwarves who severed ties with their imperial kin under Blackrock Mountain. From their camp atop Thorium Point, they work as master smiths and artificers, trading knowledge and crafting secrets to any traveler who aids them against the Dark Iron forces below.
faq.q: Who are the dwarves living at Thorium Point?

faq.a: The Cauldron is a massive open excavation dominated by the Dark Iron clan, containing the subterranean Slag Pit. Dark Iron overseers and war golems use captured prisoners as slave labor to extract precious ores—including valuable Dark Iron deposits—to feed the great forges inside Blackrock Mountain.
faq.q: What is going on in the Cauldron?

faq.a: The passage from Loch Modan through Stonewrought Pass is barred by a heavy locked gate guarded by Ironforge mountaineers. Travelers must either obtain the Key to Searing Gorge through an official task for Curator Thorius, have a skilled rogue pick the mechanism, or bypass the gate entirely by taking the open trail south of Kargath in the Badlands.
al: how to open searing gorge door
faq.q: How do you get into Searing Gorge from Loch Modan?

faq.a: Operating from the nearby fortress of Kargath in the Badlands, Horde commanders carved a mountain pass into the gorge to scout Dark Iron troop movements and secure tactical routes toward Blackrock Mountain, which holds immense strategic importance.
faq.q: Why is the Horde interested in Searing Gorge?

faq.a: There are no instance portals directly in the gorge itself, but the southern entrance leads straight into Blackrock Mountain. That mountain houses Blackrock Depths, Blackrock Spire, and the deep passages leading into the Molten Core.
faq.q: Are there any dungeons or raid entrances inside Searing Gorge?

text.s: Searing Gorge is a scorched, desolate canyon in southern Khaz Modan, bordering Blackrock Mountain to the south. Once a verdant expanse of the Redridge Mountains, it was devastated over two centuries ago by the apocalyptic summoning of Ragnaros the Firelord. Today, the gorge is heavily worked by the Dark Iron clan, whose extensive slave mines in the Cauldron are closely monitored by the breakaway Thorium Brotherhood.

sec.b: Before the War of the Three Hammers, the territory that is now Searing Gorge was a green, rolling mountain region connected to the Redridge chain. That lush landscape ceased to exist over two hundred and thirty years ago when Sorcerer-Thane Thaurissan, desperate to turn the tide of defeat, summoned Ragnaros from the depths beneath the world. The cataclysmic emergence of the Firelord tore the earth asunder, raised Blackrock Mountain, reduced the grand Dark Iron city of Thaurissan to smoking ruins, and burned the northern valley into a cracked expanse of ash, sulfur, and volcanic glass.

Seeking raw materials to supply their war machine after the loss of their old capital, the Dark Iron dwarves seized the desolate gorge. In the center of the valley lies the Cauldron, a colossal open-pit excavation plunging deep into the stone. Within its lower recesses sits the Slag Pit, a brutal subterranean mining complex. Here, Dark Iron overseers and lumbering war golems drive captured enemies into grueling slave labor, pulling iron, mithril, and rare deposits of Dark Iron ore out of the burning rock under the constant threat of lava surges and roaming beasts.
sec.t: The Cauldron and the Slag Pit

sec.b: Perched on the northern crags overlooking the excavation sits Thorium Point, the fortified outpost of the Thorium Brotherhood. Having split from their kin in Blackrock Mountain, these master craftsmen offer neutral shelter to travelers willing to undermine the Dark Iron operations or supply them with rare smelting components. Access to the gorge itself is tightly restricted: the Alliance keeps the Stonewrought Pass locked down behind heavy iron gates toward Loch Modan, while Horde expeditions from nearby Kargath have cut a narrow trail through the eastern badlands to scout the region.

zone:shadowfang.s: Castillo de Colmillo Oscuro. Encaramado en los abruptos riscos sobre Aldea Piroleña, el Castillo de Colmillo Oscuro es la sombría fortaleza del mago renegado del Kirin Tor, el archimago Arugal. Antaño la hacienda ancestral del Barón Filargenta, el bastión ahora rebosa de feroces bestias huargen y de los atormentados fantasmas de sus defensores masacrados. Para los aventureros que cruzan el sur de Bosque de Argénteos, el castillo representa el oscuro epicentro de la plaga bestial que consume la región. Antes de quedar envuelto en la pesadilla, Colmillo Oscuro era conocido como el Castillo Filargenta, una noble sede leal a los señores gilneanos y guarnecida por el piadoso Comandante Vallefont. Cuando la Plaga arrasó Lordaeron durante la Tercera Guerra, los magos de Dalaran cayeron a raudales. Desesperado por frenar a los muertos que se alzaban, el archimago Arugal desafió al liderazgo del Kirin Tor y profundizó en las investigaciones del mago Ur, invocando huargen extradimensionales para cambiar las tornas. Las bestias invocadas destrozaron a los no-muertos, pero rápidamente escaparon a todo control mortal, irrumpiendo en el sur de Bosque de Argénteos y asaltando el bastión. El Barón Filargenta y toda su corte fueron masacrados, condenados a vagar por los salones de piedra junto a los feroces monstruos que invadieron su hogar.

ang.class:Mage: The tragedy of Shadowfang serves as a grim warning of what happens when a Kirin Tor wizard meddles in extra-dimensional summoning beyond mortal control.
ang.class:Paladin: The restless spirit of Commander Springvale stands as a sorrowful reminder of fallen Silver Hand defenders whose sacred oaths were warped by death.
ang.class:Warlock: The dark energies, voidwalkers, and fell sorceries inside the keep draw the interest of practitioners looking to recover ancient relics like the Orb of Soran'ruk.
ang.faction:Horde: The Forsaken view Arugal's encroaching packs as an immediate danger to their fledgling territory in Silverpine, making the keep a priority target for Deathstalker operatives and the Royal Apothecary Society.

faq.a: Slaying Arugal decapitates the central force controlling the worgen packs in southern Silverpine. Horde adventurers deliver his severed head to Dalar Dawnweaver at the Sepulcher under orders from Lady Sylvanas Windrunner. While his demise breaks the direct will directing the Shadowfang pack, the feral beasts and ghostly remnants lingering in the keep and the surrounding woods remain a persistent danger to travelers.
faq.q: What happens when Archmage Arugal is defeated?

faq.a: During the Third War, the armies of Dalaran were suffering disastrous defeats against the Scourge. Fallen wizards continuously rose as undead soldiers for the Lich King. Seeking a weapon to turn the tide, Arugal used the arcane research of the wizard Ur to summon extra-dimensional worgen, believing their savagery could halt the Scourge.
faq.q: Why did Arugal summon the worgen?

faq.a: Baron Silverlaine was the human nobleman who ruled the keep and oversaw the neighboring hamlet of Pyrewood before the Third War. When Arugal's summoned beasts escaped control, they stormed the stronghold and butchered the baron, his household, and his guards. Silverlaine's vengeful ghost still haunts the great dining halls, cursed to walk alongside the monsters that slew him.
faq.q: Who was Baron Silverlaine?

faq.a: Arugal subjected the inhabitants of nearby Pyrewood Village to his dark magic. By day, they retain their human form, minds, and peaceful demeanor toward Alliance travelers. At sundown, the curse takes hold, transforming the entire population into savage worgen loyal to the mad archmage in the keep.
faq.q: Why are Pyrewood Village villagers friendly during the day?

faq.a: Commander Springvale was a paladin of the Silver Hand and the military officer responsible for defending Silverlaine Keep. When the worgen overrun the stronghold, he fought to the death. His restless spirit still patrols the upper hallways, clinging to martial duty even in undeath.
faq.q: Who is Commander Springvale?

faq.a: The Book of Ur is a tome containing the research of Ur, an archmage of Dalaran who studied extra-dimensional entities, including the worgen. Arugal used Ur's writings to perform his disastrous summons. The Royal Apothecary Society in the Undercity seeks the book to understand the nature of the wolf-creatures and their bizarre magic.
faq.q: What is the Book of Ur?

text.s: Perched on the rugged bluffs above Pyrewood Village, Shadowfang Keep is the gloomy stronghold of the rogue Kirin Tor wizard, Archmage Arugal. Once the ancestral estate of Baron Silverlaine, the bastion now teems with feral worgen beasts and the tormented phantoms of its slaughtered defenders. For adventurers traversing southern Silverpine, the keep represents the dark epicenter of the beastly scourge consuming the region.

sec.b: Before it was shrouded in nightmare, Shadowfang was known as Silverlaine Keep, a noble seat loyal to Gilnean lords and garrisoned by the pious Commander Springvale. When the Scourge swept through Lordaeron during the Third War, Dalaran's wizards fell in droves. Desperate to stem the rising dead, Archmage Arugal defied Kirin Tor leadership and delved into the research of the wizard Ur, summoning extra-dimensional worgen to turn the tide. The summoned beasts savaged the undead, but rapidly slipped beyond all mortal control, breaking into southern Silverpine and storming the bastion. Baron Silverlaine and his entire court were massacred, doomed to haunt the stone halls alongside the feral monsters that overran their home.

Broken by guilt and madness, Arugal retreated within the blood-stained battlements, adopting the ravenous wolf-men as his beloved 'children' and christening the castle Shadowfang Keep. Deep in the stone roosts, lupine packs and shadowy hounds flourish under trainers like Wolf Master Nandos, watched over by Arugal's massive lupine beast, Fenrus the Devourer. Outside the walls, the curse did not halt; nearby Pyrewood Village remains trapped in a horrifying nocturnal cycle, its residents walking as men by day and hunting as ravenous worgen beneath the moon, tethered inexorably to the mad archmage perched on the heights above.

Recognizing the dire threat Arugal poses to their dominion in Silverpine Forest, Lady Sylvanas Windrunner dispatched the Royal Apothecary Society and elite Deathstalkers to root out the source of the worgen curse. Infiltration teams suffered brutal casualties within the dungeons, but Horde heroes answering the call from the Sepulcher ultimately breach the highest tower. Striking down the Archmage brings a formal end to the master of the pack, severing the mind orchestrating the beasts' spread across the wilderness and claiming his head as proof of Lordaeron's vengeance.

zone:shendralas.s: Shen'dralas. Shen'dralas es una tierra salvaje, escarpada y disputada situada entre Feralas, Mulgore y el sureste de Desolace. Dominada por antiguos vestigios de los elfos de la noche y fronteras conflictivas, sirve como una encrucijada inestable donde chocan centauros invasores, desterrados desplazados y erizados jabaespines. Escondida en las alturas al sureste de Desolace y bordeada por Mulgore y Feralas, Shen'dralas es una tierra fronteriza agreste, muy alejada de las capitales de las principales facciones. Sus desfiladeros escarpados y enclaves ocultos albergan a grupos desesperados que se labran la vida al borde del Kalimdor salvaje. Desde miradores apartados como Evenshade Overlook hasta refugios sin ley como el Escondrijo de los Desterrados, la zona se define por aquellos que desean vigilar sin ser vistos o permanecer en el olvido.

ang.faction:Alliance: A remote, contested wilderness providing alternate routes between Feralas and central Kalimdor, fraught with dangers that require keen vigilance.
ang.faction:Horde: Positioned just outside the southern reaches of Mulgore, keeping the Magram and quilboar contained here is vital for protecting Horde frontiers.
ang.race:NightElf: The name evokes the ancient Highborne lore of Eldre'Thalas, drawing the attention of sentinels wary of reckless arcana in southern Kalimdor.
ang.race:Tauren: With the region bordering Mulgore and Desolace, the aggression of quilboar and centaur along these ridges poses a direct threat to nearby ancestral hunting grounds.

faq.a: Shen'dralas lies south-east of Desolace, nestled between the borders of Feralas and Mulgore. Travelers arriving on foot typically enter from Desolace by passing through the Valley of Bones.
faq.q: Where is Shen'dralas located?

faq.a: Neither faction holds dominion here. Shen'dralas is a contested frontier populated by roving centaur, hostile quilboar, outcasts, and isolated encampments.
faq.q: Is Shen'dralas controlled by the Alliance or the Horde?

faq.a: Prominent landmarks include the Valley of Bones, Bristleback Retreat, Evenshade Overlook, the Magram Front, Outcast Hideaway, and the central expanse of Shen'dralas itself.
faq.q: What major settlements or landmarks are here?

faq.a: Centaur territorial wars extend from the plains of Desolace straight into the region along the Magram Front, where the clan clashes against local defenders and rival factions.
faq.q: Why are there centaur here?

faq.a: Bristleback Retreat is a fortified outpost held by Bristleback quilboar who have established a fierce foothold along the edges of the zone.
faq.q: What is Bristleback Retreat?

faq.a: Geographically, the wilderness of Shen'dralas sits across the mountainous territory where the secluded Lake Dumont sits tucked away in old survey charts.
faq.q: What is the connection between this zone and Lake Dumont?

text.s: Shen'dralas is a rugged, contested wilderness situated between Feralas, Mulgore, and south-eastern Desolace. Dominated by ancient night elven remnants and troubled borders, it serves as a volatile crossroads where encroaching centaur, displaced outcasts, and bristling quilboar collide.

sec.b: Tucked away in the heights south-east of Desolace and bordered by Mulgore and Feralas, Shen'dralas is a raw borderland far removed from major faction capitols. Its craggy passes and hidden enclaves harbor desperate groups carving out existence on the edge of wild Kalimdor. From secluded vantage points like Evenshade Overlook to lawless refuges like Outcast Hideaway, the zone is defined by those who wish to watch unseen or stay forgotten.

The land bears the distinct mark of the highborne legacy that gave it its name, yet it is far from peaceful. Centaur conflict bleeds across the Magram Front, keeping old blood feuds alive and well along its borders. Meanwhile, encroaching quilboar maintain fortified redoubts such as Bristleback Retreat, turning every shadowed ravine into contested territory for any traveler passing through.

Leading out north-west toward Desolace lies the Valley of Bones, a grim corridor that serves as the primary overland access route into Shen'dralas. Bleached by sun and wind, this passage stands as a harsh reminder of the violent struggles that constantly ripple through these crags.

zone:silverpine.s: Bosque de Argénteos. El Bosque de Argénteos es un bosque inquietante y envuelto en niebla que se extiende a lo largo de la costa occidental de Lordaeron, entre Claros de Tirisfal y la cerrada Muralla de Cringrís. Asolado por las cicatrices persistentes de la peste propagada por la Plaga, sirve como la disputada frontera sur de los Renegados. Quienes viajan por aquí se enfrentan a feroces huargen que merodean entre las sombras, gnolls enfermos y enclaves humanos hostiles. Antaño celebrado como una frondosa maravilla de Lordaeron por la que los nobles viajaban hacia Ciudad Capital, el Bosque de Argénteos se ha marchitado bajo el impacto de la Tercera Guerra. Nieblas espectrales serpentean entre pinos agonizantes de corteza plateada, y granjas en ruinas yacen abandonadas a merced de la naturaleza. Al norte se encuentran los Claros de Tirisfal, mientras que la orilla este limita con el Lago Lordamere. Al sur se alza la imponente y sellada Muralla de Cringrís, que aísla al reino aislacionista de Gilneas del caos circundante. Los Renegados mantienen su puesto principal en El Sepulcro, esforzándose por asegurar el bosque frente a enemigos por todos los frentes.

ang.class:Mage: The presence of Ambermill and the fall of Archmage Arugal into lupine madness make Silverpine a grim cautionary tale of Kirin Tor magic gone disastrously astray.
ang.faction:Alliance: Alliance explorers will find a profoundly hostile forest, punctuated only by a fragile Dalaran garrison at Ambermill and the tragic, cursed villagers of Pyrewood Village.
ang.race:Undead: Silverpine represents the immediate front line of Forsaken expansion south of Tirisfal Glades, where the Royal Apothecary Society tests new concoctions and the Deathguard battles lingering Scourge agents.

faq.a: The Greymane Wall is a massive stone barrier built by King Genn Greymane to completely isolate his kingdom of Gilneas from the rest of Lordaeron. When the Scourge ravaged the continent during the Third War, Gilneas locked its gates and refused outside aid, leaving the lands north of the wall—including southern Silverpine—to fend for themselves.
al: why is there a giant wall
faq.q: What is the Greymane Wall at the southern border?

faq.a: The inhabitants of Pyrewood Village suffer from Archmage Arugal's worgen curse. By day, they retain human form and maintain their daily routines, remaining friendly to the Alliance. When the moon rises, the curse takes hold, transforming the entire population into savage, bloodthirsty worgen that violently attack anyone nearby.
al: why are pyrewood humans hostile at night
faq.q: Why do the villagers of Pyrewood Village attack at night?

faq.a: Thule Ravenclaw is a powerful necromancer serving the Scourge. Operating out of Fenris Keep on Fenris Isle within Lordamere Lake, he commands legions of undead and exerts influence over the diseased Rot Hide gnolls across eastern Silverpine, directly threatening the Forsaken's eastern flank.
faq.q: Who is Thule Ravenclaw?

faq.a: Ambermill is held by wizards of Dalaran led by Archmage Ataeric. Operating from the village, these human mages monitor Forsaken movements, study the magical afflictions plaguing the forest, and seek to contain the nearby worgen outbreak radiating from Shadowfang Keep.
al: why is the alliance in ambermill
faq.q: Why is Dalaran occupying Ambermill?

faq.a: The Sepulcher is the primary Forsaken military outpost and travel hub in Silverpine Forest. Under the command of High Executor Hadrec, it serves as the base of operations for Deathguard patrols, Deathstalker scouts, and the Royal Apothecary Society as they fight to secure the forest.
faq.q: What is the Sepulcher?

faq.a: Silverpine Forest has no Alliance quest hubs or friendly towns; all local quests are exclusively for the Horde. Alliance adventurers typically only enter the forest when traveling from Southshore to explore Shadowfang Keep or to battle hostile Forsaken forces.
faq.q: Can Alliance players quest in Silverpine Forest?

text.s: Silverpine Forest is an eerie, mist-laden woodland stretching along Lordaeron's western coast between Tirisfal Glades and the sealed Greymane Wall. Haunted by the lingering scars of the Scourge plague, it serves as the contested southern frontier of the Forsaken. Travelers here face feral worgen roaming the shadows, diseased gnolls, and hostile human enclaves.

sec.b: Once celebrated as a lush wonder of Lordaeron through which noble travelers journeyed to Capital City, Silverpine Forest has withered under the touch of the Third War. Ghostly fogs weave between dying, silver-barked pines, and ruined farmsteads sit abandoned to the wilderness. To the north lies Tirisfal Glades, while the eastern shore borders Lordamere Lake. To the south stands the imposing and shut Greymane Wall, sealing off the isolationist kingdom of Gilneas from the surrounding chaos. The Forsaken maintain their central outpost at the Sepulcher, striving to secure the woods from enemies on all sides.

Silverpine's most infamous peril is the worgen curse. High above the southwest woods sits Shadowfang Keep, the former seat of Baron Silverlaine, now dominated by the mad Dalaran archmage Arugal. Seeking to repel the Scourge during the Third War, Arugal summoned extra-dimensional wolf-beasts. The creatures turned on their summoners, spreading a lycanthropic curse across the southern woods. In Pyrewood Village, ordinary-looking human villagers go about their chores by daylight, but transform into savage worgen beneath the night sky.

The Forsaken claim to Silverpine is hotly contested by living and undead factions alike. To the east on Fenris Isle, Thule Ravenclaw leads a force of Scourge remnants while commanding the plague-addled Rot Hide gnolls that plague northern farmlands. In the south, human mages from Dalaran hold the fortified settlement of Ambermill, conducting mystical research and opposing Forsaken expansion. The Royal Apothecary Society and High Executor Hadrec at the Sepulcher wage a brutal, multifaceted campaign to eliminate these threats and test virulent new plagues.

zone:stockade.s: Las Mazmorras. Las Mazmorras son el complejo penitenciario de alta seguridad de Ventormenta, escondido bajo el distrito de los canales de la ciudad, cerca del Barrio de los Magos. Construidas para albergar a los asesinos más peligrosos del reino, insurgentes políticos y enemigos del estado capturados, las instalaciones han caído recientemente en una violenta anarquía. El alcaide Thelagua se ha visto obligado a retroceder hasta la entrada, reclutando desesperadamente a aventureros capaces para sofocar el motín desde dentro antes de que se extienda a la capital. Bajo los tranquilos canales de Ventormenta, Las Mazmorras se han convertido en una zona de guerra. Cuando el ejército regular marchó a luchar en frentes lejanos, la prisión, falta de personal, dependió de jóvenes inexpertos —incluidos reclutas de catorce años— para mantener el orden. No aguantaron. Los reclusos iniciaron una rebelión sangrienta y coordinada, rasgando sus mantas de lana para hacer pañuelos que identificaran a su banda y aniquilando a los guardias restantes. El alcaide Thelagua apenas pudo mantener el control de la entrada, dejando las celdas, los pasillos y los bloques de detención en las despiadadas manos de los convictos.

ang.class:Mage: Located right on the canal edge of the Mage Quarter, the prison contains physical brawlers vulnerable to slowing spells, while the ogre mage Hamhock can unleash Chain Lightning.
ang.class:Rogue: The prison layout presents an intricate web of locked iron cells and Defias connections, offering unique lockpicking practice and insight into Bazil Thredd's underworld syndicate.
ang.faction:Alliance: The rebellion threatens the very heart of the capital; putting down the uprising preserves Stormwind's internal security while honoring off-the-books bounties for Redridge, Duskwood, and Ironforge.
ang.race:Dwarf: The presence of Kam Deepfury in Stormwind's cells is an affront to Dun Modr; the Kingdom of Ironforge demands his head to avenge dwarven lives lost in the Wetlands.

faq.a: The Defias Brotherhood orchestrated a prison-wide riot while the facility was severely understaffed. With the Stormwind Army deployed to distant battlefronts, teenage volunteers were left guarding hardened killers. The convicts ambushed the staff, seized weapons, and forced Warden Thelwater out of the cellblocks.
faq.q: Why is the Stockade in open rebellion?

faq.a: The mastermind behind the revolt is Bazil Thredd, an influential Defias felon incarcerated in the eastern cellblock. Other dangerous prisoners include Bruegal Ironknuckle, Hamhock, and Kam Deepfury.
faq.q: Who is running the uprising inside?

faq.a: Both were condemned to death, but corrupt politicians within the House of Nobles placed bureaucratic holds on their executions to use them as political leverage. This interference outraged allies in Lakeshire and Darkshire, prompting them to send adventurers to eliminate the prisoners during the chaos.
faq.q: Why are prisoners like Targorr and Dextren Ward still alive?

faq.a: Bruegal Ironknuckle is a dangerous dwarven brawler among the rioters. Defeating him removes one threat from the prison while adventurers work to put down the uprising.
faq.q: What does defeating Bruegal Ironknuckle mean for the prison?

faq.a: The Stockade serves as a maximum-security holding pen for high-value prisoners of war. Targorr the Dread led Blackrock orc attacks in Redridge, while Kam Deepfury conducted sabotage for the Dark Iron clan in the Wetlands before both were captured and transferred to the capital.
faq.q: Why are there Dark Iron dwarves and orcs inside a human jail?

faq.a: Yes, but it is exceptionally hazardous. The dungeon entrance sits directly inside Stormwind City near the Mage Quarter canals. Horde infiltrators must sneak past the city guards and the capital's defenders to reach the portal.
faq.q: Can Horde players enter the Stockade?

text.s: The Stockade is Stormwind's high-security prison complex, tucked beneath the city's canal district near the Mage Quarter. Built to hold the kingdom's most dangerous cutthroats, political insurgents, and captured enemies of state, the facility has recently collapsed into violent anarchy. Warden Thelwater has been forced back to the threshold, desperately recruiting capable adventurers to crush the riot from within before it spills out into the capital.

sec.b: Beneath the tranquil canals of Stormwind, the Stockade has become a war zone. When the regular army marched out to fight on distant fronts, the understaffed prison leaned on inexperienced youth—including fourteen-year-old recruits—to maintain order. It did not hold. The inmates launched a bloody, coordinated rebellion, tearing their wool blankets into gang scarves and cutting down the remaining guards. Warden Thelwater barely maintained control of the entryway, leaving the cells, hallways, and holding blocks in the ruthless hands of the convicts.

The riot laid bare the ugly underbelly of Stormwind's political machine. Outside territories had long grown frustrated with the House of Nobles halting executions for their own leverage. Redridge guard Berton wanted the captured orc Targorr the Dread executed for atrocities, only to watch nobles freeze the sentence. Darkshire councilman Millstipe watched the grave-robber Dextren Ward get spared the gallows despite desecrating graves for the necromancer Morbent Fel. Even the dwarves of Dun Modr sent word demanding the death of Dark Iron saboteur Kam Deepfury. With the Stockade in chaos, local authorities quietly hired adventurers to carry out the executions the capital's courts refused to enforce.

Behind the prison's synchronized collapse sits Bazil Thredd, a cunning felon tied directly to the Defias Brotherhood who orchestrated the uprising from his cell. Among the rioters is Bruegal Ironknuckle, a dangerous dwarven brawler. He is one of several hardened convicts adventurers may encounter while helping Thelwater reclaim the prison.

zone:stonetalon.s: Sierra Espolón. Sierra Espolón es una escarpada cordillera de picos rocosos esculpidos por el viento que limita con Vallefresno, Los Baldíos y Desolace. Venerada tanto por los elfos de la noche como por los tauren como un santuario sagrado, las cumbres sagradas de la región contrastan fuertemente con el humo y la maquinaria que asfixian sus cañones inferiores. Hoy en día, las montañas están desgarradas por la deforestación, la devastación elemental volátil y las latentes hostilidades fronterizas. Elevándose abruptamente desde el centro de Kalimdor, la cordillera de Espolón atrapa la humedad que llega de los mares occidentales, dando lugar a repentinos aguaceros y traicioneros senderos de arenisca resbaladizos por la lluvia. El rasgo predominante de los valles bajos es el incesante vendaval abrasador conocido como los Vientos Aciagos, capaz de cegar a los viajeros con arenilla o de arrojar a los descuidados directamente por los escarpados acantilados. Más arriba, bosques de hoja perenne cubren las crestas que rodean Cima del Espolón, donde los elfos de la noche cuidan túmulos ancestrales y claros, vigilando los nidos sagrados de dracoleones e hipogrifos que anidan a lo largo del Lago Mirkfallon.

ang.class:Druid: The desecration of Windshear Crag and the scorched corruption of the Charred Vale serve as a grave summons for druids seeking to soothe enraged nature spirits and protect sacred roosts.
ang.class:Shaman: The cry of the mountain spirits under assault by goblin drills can be heard as far as Orgrimmar, calling shamans to quell rampaging rock elementals and restore balance to the peaks.
ang.faction:Alliance: Stationed high atop Stonetalon Peak and in hidden camps around Windshear Crag, the Alliance defends ancient kaldorei barrows from goblin machines and encroaching territorial rivals.
ang.faction:Horde: Horde adventurers rely on the secluded refuge of Sun Rock Retreat and the southern troll post of Malaka'jin to curb Venture Company industrial pollution and root out treacherous Grimtotem outlaws.

faq.a: Most travelers enter via the Talondeep Pass, a mountain trail cutting into the range from southwestern Ashenvale. There are also high trails leading south into Desolace and routes descending eastward directly into the northern expanses of the Barrens.
faq.q: How do I get to the Stonetalon Mountains?

faq.a: The Charred Vale was once a lush haven, but cataclysmic devastation consumed the valley in flames. It has been reduced to a smoldering ruin crawling with aggressive fire elementals, rogue drakes, and deadly harpies.
faq.q: Why is the Charred Vale burned and ruined?

faq.a: The Venture Company is ruthlessly clear-cutting timber and drilling deep into the mountainside for mineral wealth. Their operations have fouled Cragpool Lake with engine grease, stripped the valleys bare, and enraged the local spirits and native inhabitants.
faq.q: What is the Venture Company doing in Windshear Crag?

faq.a: Alliance heroes use the flight master perched at the high sanctuary of Stonetalon Peak in the north, while Horde adventurers base themselves in the central mountain village of Sun Rock Retreat.
faq.q: Where are the main flight masters located?

faq.a: Guided by visions of the Prophet Medivh, Thrall and Jaina Proudmoore climbed the caverns of Stonetalon Peak in search of the Oracle. There, the two faction leaders forged the historic temporary alliance that united against the Burning Legion at Mount Hyjal.
faq.q: What happened at Stonetalon Peak during the Third War?

faq.a: The Grimtotem are a ruthless, renegade tauren tribe hostile to outsider influence. In the Stonetalons, they have occupied a mountain post near the border of the Barrens, terrorizing local travelers and taking prisoners.
faq.q: Who are the Grimtotem in Stonetalon?

text.s: The Stonetalon Mountains are a rugged, wind-carved chain of craggy peaks bordering Ashenvale, the Barrens, and Desolace. Revered by both the night elves and the tauren as a sacred sanctuary, the region's sacred heights stand in sharp contrast to the smoke and machinery choking its lower canyons. Today, the mountains are torn by deforestation, volatile elemental devastation, and simmering border hostilities.

sec.b: Rising sharply out of central Kalimdor, the Stonetalon range catches the moisture drifting from the western seas, giving birth to sudden downpours and treacherous, rain-slick sandstone trails. The dominant feature of the lower valleys is the incessant scouring gale known as the Ill Winds, capable of blinding travelers with grit or throwing the careless straight off sheer cliffsides. Higher up, evergreen forests mantle the ridges surrounding Stonetalon Peak, where the night elves tend ancestral barrows and glades, watching over the sacred roosts of wyverns and hippogryphs that nest along Mirkfallon Lake.
sec.t: The Ill Winds and the Peaks

sec.b: The peaceful solitude of the range has been violently disrupted by the arrival of the Venture Company. Setting up sprawling logging camps and digging deep strip mines in Windshear Crag, the goblins—aided by the deranged leper gnome Gerenzo Wrenchwhistle—have clear-cut old-growth timber, blackened the skies with furnace smoke, and poured industrial sludge into the mountain runoff. Their greed has provoked swift retaliation: local shamans from Orgrimmar answered the agonized cries of the mountain spirits, while small Alliance camps stationed nearby fight back against the defilers to protect what remains of the highlands.

To the south lies the Charred Vale, once a blossoming wilderness, now reduced to an ash-covered wasteland churning with rogue fire elementals, black dragonspawn, and harpies. While the peaks were the historic site where the Horde and Alliance forged an uneasy truce during the Third War under the guidance of the mysterious Oracle, current relations are fraying. Renegade Grimtotem tauren operate out of seized encampments, and Darkspear trolls in Malaka'jin clash with Alliance incursions pushing outward from the Barrens and Ashenvale.

faq.a: El príncipe Anduin Wrynn, de diez años de edad, ostenta la corona, pero el gobierno real corre a cargo del Alto Señor Bolvar Fordragón, quien actúa como regente de Ventormenta y comandante supremo de sus fuerzas militares. Bolvar depende enormemente del consejo de la consejera real Lady Katrana Prestor mientras el Rey Varian Wrynn sigue desaparecido.

El Rey Varian desapareció en circunstancias sospechosas mientras viajaba en barco hacia una cumbre diplomática en Theramore. Su desaparición se mantuvo en secreto para preservar la estabilidad, aunque los rumores corren desbocados por las calles y el campo.

La ciudad original fue reducida a cenizas por la Horda orca durante la Primera Guerra. Tras la Segunda Guerra, la Hermandad de los Albañiles, liderada por el maestro artesano Edwin VanCleef, reconstruyó minuciosamente la capital con reluciente piedra blanca gracias al respaldo financiero de la Alianza de Lordaeron.

La Casa de los Nobles acumuló cuantiosas deudas al expandir el ejército de Ventormenta y se negó a pagar a la Hermandad de los Albañiles el salario prometido. Cuando Edwin VanCleef exigió una compensación, los nobles disolvieron el gremio. Los trabajadores se amotinaron, la reina Tiffin Wrynn murió a causa de una pedrada y los canteros desterrados formaron la Hermandad Defias.

Las estatuas honran a los Hijos de Lothar: el general Turalyon, la capitana forestal Alleria Brisaveloz, el archimago Khadgar, Kurdran Martillo Salvaje y Danath Aterratrols. Se erigieron para conmemorar a los héroes que se adentraron a través del Portal Oscuro hacia Draenor con el fin de sellar la fisura y proteger Azeroth.

Ventormenta se conecta con Forjaz mediante el Tren subterráneo, una vía ferroviaria subterránea construida por el Manitas Mayor Gelbin Mekkatorque y encargada por el Rey Magni Barbabronce para facilitar un comercio ágil y rápidos refuerzos militares entre ambas capitales.

La corte real, fuertemente asesorada por Lady Katrana Prestor, insiste en que la ciudad no puede prescindir de tropas apostadas en sus propias murallas y fronteras inmediatas. Con la economía del reino al límite y las disputas políticas paralizando la Casa de los Nobles, los pueblos de la región han sido abandonados a su suerte, dependiendo de milicias locales.

zone:stormwind.s: Ciudad de Ventormenta. La Ciudad de Ventormenta es la bulliciosa capital del Reino de Ventormenta y el principal bastión humano en el mundo tras la caída de Lordaeron. Reconstruida de sus cenizas por la Hermandad de los Albañiles tras su destrucción en la Primera Guerra, sus magníficos distritos de piedra blanca albergan ahora el corazón de la Gran Alianza. No obstante, bajo sus majestuosos canales y catedrales, la ciudad lidia con la repentina desaparición del Rey Varian Wrynn y una creciente intriga política. Fundada hace más de un milenio por los descendientes de los Arathi, Ventormenta se mantuvo durante generaciones como un reino próspero y autosuficiente. Esa época dorada terminó cuando la Horda orca cruzó a raudales El Portal Oscuro, asolando el continente meridional y arrasando la capital por completo en la Primera Guerra. Los supervivientes, liderados por Sir Anduin Lothar, huyeron al norte a través del Mare Magnum hacia Lordaeron. Tras la derrota de la Horda en la Segunda Guerra, el Rey Terenas Menethil II y la Alianza financiaron una reconstrucción total. La Hermandad de los Albañiles reconstruyó minuciosamente la capital para convertirla en Nueva Ventormenta: una resplandeciente ciudadela de pulida piedra blanca y distritos entrelazados por canales.

ang.class:Paladin: The Cathedral of Light serves as the supreme sanctuary of your faith in the south, training knights of the Silver Hand and upholding justice.
ang.class:Rogue: Beneath the pristine stone streets lies the SI:7 headquarters in Old Town, operating the Alliance's primary intelligence and espionage network.
ang.faction:Alliance: As the most populous metropolis within the Grand Alliance, Stormwind provides naval might, spiritual grounding, and vital diplomatic leadership.
ang.race:Dwarf: Through the Deeprun Tram, your kin in the Dwarven District maintain deep commercial ties and forge brotherly military bonds with the human kingdom.
ang.race:Human: Stormwind stands as your people's last great seat of sovereign power following the destruction of Lordaeron, Alterac, and Dalaran in the north.

faq.a: Ten-year-old Prince Anduin Wrynn holds the crown, but actual governance is handled by Highlord Bolvar Fordragon, who acts as Regent of Stormwind and supreme commander of its military. Bolvar relies heavily on the counsel of royal advisor Lady Katrana Prestor while King Varian Wrynn remains missing.
faq.q: Who rules Stormwind right now?

faq.a: King Varian vanished under suspicious circumstances while traveling by ship to a diplomatic summit in Theramore. His disappearance was kept quiet to maintain stability, though rumors run rampant through the streets and countryside.
faq.q: What happened to King Varian Wrynn?

faq.a: The original city was burned to the ground by the Orcish Horde during the First War. After the Second War, the Stonemasons Guild, led by master craftsman Edwin VanCleef, painstakingly rebuilt the capital out of gleaming white stone with financial backing from the Alliance of Lordaeron.
faq.q: Why was the city rebuilt, and by whom?

faq.a: The House of Nobles amassed heavy debts expanding Stormwind's military and refused to pay the Stonemasons Guild their promised wages. When Edwin VanCleef demanded restitution, the nobles disbanded the guild. The workers rioted, Queen Tiffin Wrynn was killed by a thrown rock, and the exiled stonemasons formed the Defias Brotherhood.
faq.q: Why did the stonemasons rebel against the crown?

faq.a: The statues honor the Sons of Lothar: General Turalyon, Ranger Captain Alleria Windrunner, Archmage Khadgar, Kurdran Wildhammer, and Danath Trollbane. They were raised to commemorate the heroes who ventured through the Dark Portal to draenor to seal the rift and protect Azeroth.
faq.q: Who are the giant statues in the Valley of Heroes?

faq.a: Stormwind is connected to Ironforge by the Deeprun Tram, a subterranean railway built by High Tinker Gelbin Mekkatorque and commissioned by King Magni Bronzebeard to enable swift trade and rapid military reinforcement between both capitals.
faq.q: How does Stormwind connect to Ironforge?

faq.a: The royal court, heavily advised by Lady Katrana Prestor, insists the city cannot spare troops from its own walls and immediate borders. With the kingdom's finances stressed and political infighting paralyzing the House of Nobles, regional towns have been abandoned to rely on local militias.
faq.q: Why isn't Stormwind sending troops to help Westfall and Redridge?

text.s: Stormwind City is the bustling capital of the Kingdom of Stormwind and the premier human bastion in the world following the fall of Lordaeron. Rebuilt from ashes by the Stonemasons Guild after its destruction in the First War, its magnificent white stone districts now house the heart of the Grand Alliance. Beneath its majestic canals and cathedrals, however, the city grapples with the sudden disappearance of King Varian Wrynn and brewing political intrigue.

sec.b: Founded over a millennium ago by the descendants of the Arathi, Stormwind stood for generations as a flourishing, self-sufficient realm. That golden era ended when the Orcish Horde poured through the Dark Portal, laying waste to the southern continent and razing the capital to the ground in the First War. Survivors led by Sir Anduin Lothar fled north across the Great Sea to Lordaeron. Following the Horde's defeat in the Second War, King Terenas Menethil II and the Alliance funded a complete reconstruction. The Stonemasons Guild painstakingly rebuilt the capital into New Stormwind—a gleaming citadel of polished white stone and canal-laced boroughs.

Despite its outward majesty, the capital is locked in domestic turmoil. A dispute between the House of Nobles and the Stonemasons Guild over wages left the kingdom paralyzed by debt. The ensuing rioting claimed the life of Queen Tiffin Wrynn and drove the exiled artisans into criminality as the Defias Brotherhood. Now, King Varian Wrynn has mysteriously vanished en route to a diplomatic summit. To avert panic, the crown was placed upon his young son, ten-year-old Prince Anduin Wrynn, with Highlord Bolvar Fordragon ruling as Regent and military commander alongside royal advisor Lady Katrana Prestor.

With Lordaeron overrun by the Scourge, Stormwind has inherited the mantle of humanity's greatest haven and the epicenter of the Alliance. It connects directly to the dwarven kingdom of Ironforge via High Tinker Mekkatorque's subterranean Deeprun Tram. Visitors crossing the Valley of Heroes are greeted by towering statues of the Sons of Lothar who vanished beyond the Dark Portal. From the spiritual beacon of the Cathedral of Light to the arcane studies within the Wizard's Sanctum, Stormwind stands as the supreme hub of trade, culture, and defense across the southern seas.

The discord plaguing the kingdom is no mere administrative accident. Lady Katrana Prestor has covertly guided the decisions of the House of Nobles, inflaming hostility with the stonemasons and willfully neglecting appeals for military relief from outlying settlements like Westfall and Redridge. By whispering poison into the ears of Highlord Bolvar and dividing the realm's attention, she works to keep Stormwind’s legions idle and divided while unrest festering beyond the city walls threatens the throne itself.

zone:stranglethorn.s: Vega de Tuercespina. La Vega de Tuercespina es una jungla densa e indómita que domina el extremo sur de los Reinos del Este, al sur del Bosque del Ocaso. En su día sede del gran imperio Gurubashi, la selva tropical está ahora sembrada de ruinas trol derruidas, bestias salvajes y campamentos rivales de goblins, piratas y soldados. El control de la región se lo disputan con fiereza las tribus locales de trols, Ventura y Cía. y las facciones rivales que intentan afianzarse entre el calor. Durante milenios, el valle estuvo gobernado por el poderoso imperio Gurubashi desde su capital, Zul'Gurub. Ese dominio se hizo añicos cuando unos sacerdotes radicales invocaron a Hakkar el Cazador de Almas, sumiendo a la región en una catastrófica guerra civil. Aunque los Zandalari intervinieron para aplastar el alzamiento del dios de la sangre, el imperio quedó fragmentado sin remedio. Hoy en día, la selva está invadida por facciones sucesoras enfrentadas —destacando los Sangrapellejo en el noroeste y los Machacacráneos en el este—, y ambas masacran con celo a los forasteros para reclamar su hogar ancestral.

ang.class:Hunter: The northern riverbank is home to the famed big-game hunter Hemet Nesingwary, who challenges marksmen to test their mettle tracking the jungle's fiercest raptors, panthers, and crocolisks.
ang.faction:Alliance: Stormwind's historical efforts to conquer and pacify the jungle saddled the kingdom with severe debt, and today its interests are defended only by hard-pressed mutineers at the Rebel Camp.
ang.faction:Horde: Grom'gol Base Camp offers the Horde an indispensable strategic stronghold on the southern continent, supplied directly by zeppelins from Durotar and the Undercity.
ang.profession:Herbalism: The humid canopy nourishes valuable flora, making the riverbanks and coastlines ideal hunting grounds for Wild Steelbloom, Fadeleaf, Goldthorn, and Purple Lotus.
ang.race:Troll: Stranglethorn is the ancestral cradle of the jungle trolls, whose ancient Gurubashi empire fell to civil war after worshipping Hakkar the Soulflayer, driving tribes like the Darkspear across the seas.

faq.a: No single power rules the vale. The jungle is divided among rival jungle troll tribes like the Bloodscalps and Skullsplitters, rogue encampments like Kurzen's Compound, the mercenary Venture Company, and scattered Horde and Alliance military posts. The largest urban settlement is the neutral goblin port of Booty Bay, governed by Baron Revilgaz and the Blackwater Raiders.
faq.q: Who controls Stranglethorn Vale?

faq.a: Booty Bay is a sprawling port city built on the southern bluffs of the Cape of Stranglethorn. Originally a human settlement known as Blackwater Cove, it was captured by trolls and eventually secured by the Steamwheedle Cartel. Today, Baron Revilgaz and Fleet Master Seahorn run it as a neutral trading port connecting travelers to Ratchet across the Great Sea.
faq.q: What is Booty Bay?

faq.a: Colonel Kurzen led an expedition into the jungle on behalf of Stormwind, but his mind fell under the sway of Mai'Zoth, an ogre mage wielding a powerful relic called the Mind's Eye. Kurzen became increasingly erratic and despotic, forcing loyal soldiers like Lieutenant Doren to break away and form the Rebel Camp to stop him.
faq.q: Why did Colonel Kurzen go rogue?

faq.a: Zul'Gurub is the ancient, temple-studded capital city of the Gurubashi Empire nestled in northeastern Stranglethorn. It was the epicenter of the civil war that ended the empire fifteen centuries ago, after radical priests summoned the blood god Hakkar the Soulflayer. Though long abandoned to vines and ruins, dark rituals continue to threaten its halls.
faq.q: What is Zul'Gurub?

faq.a: The Stone of the Tides is a legendary relic from ancient Gurubashi history discovered on the coast by a troll warrior. It granted its bearer dominion over water and elemental summons akin to a powerful mage, earning the wielder the title 'Tidebearer'. However, it bore a curse that caused the wielder to slowly fade from the physical realm, leading each bearer to walk into the sea and vanish.
faq.q: What was the Stone of the Tides?

faq.a: Travelers can walk south across the river border from Duskwood into northern Stranglethorn. The Horde maintains direct zeppelin towers connecting Grom'gol Base Camp to Durotar and Tirisfal Glades. Travelers from Kalimdor can also board the regular merchant vessel sailing between Ratchet in the Barrens and Booty Bay.
faq.q: How do I travel to Stranglethorn Vale?

text.s: Stranglethorn Vale is an untamed, dense jungle dominating the southern tip of the Eastern Kingdoms, south of Duskwood. Once the seat of the great Gurubashi Empire, the rainforest is now strewn with crumbling troll ruins, savage beasts, and competing encampments of goblins, pirates, and soldiers. Control of the region is hotly contested by local troll tribes, the Venture Company, and rival factions carving out footholds in the heat.

sec.b: For millennia, the vale was governed by the mighty Gurubashi Empire from their capital city, Zul'Gurub. That dominion shattered when radical priests summoned Hakkar the Soulflayer, plunging the region into a catastrophic civil war. Though the Zandalari stepped in to crush the blood god's uprising, the empire splintered beyond repair. Today, the jungle is overrun by warring successor factions—most prominently the Bloodscalp in the northwest and the Skullsplitter in the east—both zealously slaughtering outsiders to reclaim their ancestral home.

Where ancient ruins fall silent, commercial greed fills the void. At the southern tip lies Booty Bay, a bustling haven carved out by the Steamwheedle Cartel and run by the Blackwater Raiders under Baron Revilgaz. The port serves as the prime hub of southern commerce and seafaring transport, though it is perpetually besieged by the rival Bloodsail Buccaneers anchored along the coast. Further inland, the Venture Company aggressively strips the jungle of timber and mines the hills for rare singing crystals.

Stranglethorn Vale serves as one of the most volatile borderlands in the world. The Horde commands Grom'gol Base Camp on the western coast, tethered by goblin zeppelins to Durotar and Tirisfal Glades, while Alliance loyalists operate out of the Rebel Camp to track down the rogue Colonel Kurzen. Amid the dense foliage, the legendary hunter Hemet Nesingwary leads daring big-game expeditions, drawing wanderers into perilous encounters with prowling panthers, enormous apes, and enemy soldiers.

Not all threats in northern Stranglethorn are wild beasts. Colonel Kurzen, once a decorated commander dispatched by Stormwind, went mad within the brush and established a tyrannical mercenary redoubt. In truth, Kurzen's mind was ensnared through the sorcery of the Mind's Eye, an artifact wielded by the ogre mage Mai'Zoth of the nearby Mosh'Ogg Ogre Mound, driving the expedition into utter insanity and prompting his former men to form the breakaway Rebel Camp.

zone:swampofsorrows.s: Pantano de las Penas. El Pantano de las Penas es un humedal turbio y salobre encajonado entre el Paso de la Muerte y las áridas Tierras Devastadas. Antaño la extensión septentrional de la antigua Ciénaga Negra, sus cenagales cubiertos de costras de sal albergan una fauna peligrosa, dragonantes verdes y las ruinas del Templo de Atal'Hakkar sumergidas bajo la Charca de Lágrimas. Aunque la Horda mantiene la guarnición fortificada de Rocal, la Alianza carece de refugio seguro en la ciénaga, lo que deja estas tierras salvajes en gran medida indómitas. Mucho antes de la llegada de la Horda orca, estas marismas formaban la mitad norte de un enorme humedal conocido como la Ciénaga Negra. Tras la caída del Imperio Gurubashi, los fanáticos trols Atal'ai huyeron a la ciénaga para erigir el Templo de Atal'Hakkar con la intención de invocar a su sanguinario loa, Hakkar el Cazador de Almas. Al presentir la catástrofe, el Aspecto Ysera desató sus poderes y ahogó la pirámide maldita bajo las aguas de la Charca de Lágrimas. Se apostaron guardianes del Vuelo Verde liderados por Eranikus para vigilar con celo la estructura anegada. Cuando el cataclismo del Portal Oscuro calcinó más tarde el sur del pantano convirtiéndolo en Las Tierras Devastadas, este cenagal septentrional recibió su lamentable nombre actual.
