ang.faction:Alliance: Without an outpost to rally behind, traveling through the swamp is an isolated, hostile venture requiring careful preparation from Darkshire or Nethergarde Keep.
ang.faction:Horde: Stonard serves as your vital forward redoubt in the southern continent, hosting direct wyvern routes to Kargath, Flame Crest, and Grom'gol Base Camp.
ang.profession:Blacksmithing: Tough adventurers can gather iron, gold, mithril, and truesilver along the mountainous crags framing the swamp's northern and southern edges.
ang.profession:Herbalism: The marsh is one of the few places in Azeroth rich in blindweed, alongside generous growths of liferoot, fadeleaf, and stranglekelp.
ang.race:Troll: The sunken ruins of Atal'Hakkar stand as a dire reminder of the dark blood magic that fractured the Gurubashi Empire and drew the wrath of the Dragon Aspects.

faq.a: The most common overland route leads east from Darkshire in Duskwood, through the perilous haunted defile of Deadwind Pass, and straight down into the marsh. Alternatively, travelers coming from the south can walk north along the main road out of the Blasted Lands.
al: how to get to swamp of sorrows
faq.q: How do I reach the Swamp of Sorrows?

faq.a: Centuries ago, the Atal'ai priesthood tried to summon Hakkar the Soulflayer into Azeroth. Ysera, the Dragon Aspect of the Green Flight, discovered their demonic blood rites and drowned the entire temple into the bog to avert the disaster, leaving behind green dragonspawn to guard the submerged halls.
faq.q: Why is the Temple of Atal'Hakkar underwater?

faq.a: Stonard was one of the first settlements built by the Orcish Horde after crossing through the Dark Portal during the First War. Though ravaged during the fighting, it was recently reclaimed and rebuilt under Thrall's orders to anchor Horde logistics near the Blasted Lands.
faq.q: What is Stonard?

faq.a: No. The Alliance maintains no towns, guards, or flight paths in the Swamp of Sorrows. Alliance adventurers operating in the area must base themselves out of Darkshire in Duskwood to the west or Nethergarde Keep in the Blasted Lands to the south.
faq.q: Are there any Alliance settlements here?

faq.a: They are draenei who were stranded on Azeroth following the collapse of the Dark Portal. Severed from their world, most went mad from despair and turned into hostile Lost Ones. A small pocket of sane Broken exiles took refuge in the northwest at the Harborage, choosing neutral survival over mindless rage.
faq.q: Who are the strange mutated humanoids in the swamp?

faq.a: Sorrowmurk is the dense tract of marshland directly east of the Pool of Tears. It serves as a patrol ground for elite green dragonspawn and whelps who violently turn away mortals to safeguard the secrets of the Sunken Temple.
faq.q: What is Sorrowmurk?

text.s: The Swamp of Sorrows is a murky, brackish wetland tucked between Deadwind Pass and the arid Blasted Lands. Once the northern expanse of the ancient Black Morass, its salt-crusted bogs are home to dangerous wildlife, green dragonspawn, and the ruined Temple of Atal'Hakkar sunken beneath the Pool of Tears. While the Horde maintains the fortified garrison of Stonard, the Alliance has no safe haven within the mire, leaving the wilderness largely untamed.

sec.b: Long before the coming of the Orcish Horde, these marshes formed the northern half of an enormous wetlands known as the Black Morass. Following the shattering of the Gurubashi Empire, the fanatical Atal'ai trolls fled into the mire to erect the Temple of Atal'Hakkar, intending to summon their bloodthirsty loa, Hakkar the Soulflayer. Sensing the catastrophe, the Aspect Ysera unleashed her powers, drowning the cursed pyramid beneath the waters of the Pool of Tears. Green dragonflight guardians led by Eranikus were stationed to vigilantly watch over the drowned structure. When the Dark Portal's cataclysm later scorched the southern morass into the Blasted Lands, this northern fen earned its current sorrowful name.

Stonard serves as the primary civilized foothold in the swamp. Originally established during the First War alongside the now-ruined settlements of Rockard and Kyross, the outpost was rebuilt under Thrall to serve as the Horde's southernmost staging ground in the Eastern Kingdoms. Beyond Stonard's palisades, strange wanderers roam the fen. A group of draenei stragglers stranded on Azeroth succumbed to homesickness and madness, degenerating into feral Lost Ones. However, a small enclave of lucid Broken exiles persists at the Harborage, wary but willing to trade peacefully with travelers.

Surviving the swamp requires constant vigilance against its predatory wildlife. Deep bogs hide lunging crocolisks, venomous spiders, prowling swamp jaguars, and wandering bog beasts encrusted with marsh debris. Coastal caverns and the Misty Reed Strand crawl with vicious murlocs, while the salt-laden tide creeps continually inland, preserving rotten logs in thick briny crusts. Farther east lies Sorrowmurk, where aggressive elite dragonspawn fiercely guard the approaches to the Sunken Temple, attacking anyone who strays near their vigil.

faq.a: Tras la devastación de Nordrassil al final de la Tercera Guerra, los elfos de la noche perdieron su inmortalidad. El archidruida Fandral Corzocelada instó al Círculo de los Ancestros y a los druidas del Círculo Cenarion a plantar un nuevo Árbol del Mundo en el mar, con la esperanza de recuperar lo que su pueblo había perdido.

Nordrassil otorgaba originalmente la inmortalidad gracias a la bendición de Nozdormu, el Atemporal. Cuando se alzó Teldrassil, Nozdormu consideró que el deseo de los elfos de la noche era arrogante y se negó a conceder su bendición al nuevo árbol.

Los viajeros deben dirigirse a través de Darnassus hacia el portal rosa de Los Jardines del Templo, que los transporta a la Aldea Rut'theran, en la base del tronco. Desde Rut'theran, un barco navega a través del mar hacia Auberdine, en la costa de Costa Oscura, además de haber rutas de hipogrifos disponibles.

Toda la zona se asienta sobre las ramas vivas y la madera de un descomunal Árbol del Mundo, en lugar de roca continental natural. Al no existir una corteza subterránea pétrea, no se forman vetas de metal ni yacimientos de mineral, aunque las hierbas florecen en gran abundancia.

Una siniestra presencia ha comenzado a filtrarse en las raíces no bendecidas de Teldrassil. La enfermedad ha corrompido el agua y la flora locales, empujando a los pacíficos maderizos y a la tribu fúrbolg Tuercepinos a una agresión frenética, mientras los reductos de sátiros cultivan activamente la corrupción.

Cañada Umbría es un valle resguardado y apartado en las ramas orientales de Teldrassil que rodea al gran árbol Aldrassil. Sirve como un santuario pacífico donde los jóvenes elfos de la noche comienzan su instrucción antes de aventurarse en el resto del mundo.

zone:teldrassil.s: Teldrassil. Teldrassil, que significa «Corona de la Tierra», es un nuevo y gigantesco Árbol del Mundo alzado frente a la costa noroeste de Kalimdor. Creado por los druidas tras la Tercera Guerra, sus colosales ramas albergan una vasta naturaleza en penumbra y la capital de los elfos de la noche, Darnassus. Sin embargo, bajo su apacible fronda iluminada por la luna, ha comenzado a agitarse una insidiosa corrupción. Teldrassil no es un simple árbol; es un ecosistema elevado que se alza majestuoso en las aguas del Mar Velado. Sus gigantescas ramas sostienen colinas onduladas, ríos alimentados por el rocío matinal, lagos brumosos y densos claros ancestrales. En su extremo occidental se encuentra Darnassus, la gran capital de los kaldorei. En la base de su monumental tronco descansa la Aldea Rut'theran, conectada con la copa superior mediante un portal místico y convertida en el puerto principal de la isla.

ang.class:Druid: With Malfurion trapped in the Emerald Dream, Archdruid Fandral Staghelm leads the Cenarion Circle here, though many druids worry that Teldrassil was raised in haste.
ang.faction:Alliance: Teldrassil serves as the northernmost bastion of the Alliance in Kalimdor, anchoring naval communication and trade between Darnassus and mainland kingdoms.
ang.profession:Herbalism: Lacking minerals and ore entirely, the tree's verdant canopy makes up for it by acting as a paradise for gatherers of Peacebloom, Silverleaf, and Earthroot.
ang.race:NightElf: This massive tree is your people's fresh beginning after the devastation of Mount Hyjal, but the absence of the Aspects' blessings makes defending it an urgent duty.

faq.a: After Nordrassil was devastated at the end of the Third War, the night elves lost their immortality. Archdruid Fandral Staghelm pushed the Circle of Ancients and Cenarion druids to plant a new World Tree in the sea, aiming to restore what their people had lost.
faq.q: Why was Teldrassil grown?

faq.a: Nordrassil originally granted immortality because Nozdormu, the Timeless One, blessed it. When Teldrassil was raised, Nozdormu judged the night elves' desire as arrogant and refused to bestow his blessing upon the new tree.
faq.q: Why didn't Teldrassil restore night elf immortality?

faq.a: Travelers must head through Darnassus to the pink portal in the Temple Gardens, which transports them down to Rut'theran Village at the trunk's base. From Rut'theran, a ship sails across the sea to Auberdine on the mainland of Darkshore, alongside available hippogryph routes.
faq.q: How do you leave Teldrassil?

faq.a: The entire zone is situated atop the living branches and wood of a colossal World Tree rather than natural continental rock. Because there are no stony subterranean crusts, no metal veins or ore deposits form here, though herbs flourish in great abundance.
faq.q: Why are there no mining nodes in Teldrassil?

faq.a: A sinister presence has begun to seep into Teldrassil's unblessed roots. Sickness has corrupted the local water and flora, driving peaceful timberlings and the Gnarlpine furbolg tribe into frenzied aggression, while remnants of satyrs actively cultivate the taint.
faq.q: What is causing the furbolgs and beasts to turn mad?

faq.a: Shadowglen is a sheltered, secluded vale on the eastern boughs of Teldrassil surrounding the great tree Aldrassil. It serves as a peaceful sanctuary where young night elves begin their training before venturing into the wider world.
faq.q: What is Shadowglen?

text.s: Teldrassil, meaning 'Crown of the Earth', is a gargantuan new World Tree raised off Kalimdor's northwest coast. Grown by the druids in the wake of the Third War, its colossal boughs support an entire twilit wilderness and the night elf capital of Darnassus. Yet beneath its tranquil, moonlit canopy, a creeping corruption has begun to stir.

sec.b: Teldrassil is not merely a tree; it is an elevated ecosystem standing tall amidst the waters of the Veiled Sea. Its gargantuan limbs support rolling hills, flowing rivers fed by morning dew, misty lakes, and dense ancient glades. At its western edge sits Darnassus, the grand capital of the kaldorei. At the base of its monumental trunk lies Rut'theran Village, connected to the crown above by a mystical gateway and serving as the island's primary harbor.

Following the sacrifice of Nordrassil during the Third War and the mysterious disappearance of Shan'do Malfurion Stormrage into the Emerald Dream, Archdruid Fandral Staghelm convinced the Circle of Ancients to grow a replacement. Staghelm hoped to restore the kaldorei to their lost immortality. However, Nozdormu and the Dragon Aspects deemed the effort hubristic and withheld their blessings. Without their vital warding, Teldrassil's growth has suffered from unnatural flaws.

Despite its outward majesty, the nascent World Tree harbors a dark sickness. The local wildlife has turned violent: peaceful furbolg tribes have fallen into madness, twisted grells multiply in the barrows, and vile satyrs work dark rites in shadows like Fel Rock. Down upon the shores of Darkshore, sea giants, threshers, and turtles beach themselves to flee the tainted waters around the tree. Naturalists and sentinels now labor frantically across the boughs to identify the shadow slowly strangling their new home.

zone:thousandneedles.s: Las Mil Agujas. Las Mil Agujas es un extenso cañón de escarpados pilares de arenisca y salinas abrasadas por el sol en el sur de Kalimdor. Las tribus tauren se aferran a asentamientos en lo alto de imponentes mesetas para escapar de las agresivas manadas de centauros, mientras que manitas gnomos y goblins conducen coches cohete de alta velocidad por el lecho marino seco de El Desierto de Sal. Antes de que el Gran Cataclismo destrozara el antiguo Kalimdor, este territorio era un frondoso cañón fluvial alimentado por vías fluviales interiores que desembocaban en el mar. El cataclismo desgarró el continente, elevando el lecho del río por encima del nivel freático y alterando su curso hasta que solo quedaron piedra seca y agujas de arenisca. Hoy en día, decenas de esbeltas columnas cilíndricas se alzan desde el fondo del cañón como un bosque petrificado. Los tauren se asentaron en las cumbres, tendiendo precarios puentes de cuerda entre los picos para establecer aldeas fuera del alcance de los hostiles merodeadores centauros que patrullan el sombrío fondo del cañón.

ang.faction:Horde: The Great Lift links the Barrens to your stronghold at Freewind Post, serving as a strategic southern boundary against centaur clans and rebel tauren.
ang.profession:Engineering: The salt flats are a pilgrimage site for tinkerers looking to study rocket fuel, vehicle parts, and high-speed propulsion at the Mirage Raceway.
ang.race:Gnome: The Mirage Raceway in the Shimmering Flats is your faction's premier chance to demonstrate the precision and elegance of gnomish engineering over shoddy goblin contraptions.
ang.race:Tauren: Freewind Post stands as a reminder of how high your people had to climb to escape centaur slaughter, and a staging ground against the treacherous Grimtotem at Darkcloud Pinnacle.

faq.a: The zone is named after the dozens of massive, cylindrical sandstone spires that erupt from the canyon bottom. Originally carved by rushing river currents before the Great Sundering, these geological towers now resemble a forest of giant needles.
al: why is it called thousand needles
faq.q: How did Thousand Needles get its name?

faq.a: Travelers take the Great Lift, an immense double-car elevator operated by Horde guards on the southern border of the Barrens. Stepping off the edge is fatal, so waiting for the platform is essential. Alliance travelers can also hike in from the west via Thalanaar in Feralas.
al: how to get to thousand needles
faq.q: How do you get down into Thousand Needles from the Barrens?

faq.a: Centaur warbands once pushed the nomadic tauren nearly to extinction. Building outposts like Freewind Post atop inaccessible stone pillars kept them safe from ground charges. They connected the mesas using wooden suspension bridges, allowing high-altitude travel above the predators and raiders below.
faq.q: Why do the tauren live on top of the mesas?

faq.a: The Mirage Raceway is an engineering proving ground on the Shimmering Flats salt pan. Gnomish and goblin tinkerers run experimental rocket-propelled racecars across the flat salt bed to settle their ongoing rivalry over which race builds the finest machinery.
faq.q: What is the Mirage Raceway?

faq.a: The Grimtotem clan occupies Darkcloud Pinnacle, a fortified cluster of spires directly opposing Freewind Post. Unlike the rest of the tauren tribes who pledged to the Horde, the Grimtotem actively attack other tauren and conspire to seize dominance over the mesas.
faq.q: What is the Grimtotem presence in the canyon?

faq.a: The Shimmering Flats are a vast, dried lakebed east of the canyon mesas. The salt crust formed when the ancient inland sea evaporated after the Sundering. The searing heat, blinding white salt, and harsh predators make it an inhospitable desert used mainly for high-speed vehicular testing.
faq.q: What are the Shimmering Flats?

text.s: Thousand Needles is a sprawling canyon of sheer sandstone pillars and sunbaked salt pans in southern Kalimdor. Tauren tribes cling to settlements atop towering mesas to escape aggressive centaur packs, while gnomish and goblin tinkerers run high-speed rocket cars across the dried-up seabed of the Shimmering Flats.

sec.b: Before the Great Sundering shattered ancient Kalimdor, this territory was a lush river canyon fed by inland waterways flowing out toward the sea. The cataclysm tore the continent apart, thrusting the riverbed above the water table and altering the river's path until only dry stone and sandstone spires remained. Today, dozens of slender cylindrical columns rise from the canyon floor like a petrified forest. Tauren settled on the summits, stringing precarious rope bridges between peaks to establish villages out of reach of the hostile centaur marauders patrolling the shadow-draped canyon floor below.

Atop the needle-like spires, life is far from peaceful. At Freewind Post, tauren loyal to the Horde contend not only with predatory wind serpents and wyverns from Highperch, but also with their treacherous kin: the militant Grimtotem clan entrenched at Darkcloud Pinnacle. Cliffwatcher Longhorn oversees the defense of the plateau, seeking bold fighters to strike at Grimtotem agitators and secure the fragile bridges linking the peaks. To the north, the enormous mechanical winches of the Great Lift carry travelers down from the southern Barrens, though crossing the canyon floor remains a deadly gambit.

To the southeast, the canyon walls peel back into the Shimmering Flats, an enormous, desiccated salt pan sitting below sea level. In this harsh, blinding white expanse, gnomes and goblins maintain an uneasy neutrality around the Mirage Raceway. Rival engineers Pozzik and Fizzle Brassbolts race experimental rocket cars across the hard salt to settle which race possesses technological superiority. The pit stop attracts scoundrels, swindlers like Kravel Koalbeard, and hunters hunting the hardy scorpions, turtles, and basilisks that roam the searing basin.

faq.a: El Gran Jefe Cairne Pezuña de Sangre gobierna Cima del Trueno y lidera a las tribus tauren unidas. Venerado por su sabiduría, paciencia y colosal fuerza, Cairne fundó la ciudad tras aliarse con la Horda de Thrall y expulsar a los centauros de Mulgore.

Los visitantes que llegan a pie o a lomos de un kodo deben montar en inmensos elevadores de plataformas de madera situados en los lados suroeste y noreste de la meseta central. Como alternativa, la ciudad cuenta con un nido de jinetes del viento con rutas de vuelo por todo Kalimdor.

Los siglos de existencia nómada estuvieron marcados por implacables ataques relámpago de agresivos clanes centauros. Los escarpados acantilados de los riscos de Mulgore proporcionan una defensa natural, protegiendo las viviendas, forjas y ancianos sagrados de los tauren de las emboscadas terrestres y permitiéndoles asentarse permanentemente en paz.

La ciudad se extiende por una meseta central (dividida en niveles inferior, medio y superior) rodeada por tres mesetas exteriores. El Alto de los Cazadores está dedicado a guerreros, cazadores y pabellones de rastreo. El Alto de los Ancestros es el hogar de druidas, sabios y la facción Tótem Siniestro. El Alto de los Espíritus alberga santuarios dedicados a la Madre Tierra, instructores de chamanes, sacerdotes y magos, y las cavernosas Pozas de las Visiones.

Las Pozas de las Visiones son cavernas subterráneas sagradas ocultas bajo el Alto de los Espíritus. Videntes tauren, caminantes espirituales y practicantes de lo arcano se reúnen en estas aguas tranquilas y envueltas en niebla para comulgar con los elementos e interpretar presagios sobre el futuro de su pueblo.

Magatha Tótem Siniestro es la matriarca y Vieja Bruja del formidable clan Tótem Siniestro. Aunque reside en el Alto de los Ancestros y participa aparentemente en el consejo de Cairne, es ferozmente tradicional, desconfía de los forasteros y desafía en secreto la postura tolerante de la tribu Pezuña de Sangre hacia la Horda.

zone:thunderbluff.s: Cima del Trueno. Cima del Trueno es la magnífica capital de los tauren, erigida en lo alto de mesetas de roca roja azotadas por el viento que se alzan sobre las praderas de Mulgore. Fundada por el Gran Jefe Cairne Pezuña de Sangre tras unir a las tribus nómadas con la ayuda de la Nueva Horda, sirve como corazón cultural, espiritual y mercantil de su pueblo. Conectada por puentes colgantes de cuerda y elevadores de madera, la ciudad ofrece protección frente a los merodeadores centauros y un santuario pacífico para los viajeros de todo Kalimdor. Durante incontables generaciones, los tauren vivieron como nómadas errantes por Kalimdor, enfrascados en una brutal lucha por la supervivencia contra voraces tribus de centauros. Esa era desesperada llegó a su fin durante la Tercera Guerra, cuando Cairne Pezuña de Sangre unió fuerzas con el Jefe de Guerra Thrall. Juntos, orcos y tauren repelieron los asaltos de los centauros y aseguraron los exuberantes pastos de Mulgore. Para proteger su futuro, Cairne condujo a las tribus aliadas a la seguridad de estos bastiones naturales de piedra, fundando Cima del Trueno como el primer hogar unificado y permanente que los tauren habían tenido en siglos.

ang.class:Druid: Elder Rise serves as the Horde's supreme sanctuary of nature magic, headed by Archdruid Hamuul Runetotem, the first tauren druid taught in thousands of years.
ang.class:Shaman: Spirit Rise and the subterranean Pools of Vision provide a serene nexus where the elemental spirits and spirits of tauren ancestors are revered and heard.
ang.faction:Horde: Far more tranquil and spiritual than the harsh battlements of Orgrimmar, Thunder Bluff serves as the pastoral anchor of the New Horde's southern influence in Kalimdor.
ang.race:Tauren: Thunder Bluff represents the hard-won unity and rebirth of your people after generations of nomadic wandering and centaur harassment under High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof.

faq.a: High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof rules Thunder Bluff and leads the united tauren tribes. Revered for his wisdom, patience, and mighty strength, Cairne founded the city after allying with Thrall's Horde and driving the centaur from Mulgore.
faq.q: Who rules Thunder Bluff?

faq.a: Visitors arriving on foot or kodo must ride massive wooden platform elevators located on the southwestern and northeastern sides of the central mesa. Alternatively, the city features a Wind Rider roost with flight paths across Kalimdor.
faq.q: How do you get up to Thunder Bluff?

faq.a: Centuries of nomadic existence were marked by relentless hit-and-run attacks from aggressive centaur clans. The sheer cliffs of Mulgore's bluffs provide natural defense, shielding the tauren's dwellings, smiths, and sacred elders from ground ambushes and allowing them to permanently settle in peace.
faq.q: Why did the tauren build on high mesas instead of the ground?

faq.a: The city spans a central mesa (divided into lower, middle, and high tiers) surrounded by three outer mesas. Hunter Rise is dedicated to warriors, hunters, and tracking lodges. Elder Rise is home to druids, wisemen, and the Grimtotem faction. Spirit Rise holds shrines to the Earth Mother, trainers of shamans, priests, and mages, and the cavernous Pools of Vision.
faq.q: What are the different rises of the city?

faq.a: The Pools of Vision are sacred underground caverns tucked beneath Spirit Rise. Tauren seers, spiritwalkers, and practitioners of the arcane gather in these quiet, mist-shrouded waters to commune with the elements and interpret omens regarding the future of their people.
faq.q: What are the Pools of Vision?

faq.a: Magatha Grimtotem is the matriarch and Elder Crone of the formidable Grimtotem clan. While she resides on Elder Rise and outwardly participates in Cairne's council, she is fiercely traditional, distrusting outsiders and quietly challenging the Bloodhoof tribe's soft stance toward the Horde.
faq.q: Who is Magatha Grimtotem?

text.s: Thunder Bluff is the magnificent capital city of the tauren, perched atop windswept red-rock mesas rising above the grasslands of Mulgore. Founded by High Chieftain Cairne Bloodhoof after uniting the nomadic tribes with the aid of the New Horde, it serves as the cultural, spiritual, and mercantile heart of his people. Connected by swaying rope bridges and wooden lifts, the city offers safety from centaur marauders and a peaceful sanctuary for travelers across Kalimdor.

sec.b: For countless generations, the tauren lived as nomadic wanderers across Kalimdor, locked in a brutal struggle for survival against ravenous centaur tribes. That desperate era ended during the Third War when Cairne Bloodhoof joined forces with Warchief Thrall. Together, the orcs and tauren broke the centaur assaults and secured the lush pastures of Mulgore. To protect their future, Cairne led the allied tribes to the safety of these natural stone bastions, founding Thunder Bluff as the first unified, permanent home the tauren had possessed in centuries.

Spanning several high mesas linked by suspended rope bridges, Thunder Bluff seamlessly blends natural architecture with tauren practicality. The central bluffs host the bustling markets, bank, inn, and towering Wind Rider roost, while three specialized mesas branch out across the abyss. Hunter Rise serves the city's scouts and trackers; Elder Rise hosts lorekeepers and the Cenarion Circle under Archdruid Hamuul Runetotem; and Spirit Rise is devoted to spiritual communion, sheltering shamans, priests, and the mysterious subterranean caverns known as the Pools of Vision.

While Cairne Bloodhoof commands immense respect from almost every tribe, governing a recently settled, proud people is not without friction. Notably, the Grimtotem tribe—led by the shrewd and sharp-tongued Elder Crone Magatha Grimtotem—maintains a brooding presence on Elder Rise. Magatha openly questions Cairne's conciliatory methods and allegiance to the foreign races of the Horde. Though peace endures beneath the chieftain's watchful gaze, ideological rifts murmur among the council fires above the plains.

faq.a: Durante la Tercera Guerra, el príncipe Arthas y la Plaga desataron la peste de la no-muerte por todo el Reino de Lordaeron. La plaga mágica no solo envenenó a la población, sino también la tierra, los árboles y el agua misma, dejando los claros en un estado eterno de inquietante y enfermiza decadencia.

Los Renegados son no-muertos que se liberaron de la dominación telepática del Rey Exánime tras la batalla del Monte Hyjal, eligiendo seguir a Lady Sylvanas Brisaveloz por propia voluntad. La Plaga que merodea por las haciendas y ruinas sigue formada por esclavos desalmados sometidos a las órdenes del Rey Exánime.

Pertenecen a la Cruzada Escarlata, una facción escindida e inflexible de antiguos paladines de la Mano de Plata y supervivientes. Convencidos de que todos los no-muertos son abominaciones irredimibles que deben purificarse a espada y fuego, ejecutan tanto a los autómatas sin mente como a los Renegados con libre albedrío con odio fanático.

La región recibe su nombre en honor al guardián de los titanes Tyr. Según la leyenda, Tyr cayó en combate contra horrores arcanos en este claro. En la antigua lengua vrykul, «la caída de Tyr» evolucionó hasta convertirse en «Tirisfal», y la mano de plata del guardián se convirtió en un emblema profundamente arraigado en la mitología humana primigenia.

Los Renegados recién despertados emergen de las criptas del Sepulcro Sombrío, en el interior de Camposanto, una población enclaustrada situada en el suroeste de Tirisfal. Allí, administradores y ejecutores evalúan si los muertos resucitados poseen la cordura y la lealtad necesarias para servir a la Dama Oscura.

Una gran torre de zepelines operada por goblins se alza en la ladera al sur de Rémol, justo a las afueras de las Ruinas de Lordaeron. Estas aeronaves proporcionan transporte directo y regular cruzando los mares hasta Orgrimmar en Kalimdor y el Campamento Grom'Gol en la Vega de Tuercespina.

zone:tirisfal.s: Claros de Tirisfal. Los Claros de Tirisfal son el sobrecogedor territorio septentrional de Lordaeron, que ahora constituye el corazón de los dominios de Lady Sylvanas Brisaveloz y los Renegados. Bajo cielos apestados y ramas putrefactas yacen mansiones derruidas, criptas inertes y la inmensa capital subterránea de Entrañas. Rodeado por las huestes sin voluntad de la Plaga y fervientes cruzados Escarlata, es un peligroso reino donde no-muertos provistos de libre albedrío luchan por sobrevivir. Antaño la fértil cuna de la humanidad, los Claros de Tirisfal se han marchitado bajo la maldición de la plaga del Rey Exánime. El sol rara vez atraviesa la turbia penumbra, proyectando una eterna y enfermiza palidez sobre bosques agonizantes, huertos de calabazas abandonados y frías colinas costeras. Aunque aún perduran vestigios de viejas haciendas como los Molinos de Agamand y la Hacienda Balnir, la mayoría de sus antiguos amos acabaron en fosas comunes o se alzaron como no-muertos inquietos. A pesar de la devastación, una oscura resistencia impregna la campiña, anclada por poblaciones como Rémol y el enclaustrado santuario de Camposanto, donde los Renegados recién despertados aprenden a sobrellevar su segunda vida.

ang.class:Priest: Historic holy grounds like Faol's Rest—the tomb of Archbishop Alonsus Faol, founder of the Silver Hand—lie here, warped by death and contested between zealots and Shadow priests.
ang.faction:Alliance: For the surviving nations of the Alliance, Tirisfal is a tragic monument to Lordaeron's fall, filled with the desecrated tombs of former brothers and sisters in faith.
ang.faction:Horde: Tirisfal is the Horde's vital bastion in the northern Eastern Kingdoms, anchoring diplomatic ties with the Forsaken while warding off human extremists and the Scourge.
ang.race:Undead: This is your ancestral homeland twice over: the kingdom you built in life, and the precarious sanctuary you must defend in undeath under Lady Sylvanas.

faq.a: During the Third War, Prince Arthas and the Scourge unleashed the Plague of Undeath across the Kingdom of Lordaeron. The magical blight poisoned not only the populace, but the soil, trees, and water itself, leaving the glades in an eternal state of eerie, sickly decay.
faq.q: Why is the sky green and the land rotting?

faq.a: The Forsaken are undead who broke free from the Lich King's telepathic domination after the Battle of Mount Hyjal, choosing to follow Lady Sylvanas Windrunner with their own free will. The Scourge roaming the farmsteads and ruins remain mindless slaves bound to the Lich King's commands.
faq.q: What is the difference between the Forsaken and the Scourge here?

faq.a: They belong to the Scarlet Crusade, an uncompromising splinter order of former Silver Hand paladins and survivors. Convinced all undead are irredeemable abominations that must be purified by sword and fire, they execute both mindless thralls and free-willed Forsaken with fanatical hatred.
faq.q: Who are the red-armored soldiers attacking travelers?

faq.a: The region is named in honor of the titan keeper Tyr. According to legend, Tyr fell in battle against eldritch horrors in this glade. In the ancient vrykul tongue, 'Tyr's Fall' evolved into the name 'Tirisfal,' and the keeper's silver hand became an emblem woven deeply into early human mythology.
faq.q: Where does the name Tirisfal come from?

faq.a: Newly awakened Forsaken emerge from the crypts of the Shadow Grave inside Deathknell, a cloistered town nestled in southwestern Tirisfal. There, administrators and executors evaluate whether the risen dead possess the sanity and loyalty required to serve the Dark Lady.
faq.q: Where do newly awakened Forsaken begin their journey?

faq.a: A large goblin-operated zeppelin tower sits on the hillside south of Brill, right outside the Ruins of Lordaeron. These airships provide direct, regular transit across the seas to Orgrimmar in Kalimdor and Grom'gol Base Camp in Stranglethorn Vale.
faq.q: How do travelers leave Tirisfal for other continents?

text.s: Tirisfal Glades is the haunting northern territory of Lordaeron, now serving as the heartland of Lady Sylvanas Windrunner and the Forsaken. Beneath blighted skies and rotting boughs lie fallen manors, dormant crypts, and the vast underground capital of the Undercity. Surrounded by mindless Scourge and zealous Scarlet crusaders, it is a perilous realm where free-willed undead carve out their survival.

sec.b: Once the fertile cradle of humanity, Tirisfal Glades has withered beneath the curse of the Lich King's plague. The sun rarely penetrates the murky gloom, casting an eternal sickly pale over dying woods, neglected pumpkin patches, and cold coastal hills. While remnants of old farmsteads like the Agamand Mills and Balnir Farmstead remain, their former masters have largely been swept into mass graves or risen as restless dead. Despite the devastation, a dark resilience permeates the countryside, anchored by towns like Brill and the cloistered sanctuary of Deathknell, where freshly awakened Forsaken learn to endure their second life.

Though Lady Sylvanas claims dominion over the region from the subterranean Ruins of Lordaeron, the Forsaken remain embattled on all sides. Residual Scourge thralls still infest hollows, fields, and dilapidated crypts, entirely subservient to the frozen throne of Northrend. To the east, the fanatical Scarlet Crusade has made northern Tirisfal its primary bastion, operating out of the Scarlet Monastery. Zealously devoted to the extermination of every undead creature, living and unliving alike, their outposts and patrols wage constant guerrilla warfare against Forsaken scouts and civilian travelers.

Long before human kingdoms crowned their first monarchs, the Glades bore an ancient legacy. In the ancient tongue of the vrykul, 'Tirisfal' translates to 'Tyr's Fall,' christened after the heroic titan keeper Tyr fought to the death against colossal cosmic horrors. In subsequent eras, high elven exiles briefly tried to settle these woods before shadowy energies deep beneath the earth began driving them mad, prompting their migration north. In later centuries, the secret mortal cabal known as the Council of Tirisfal chose these shadowed groves to empower solitary Guardians, shielding Azeroth from demonic intrusion.

faq.a: Bajo el palacio de Lordaeron se extendían las antiguas criptas de la realeza humana, junto con el complejo de mazmorras y la vasta red de alcantarillado de la ciudad. Albergaba prisioneros de guerra, incluido Orgrim Martillo Maldito, así como a ciudadanos desfavorecidos que vivían entre las sombras subterráneas. Tras saquear la capital, el príncipe Arthas comenzó a convertir estas catacumbas en una fortaleza de la Plaga antes de que Sylvanas se apoderase de ellas.

La ciudad superficial de Lordaeron quedó completamente destruida durante la Tercera Guerra, lo que dificultaba su defensa frente a la Cruzada Escarlata, las fuerzas de la Plaga y los supervivientes de la Alianza. Los túneles subterráneos ofrecían una fortificación natural, puntos de estrangulamiento y discreción, permitiendo a los Renegados completar la construcción inicial de la Plaga y prosperar sin ser vistos.

La ciudad está gobernada por Lady Sylvanas Brisaveloz, la Reina Alma en Pena y Reina de los Renegados. Administra su reino desde el Barrio Real, protegida por centinelas reales renegados y su subyugado lugarteniente señor del terror, Varimathras.

Sobre los ascensores principales de la ciudad reposa un monumento de piedra para el difunto rey Terenas Menethil II. No alberga sus restos, ya que su cadáver fue incinerado y sus cenizas esparcidas durante la resurrección de Kel'Thuzad. Valientes supervivientes humanos de la Alianza esculpieron el monumento entre las ruinas para que perdurara el recuerdo del último verdadero rey de Lordaeron.

En la derruida sala del trono situada sobre los ascensores de Entrañas, aún persisten ecos espectrales del pasado. Quienes se sitúen en el centro pueden escuchar tenues sonidos fantasmales: las campanas de celebración y los pétalos de rosa del regreso de Arthas, las palabras de advertencia del profeta Medivh y la conversación final entre el rey Terenas y su parricida hijo.

Los Renegados sellaron una alianza por conveniencia con la Horda del Jefe de Guerra Thrall para sobrevivir, rodeados como están por los hostiles fanáticos escarlata y las legiones de la Plaga. Aunque a las razas vivas de la Horda los vapores tóxicos y los ríos alquímicos les resultan asfixiantes, se concede paso a emisarios y viajeros para fomentar los lazos diplomáticos y militares.

zone:undercity.s: Entrañas. En las profundidades de las ruinas devastadas de la Ciudad Capital de Lordaeron se halla Entrañas, el oscuro bastión de los Renegados. Excavada originalmente en antiguas criptas reales y mazmorras por la Plaga, fue tomada por Lady Sylvanas Brisaveloz y transformada en un santuario subterráneo impenetrable. Hoy en día sirve como sede del poder de los Renegados y vital bastión de la Horda en el norte de los Reinos del Este. Mucho antes de que la plaga asolara Lordaeron, las catacumbas, mazmorras y cloacas situadas bajo el palacio se conocían colectivamente como Entrañas. Albergaban las tumbas de la nobleza, las prisiones más profundas del reino —donde el antiguo Jefe de Guerra Orgrim Martillo Maldito estuvo recluido antes de su fuga— y a los habitantes más pobres del territorio. Cuando Arthas Menethil asesinó al rey Terenas y arrasó la capital en el año 20 d. P., el príncipe ordenó a sus sirvientes no-muertos excavar y ampliar los pasadizos subterráneos para convertirlos en una sede fortificada del dominio de la Plaga.

ang.faction:Horde: As the Horde's primary foothold in the Eastern Kingdoms, the Undercity secures zeppelin links directly back to Durotar and Grom'gol Base Camp.
ang.race:Human: Beneath the soil of your fallen ancestral kingdom lies a grim perversion of Lordaeron's royal crypts, occupied by the walking corpses of your former brethren.
ang.race:Orc: Deep within these very dungeons, the legendary Warchief Orgrim Doomhammer was once imprisoned by the Alliance of Lordaeron before making his historic escape.
ang.race:Undead: The Undercity is your sovereign sanctuary and homeland, carved out by your own hands after breaking the Lich King's iron grip on your mind.

faq.a: Beneath the palace of Lordaeron lay the ancient crypts of human royalty, along with the city's dungeon complex and vast sewer network. It housed prisoners of war, including Orgrim Doomhammer, as well as destitute citizens living in the subterranean shadows. After sacking the capital, Prince Arthas began turning these catacombs into a Scourge fortress before Sylvanas captured them.
faq.q: What was the Undercity before the undead took it over?

faq.a: The surface city of Lordaeron was utterly ruined during the Third War, making it difficult to defend against the Scarlet Crusade, Scourge forces, and Alliance survivors. The subterranean tunnels offered natural fortification, choke points, and secrecy, allowing the Forsaken to complete the Scourge's initial construction and thrive unseen.
faq.q: Why is the city built underground instead of on the surface?

faq.a: The city is ruled by Lady Sylvanas Windrunner, the Banshee Queen and Queen of the Forsaken. She governs from the Royal Quarter, guarded by Forsaken royal sentries and her subjugated dreadlord lieutenant, Varimathras.
faq.q: Who rules the Undercity?

faq.a: Above the city's main lifts sits a stone memorial for the slain King Terenas Menethil II. It does not contain his body, as his corpse was cremated and his ashes discarded during Kel'Thuzad's resurrection. Surviving Alliance humans bravely carved the monument amidst the ruins so the memory of Lordaeron's last true king would endure.
al: who built the tomb above undercity
faq.q: What is King Terenas's memorial in the ruins above?

faq.a: In the ruined throne room above the Undercity lifts, spectral echoes of the past still linger. Visitors standing in the center can hear faint phantom sounds: the celebratory bells and rose petals of Arthas's return, the warning words of the prophet Medivh, and the final conversation between King Terenas and his patricidal son.
faq.q: What are the strange noises in the Lordaeron throne room?

faq.a: The Forsaken formed an alliance of convenience with Warchief Thrall's Horde for survival, surrounded as they are by hostile Scarlet zealots and Scourge legions. While living Horde races find the toxic fumes and alchemical rivers stifling, emissaries and travelers are allowed access to foster diplomatic and military ties.
al: why is undercity part of horde
faq.q: Why do the Forsaken allow other Horde members here?

text.s: Deep beneath the shattered ruins of Lordaeron's Capital City lies the Undercity, the dark stronghold of the Forsaken. Originally carved out of ancient royal crypts and dungeons by the Scourge, it was seized by Lady Sylvanas Windrunner and remade into an impenetrable subterranean sanctuary. Today it serves as the seat of Forsaken power and the Horde's vital bastion in the northern Eastern Kingdoms.

sec.b: Long before the plague swept Lordaeron, the catacombs, dungeons, and sewers beneath the palace were collectively known as the Undercity. It held the tombs of nobility, the kingdom's deepest prisons—where the former Warchief Orgrim Doomhammer was once held before his escape—and the poorest denizens of the realm. When Arthas Menethil murdered King Terenas and laid waste to the capital in 20 ADP, the prince ordered his undead servants to excavate and expand the subterranean passages into a fortified seat of Scourge rule.
sec.t: From Royal Crypts to Scourge Redoubt

sec.b: The Scourge never saw their dark capital completed. When the Lich King's powers waned following the battle of Mount Hyjal, Lady Sylvanas Windrunner broke free from the hive mind, taking thousands of undead with her. She lured Arthas into an ambush and drove him back to Northrend. After a vicious three-way civil war against Scourge remnants, dreadlords, and human resistance, Sylvanas claimed the half-finished catacombs. Naming her people the Forsaken, she oversaw years of labor completing the sprawling subterranean city.

The Undercity is laid out in concentric rings divided into functional quarters. At its heart lies the Trade Quarter, connected by great lifts to the palace ruins above. Surrounding it are the War Quarter, Rogues' Quarter, Magic Quarter, and the toxic Apothecarium, where the Royal Apothecary Society brews virulent plagues in green slime-filled canals. Deeper still lies the Royal Quarter, where the Banshee Queen holds court alongside her dreadlord commander, Varimathras, guarded by legions of towering abominations.

zone:ungoro.s: Cráter de Un'Goro. El Cráter de Un'Goro es una jungla primordial y hundida, encajada entre los áridos páramos de Tanaris y Silithus. Dominada por dinosaurios errantes, elementales vivientes y un volcán central, esta exuberante caldera está repleta de antiguas reliquias de los titanes y cristales de poder cuyos orígenes siguen siendo un profundo misterio. Emparedado entre extensiones desérticas, el Cráter de Un'Goro desafía la geografía del sur de Kalimdor. Los antiguos registros de los elfos de la noche que detallan la Guerra del Mar de Dunas señalan que los insectoides qiraji fueron repelidos en los bordes del cráter, incapaces de penetrar en lo que en su lengua llamaban las «Tierras de los Dioses». Los eruditos teorizan que la caldera sirvió como campo de pruebas o antigua morada para los titanes durante la creación de Kalimdor. A lo largo de las crestas se alzan pilones de piedra que vibran con energía, mientras formaciones de cristales azules, rojos, verdes y amarillos brotan a través de la tierra primigenia.

ang.class:Druid: Cenarion Circle druids study Un'Goro's isolated ecosystem and harvest its rich soil to propagate Morrowgrain, seeking to understand the pure, untamed life force sustaining the caldera.
ang.faction:Alliance: Alliance naturalists rally around Williden Marshal and J.D. Collie at Marshal's Refuge, racing to decipher the Titan pylons while safeguarding Darnassus researchers gathering soil samples.
ang.faction:Horde: Horde adventurers often arrive via Tanaris to test their prowess against legendary devilsaurs and assist the herbalists of Thunder Bluff in cultivating Morrowgrain from Un'Goro's primeval dirt.
ang.profession:Herbalism: The rich moisture of the basin sustains rare flora, serving as one of the few places in Kalimdor where Blindweed, Dreamfoil, and Golden Sansam flourish together alongside Firebloom on the volcano's slopes.
ang.profession:Mining: The sheer crater walls and the crags of Fire Plume Ridge are dense with Mithril Deposits and Rich Thorium Veins, making the zone a premier destination for high-end ore.

faq.a: Travelers can enter via natural ramps leading down the crater walls: one accessible from the southwestern corner of Tanaris near Thistleshrub Valley, and another leading in from northeastern Silithus. While reckless adventurers sometimes leap down the cliffs, the fall is fatal without magical assistance. Marshal's Refuge in the north provides flight connections to Gadgetzan and Cenarion Hold.
faq.q: How do you get into Un'Goro Crater?

faq.a: Scattered across the jungle floor are red, blue, green, and yellow Power Crystals. With guidance from the gnome researcher J.D. Collie at Marshal's Refuge, explorers can decipher instructions for using these crystals at the Northern, Eastern, and Western Pylons. Combining specific colors at the appropriate pylons harnesses latent Titan energies to fashion defensive or restorative charms.
al: red blue green yellow crystals ungoro
faq.q: What are the colored power crystals used for?

faq.a: Scholars believe Un'Goro's unnatural vibrancy is artificial, stemming from the Titans who shaped the world. Titanic conduits, warm volcanic geothermal activity from Fire Plume Ridge, and ancient ley energy nourish an isolated, hyper-accelerated ecosystem that resists the arid conditions of neighbouring Tanaris and Silithus.
faq.q: Why is Un'Goro lush despite being surrounded by deserts?

faq.a: According to tablets translated from the War of the Shifting Sands, the insect swarms halted their advance at the crater's threshold. Geologist Larksbane, who translated the account, ties the name to theories that the Titans once dwelt in the crater, and wonders whether Aman'Thul himself watched over the God Lands.
faq.q: Why did the Qiraji call this place the 'God Lands'?

faq.a: Piles of rich, potent dirt rest across the crater basin. When harvested, this soil can be paired with Tharlendris seeds in an Evergreen Pouch to cultivate Morrowgrain, a mystical herb intensely sought after by researchers in Thunder Bluff, Darnassus, and the Cenarion Circle.
faq.q: What is Un'Goro Soil used for?

faq.a: There are no instances, dungeons, or indigenous humanoid societies in Un'Goro Crater. The only lasting settlement is Marshal's Refuge, a small expedition outpost on the northern rim. Beyond isolated hermit hunters or lost explorers, the rest of the caldera is entirely wild.
faq.q: Are there any humanoid settlements or dungeons here?

text.s: Un'Goro Crater is a sunken, primordial jungle tucked between the arid wastes of Tanaris and Silithus. Dominated by roaming dinosaurs, living elementals, and a central volcano, this lush caldera is filled with ancient Titan relics and power crystals whose origins remain a profound mystery.

sec.b: Sandwiched between desert expanses, Un'Goro Crater defies the geography of southern Kalimdor. Ancient night elf records detailing the War of the Shifting Sands note that the insectoid Qiraji were turned back at the crater's edges, unable to penetrate what their tongue named the 'God Lands.' Scholars theorize the caldera served as a testing ground or ancient dwelling for the Titans during the shaping of Kalimdor. Stone pylons rise along the ridges, humming with energy, while crystal formations of blue, red, green, and yellow sprout through the primeval earth.

Un'Goro contains no cities, towns, or native humanoid societies. Instead, life thrives in an untamed, primeval state. Apex devilsaurs stalk the flats of Terror Run, predatory bloodpetals lash out in the marshlands, and oozes creep across the tar pits of Lakkari. At the heart of the crater looms Fire Plume Ridge, an active volcanic peak teeming with hostile fire elementals led by the entity Blazerunner. For explorers and skinners, the basin offers unmatched natural wealth—including the coveted hides of devilsaurs—provided one survives the food chain.

Civilized presence in the crater is limited almost entirely to Marshal's Refuge, an elevated camp tucked into the northern cliffs. Led by Williden Marshal, an expedition of scientists, naturalists, and fortune seekers attempted to catalogue the basin's treasures only to be battered by the monstrous wildlife and driven to high ground. Today, the refuge serves as an embattled staging ground for intrepid travelers studying the crater's mysterious power crystals, mapping volcanic activity, and keeping a watchful eye on encroaching silithid swarms breaching the southern ridges.

zone:westernplaguelands.n: Tierras de la Peste del Oeste
zone:westernplaguelands.s: Tierras de la Peste del Oeste. Antaño el fértil granero agrícola del norte de Lordaeron, las Tierras de la Peste del Oeste se asfixian ahora bajo una niebla tóxica y legiones de no-muertos. Aunque las calderas de Kel'Thuzad arruinaron las granjas y aldeas de la región, la tierra aún se aferra tenazmente a la vida. El Alba Argenta, la Alianza, los Renegados y la Cruzada Escarlata libran desesperadas campañas a lo largo de sus campos marchitos. Antes de la Tercera Guerra, esta tierra era un verde pasillo de granjas que se extendía al este desde los Claros de Tirisfal hacia el Lago Darrowmere. Vega del Amparo gobernaba la administración norteña desde el Fuerte de Mardenholde, mientras que la extensa villa de Andorhal coordinaba el almacenamiento y la exportación de grano a lo largo del reino. Ese crucial papel agrícola convirtió a la región en el objetivo primordial de Kel'Thuzad. Al introducir la plaga de la no-muerte directamente en los cargamentos de grano de Andorhal, el Culto de los Malditos convirtió el sustento de Lordaeron en su perdición.

ang.class:Paladin: The desecrated fields of Lordaeron are a somber trial for holy warriors, offering pilgrimage to Uther's Tomb as well as righteous war against the horrors of Scholomance and Hearthglen's corrupted zealots.
ang.faction:Alliance: Chillwind Camp serves as the forward Alliance garrison, where Commander Ashlam Valorfist directs campaigns to disrupt the plague cauldrons and avenge the fallen cities of Lordaeron.
ang.faction:Horde: The Bulwark marks the frontier of Forsaken sovereignty; from here, the Horde pushes eastward to neutralize Scourge commanders and contest Scarlet zealots along their vulnerable flank.
ang.profession:Herbalism: The lingering taint makes the region one of the few places where rare, dangerous flora like Plaguebloom and Arthas' Tears can take root among blighted pine groves.

faq.a: Andorhal was the agricultural shipping hub of northern Lordaeron. Kel'Thuzad intentionally targeted the regional supply, infecting grain silos and installing massive plague cauldrons across four major farmsteads to rapidly distribute undeath through food shipments across the kingdom.
faq.q: Why did the Plague hit this area so hard?

faq.a: Hearthglen and its fortress, Mardenholde Keep, are ruled by the Scarlet Crusade. Though originally a regional administrative hub for Lordaeron, the zealots now execute any outsiders who approach their borders, viewing all non-crusaders with suspicion.
faq.q: Who controls Hearthglen in the north?

faq.a: The Alliance maintains Chillwind Camp near the southern border with the Alterac Mountains, providing a flight master and Argent Dawn allies. The Horde operates from the Bulwark on the western border entering from Tirisfal Glades.
faq.q: Where can Alliance and Horde players find safe outposts?

faq.a: Erected by the Cult of the Damned at Felstone Field, Dalson's Tears, the Writhing Haunt, and Gahrron's Withering, these cauldrons pump constant plague vapors into the air and soil. Argent Dawn agents recruit adventurers to slay the Cauldron Lords and counter-engineer the toxic brews.
faq.q: What is the purpose of the plague cauldrons in the fields?

faq.a: Scholomance is a subterranean academy of necromancy run by the Scourge and the Cult of the Damned. It is hidden beneath the ruins of Caer Darrow, an island fortress situated in the southeastern waters of Darrowmere Lake.
faq.q: What is Scholomance and where is it located?

faq.a: Uther's Tomb, located on Sorrow Hill near the southern edge of the zone, remains entirely holy and untouched by blight. It stands as a consecrated memorial to the fallen High General Uther the Lightbringer and the lost Order of the Silver Hand.
faq.q: Is any part of the Western Plaguelands uncorrupted?

text.s: Once the fertile agricultural breadbasket of northern Lordaeron, the Western Plaguelands now choke beneath a toxic mist and legions of undead. While Kel'Thuzad's cauldrons ruined the region's farms and towns, the soil still clings tenaciously to life. The Argent Dawn, the Alliance, the Forsaken, and the Scarlet Crusade all wage desperate campaigns across its blighted fields.

sec.b: Before the Third War, this land was a verdant corridor of farms stretching east from Tirisfal Glades toward Darrowmere Lake. Hearthglen governed the northern administration from Mardenholde Keep, while the sprawling town of Andorhal orchestrated the storage and export of grain across the kingdom. That crucial agricultural role made the region Kel'Thuzad's primary target. By introducing the Plague of Undeath directly into the grain shipments at Andorhal, the Cult of the Damned turned Lordaeron's sustenance into its doom.

To permanently poison the soil, the Scourge raised four massive plague cauldrons across the largest agricultural estates: Felstone Field, Dalson's Tears, the Writhing Haunt, and Gahrron's Withering. Today, monstrous Cauldron Lords maintain these noxious vats, pumping venomous fog into the atmosphere. The surrounding trees twist with swollen, tumorous growths, and blighted wildlife rampages through the brush. Beneath Caer Darrow on Darrowmere Lake, Darkmaster Gandling trains necromancers within Scholomance, compounding the undead threat.

Despite the omnipresence of the Scourge, several factions maintain embattled footholds. The Scarlet Crusade controls the fortress of Hearthglen in the north, purging anything they deem tainted with rabid zeal. To the south, Alliance forces stage from Chillwind Camp, while the Forsaken defend their borders at the Bulwark. Mediating and directing the fight against the undead cauldrons is the neutral Argent Dawn, which aids champions of both factions and guards Uther's Tomb—the last truly sanctified ground in the region.

zone:westfall.s: Páramos de Poniente. En su día el fértil granero del Reino de Ventormenta, Páramos de Poniente se ha desmoronado hasta convertirse en un territorio azotado por el viento y abandonado, infestado de forajidos. Privados del apoyo oficial de la corona y de guarniciones militares, los colonos supervivientes se aferran a sus granjas mientras la Hermandad Defias afianza su dominio desde el pueblo minero abandonado de Arroyo de la Luna. Durante generaciones, Páramos de Poniente alimentó al Reino de Ventormenta. Sus ondulantes pastos y trigales prosperaron hasta que las secuelas de la Segunda Guerra trajeron el agotamiento financiero y la negligencia política. Cuando el reino volcó sus recursos en otros lugares y no logró mantener sus guarniciones, el territorio quedó en barbecho. Hoy en día, los pastos yermos, las aullantes ráfagas costeras, los gólems de la cosecha descontrolados y los saqueos de los gnolls Zarparrío convierten la supervivencia diaria en una dura prueba constante para los pocos y obstinados habitantes que se niegan a abandonar sus tierras.

ang.class:Rogue: The shadow war across Westfall pits SI:7 spies directly against the street-smart scouts, thieves, and assassins of the Defias Brotherhood.
ang.faction:Alliance: Without the People's Militia holding Sentinel Hill, the Defias Brotherhood would control the southern approaches straight to Elwynn Forest.
ang.profession:Cooking: The beleaguered homesteaders at Saldean's Farm make do with tough local beasts, teaching travelers to brew the hearty staple known as Westfall Stew.
ang.race:Human: Westfall is a painful reflection of Stormwind's political decay; the farmers starving in the dirt were abandoned by the very nobility they toiled to feed.

faq.a: Stormwind withdrew its military garrisons when upkeep became too expensive, leaving the region unprotected. Soon after, the Defias Brotherhood seized control of the countryside, driving off homesteaders, burning cropland, and reprogramming mechanical harvest watchers into lethal sentries.
faq.q: Why are so many farms abandoned in Westfall?

faq.a: The kingdom's treasury is strained, and the House of Nobles considers threats in other lands to be higher priorities. Furthermore, court manipulation has quietly starved Westfall of attention and supplies, forcing local residents to fend entirely for themselves.
faq.q: Why does Stormwind not send troops to help Westfall?

faq.a: The People's Militia is a volunteer defense outfit organized by Gryan Stoutmantle at Sentinel Hill. Because the crown refused to deploy soldiers to Westfall, the remaining farmers and settlers banded together to fight off the Defias Brotherhood and the Riverpaw gnolls.
faq.q: What is the People's Militia?

faq.a: Edwin VanCleef, the former guildmaster of the Stonemasons Guild who oversaw the rebuilding of Stormwind City. After a bitter dispute over payment resulted in riots and the death of Queen Tiffin, VanCleef led his workers into Westfall and turned to armed insurrection.
faq.q: Who leads the Defias Brotherhood in Westfall?

faq.a: Underneath an unassuming barn in Moonbrook lies the entrance to the Deadmines, an extensive abandoned gold mine that the Defias Brotherhood converted into an underground fortress and shipwright for their war against Stormwind.
faq.q: What is hidden inside Moonbrook?

faq.a: Originally built to tend the crops and scare away pests, these mechanical harvest watchers were captured and retrofitted by Defias-aligned goblin tinkerers to patrol fields and murder any trespassers.
faq.q: Why are the mechanical scarecrows attacking people?

text.s: Once the fertile breadbasket of the Kingdom of Stormwind, Westfall has collapsed into a windswept, neglected territory overrun by outlaws. Deprived of official crown support and military garrisons, its surviving homesteaders cling to their farms while the Defias Brotherhood tightens its grip from the abandoned mining town of Moonbrook.

sec.b: For generations, Westfall fed the Kingdom of Stormwind. Its rolling pastures and wheat fields flourished until the aftermath of the Second War brought financial exhaustion and political neglect. When the kingdom poured its resources elsewhere and failed to maintain its garrisons, the territory grew fallow. Today, barren pastures, howling coastal gusts, rogue harvest golems, and raiding Riverpaw gnolls make daily survival a constant trial for the stubborn few who refuse to abandon their homesteads.

Westfall's collapse accelerated when the Stonemasons Guild, denied payment for rebuilding Stormwind City, turned to open revolt. Outlawed and exiled under Edwin VanCleef, the stonemasons reconstituted themselves as the Defias Brotherhood. They claimed Westfall as their stronghold, burning stubborn farmers' fields, salting soil, and seizing abandoned mines. Operating out of the ghost town of Moonbrook, the Brotherhood now rules the majority of the countryside in all but name.

With the House of Nobles ignoring Westfall's plight, local inhabitants took up their own defense. Based at the fortified post of Sentinel Hill, Gryan Stoutmantle organized the People's Militia—a volunteer force attempting to hold the line against gnolls and bandits. Lacking formal soldiers and supplies from Stormwind, the Militia relies on wandering adventurers to push back the Defias tide and protect the remaining farms.

The true scale of the Defias threat lies concealed beneath the surface. Deep within the abandoned gold shafts of the Deadmines beneath Moonbrook, Edwin VanCleef has assembled an army of cutthroats, goblins, and renegades. Rather than simple banditry, the Brotherhood is constructing a massive ironclad juggernaut designed to sail up the coast and bombard Stormwind City directly.

zone:winterspring.s: Cuna del Invierno. Cuna del Invierno es un vasto valle cubierto de nieve ubicado en lo alto de las laderas nororientales del Monte Hyjal, justo por encima de los bosques encantados de Claro de la Luna y Frondavil. Conocida por su frío cortante, antiguas ruinas Altonato y formidables depredadores errantes, la región se articula en torno al puesto neutral goblin de Vista Eterna. Sigue siendo una tierra repleta de feroces peligros naturales que acoge a supervivientes del Vuelo Azul mientras combate la corrupción demoníaca a lo largo de sus cumbres meridionales. Encaramada a miles de metros sobre la naturaleza que la rodea, Cuna del Invierno descansa bajo un aire alpino glacial e implacables tormentas de nieve. Las enormes raíces expuestas del Árbol del Mundo, Nordrassil, atraviesan las acumulaciones de nieve como altísimos arcos de madera, deformadas y retorcidas durante las trascendentales batallas de la Tercera Guerra. Mientras que gran parte del norte de Kalimdor está dominada por densas arboledas y climas cálidos, Cuna del Invierno es una tierra apacible de bosques alpinos, peñascos rocosos y lagos helados, hogar de temibles sables de hielo, quimeras, yetis y osos invernales de espeso pelaje.

ang.class:Druid: Located high above Moonglade, Winterspring holds sacred significance as the place where Malfurion Stormrage awakened the Druids of the Talon from their ancient sleep during the Third War.
ang.faction:Alliance: Alliance heroes frequently visit Rivern Frostwind at Frostsaber Rock, working tirelessly in the extreme cold to earn the loyalty of the prestigious Winterspring Frostsaber mounts.
ang.profession:Herbalism: Winterspring is the only known habitat for Icecap, an indispensable alpine herb heavily sought after for advanced alchemical concoctions, along with scattered Mountain Silversage and rare Black Lotus blooms.
ang.profession:Mining: The icy crags and cavern walls across the valley are rich with valuable minerals, frequently yielding Small and Rich Thorium Veins alongside rare Truesilver deposits.
ang.race:NightElf: Winterspring is intimately tied to elven history, featuring the barrow dens where the Druids of the Talon rested for millennia, the tragic ruins of Kel'Theril, and exposed roots of Nordrassil damaged during the Battle of Mount Hyjal.

faq.a: Travelers must journey through Timbermaw Hold, a subterranean network of tunnels located in northeastern Felwood. Navigating the caves peacefully requires earning the trust of the native Timbermaw furbolgs, who will attack any trespassers they deem hostile. Once through the eastern exit, the snowy slopes of Winterspring open up immediately.
faq.q: How do I get to Winterspring?

faq.a: Everlook is managed by the Steamwheedle Cartel, the goblin trading conglomerate. Because of the goblins' strict profit motive and neutrality, both Horde and Alliance travelers can access its flight masters, repair vendors, banking vaults, and trade goods, provided visitors do not break the peace within town limits.
faq.q: Who runs the town of Everlook?

faq.a: They are the spirits of Highborne night elves who once inhabited the ancient city of Kel'Theril ten thousand years ago. When their sorcerers tampered with the stolen Crystal of Zin-Malor, its shattering unleashed a catastrophic curse. Subsequent expeditions of high elves centuries later were similarly driven to madness, doomed to haunt the frozen ruins alongside their ancestors.
faq.q: What are the ghosts haunting Lake Kel'Theril?

faq.a: The Winterfall furbolgs have succumbed to a spreading, unnatural corruption that has driven their clan into maddened hostility. While the nearby Timbermaw hold tightly to their sanity, the Winterfall have fallen under dark influences, prompting researchers like Donova Snowden to study their taint and clear their encampments.
faq.q: Why are the Winterfall furbolgs aggressive?

faq.a: Mazthoril is the primary roost and sanctuary of the blue dragonflight on Kalimdor. Deep within its cavernous spires, wyrmkin, elite whelps, and ancient drakes guard powerful draconic relics and arcane secrets under the watchful eye of Haleh, consort to the Aspect Malygos.
faq.q: What lives inside Mazthoril?

faq.a: Darkwhisper Gorge is a treacherous canyon in the southernmost reaches of the valley, occupied by powerful elite demons leftover from the Third War. It serves as a heavily guarded perimeter along the treacherous trails leading toward the heights of Mount Hyjal.
faq.q: What is Darkwhisper Gorge?

faq.a: At Frostsaber Rock in the far northern reaches of the valley, the night elf Rivern Frostwind tends to the native white cats. Adventurers who assist him with securing provisions and safeguarding the pride may prove themselves worthy of learning the secrets to rearing and riding a Frostsaber.
faq.q: Can you train or tame frostsabers here?

text.s: Winterspring is a vast, snow-covered valley nestled high along the northeastern slopes of Mount Hyjal, directly above the enchanted forests of Moonglade and Felwood. Known for its bitter cold, ancient Highborne ruins, and wandering apex predators, the region is anchored by the neutral goblin outpost of Everlook. It remains a land of fierce natural perils, sheltering remnants of the blue dragonflight while confronting demonic corruption along its southern heights.

sec.b: Perched thousands of feet above the surrounding wilderness, Winterspring rests beneath crisp mountain air and relentless snowstorms. Enormous exposed roots of the World Tree, Nordrassil, cut through the snowdrifts like towering wooden arches, warped and twisted during the climactic struggles of the Third War. While much of northern Kalimdor is dominated by dense woodlands and warm climates, Winterspring is a quiet land of medium alpine forests, rocky bluffs, and frozen lakes, home to formidable frostsabers, chimaeras, yetis, and thick-furred winter bears.

Reaching this high plateau requires traversing the ancient carved passages of Timbermaw Hold, guarded by uncorrupted furbolgs who closely scrutinize any travelers passing from Felwood or Moonglade. At the valley's center sits Everlook, a thriving trading town operated by the Steamwheedle Cartel. Goblins welcome both Alliance and Horde adventurers with open registers, acting as an indispensable haven of engineering, trade, and warm fires against the biting mountain frost.

Centuries before modern settlements arose, ancient elves built the lakeside city of Kel'Theril. After reckless Highborne sorcerers shattered the cursed Crystal of Zin-Malor, madness claimed them, leaving restless phantoms to wander the ruined pillars and frozen waters to this day. Further south rise the cavernous heights of Mazthoril, the traditional Kalimdor stronghold of the blue dragonflight. Here, the brood of the Spell-Weaver Malygos, overseen by the matron protector Haleh, watches over arcane currents and contests local threats.

The serenity of Winterspring is sharply broken along its southernmost border at Darkwhisper Gorge. There, elite demonic forces, remnant legions from the Third War, crawl along jagged canyons blocking the high approaches toward the summit of Mount Hyjal. Meanwhile, the native Winterfall furbolgs have succumbed to foul corruptions, prompting independent researchers like Donova Snowden to investigate the encroaching taint before the entire valley's wildlife is consumed.
sec.t: The Looming Shadow of the Gorge

faq.a: La Isla de Zephras está situada en Muro Celeste, el Plano Elemental del aire, en lugar de sobre la superficie de Azeroth. Flota entre las nubes perpetuas y las corrientes de viento de este dominio etéreo.

La isla dependía de la presencia de elementales de aire nativos que antaño coexistían con los cielonatos. Hace varios siglos, estos elementales desaparecieron, dejando que los cimientos mágicos que anclan y preservan la tierra flotante se debiliten y decaigan lentamente con el tiempo.

Son islas flotantes vecinas en Muro Celeste también pobladas por los cielonatos. La Isla de Zephras perdió la comunicación con ambas cuando los elementales desaparecieron, y los refugiados que huyen informan ahora de que tanto Anvilas como Siroccas se están derrumbando hacia el olvido.

Los cielonatos operan muelles celestes en el asentamiento de Valanaar. Los barcos voladores zarpan desde estos muelles a través de la frontera planar hacia Azeroth, aterrizando cerca de Dalaran en las Montañas de Alterac y en la Meseta de Miracielos en Mulgore.

Los cielonatos son los habitantes que tienen su hogar en la Isla de Zephras y sus reinos celestes hermanos. Tras haber morado en Muro Celeste durante generaciones, ahora afrontan la lenta destrucción de su patria flotante a medida que su magia vinculante se desvanece.

Aparte de las aldeas pacíficas y los refugiados recién llegados, la isla se ve asolada por bandidos locales, garranocturnas cavernícolas y bestias que habitan zonas como la Guarida de Chilladoras y la Caverna Garranoche.

zone:zephras.s: Isla de Zephras. La Isla de Zephras es una isla flotante suspendida en Muro Celeste, el Plano Elemental del aire. Sirve como hogar ancestral de inicio de los cielonatos, cuya sociedad se enfrenta ahora a una crisis existencial a medida que la magia que sustenta la isla se erosiona sin cesar. Con el contacto cortado con los reinos celestes vecinos, sus habitantes luchan contra el colapso elemental y la llegada de refugiados. La Isla de Zephras es una masa de tierra aislada a la deriva en los vientos interminables de Muro Celeste. Durante generaciones, los cielonatos vivieron aquí junto a los elementales de aire nativos que ayudaban a preservar las corrientes mágicas que mantenían la isla a flote. Sin embargo, hace varios siglos, esos custodios elementales desaparecieron por completo. Privados de su presencia y tutela, los encantamientos latentes que sostienen la tierra han comenzado a fallar lentamente, provocando que Zephras se fracture y desestabilice poco a poco.

ang.class:Shaman: Existing directly within the Elemental Plane of air, Zephras Isle showcases what happens to elemental lands when the spirits that balance them suddenly disappear.
ang.race:Skyborne: Zephras Isle is your ancestral home and starting ground, though its lingering beauty masks an urgent crisis of collapsing terrain and fading elemental power.

faq.a: Zephras Isle is situated inside Skywall, the Elemental Plane of air, rather than upon the surface of Azeroth. It floats among the perpetual clouds and wind currents of this ethereal domain.
faq.q: Where is Zephras Isle located?

faq.a: The island relied on the presence of native air elementals who once coexisted with the Skyborne. Several centuries ago, these elementals vanished, leaving the magical foundations that anchor and preserve the flying land to slowly weaken and decay over time.
faq.q: Why is Zephras Isle falling apart?

faq.a: They are neighboring floating islands in Skywall also populated by the Skyborne. Zephras Isle lost communication with both when the elementals disappeared, and fleeing refugees now report that both Anvilas and Siroccas are collapsing into oblivion.
faq.q: What are Anvilas and Siroccas?

faq.a: The Skyborne operate skydocks at the settlement of Valanaar. Airships launch from these docks across the planar boundary to Azeroth, landing near Dalaran in the Alterac Mountains and at Skywatcher Plateau in Mulgore.
faq.q: How do people travel between Zephras Isle and Azeroth?

faq.a: The Skyborne are the inhabitants who make their home on Zephras Isle and its sister sky-realms. Having dwelled in Skywall for generations, they now face the slow destruction of their flying homeland as its binding magic fades.
faq.q: Who are the Skyborne?

faq.a: Aside from peaceful villages and visiting refugees, the island is troubled by local bandits, cavern-dwelling nightclaws, and beasts inhabiting areas like the Shriekling Den and Nightclaw Cavern.
faq.q: Who lives on Zephras Isle besides the Skyborne?

text.s: Zephras Isle is a flying island suspended within Skywall, the Elemental Plane of air. It serves as the ancestral starting home of the Skyborne, whose society now faces an existential crisis as the island's sustaining magic steadily erodes. With contact severed from neighboring sky-realms, its inhabitants struggle against elemental collapse and arriving refugees.

sec.b: Zephras Isle is an isolated landmass adrift in the endless winds of Skywall. For generations, the Skyborne lived here alongside native air elementals who helped preserve the magical currents holding the isle aloft. However, several centuries ago, those elemental stewards vanished entirely. Deprived of their presence and guardianship, the latent enchantments upholding the land have slowly begun to fail, causing Zephras to slowly fracture and destabilize.

Zephras was not the only sanctuary inhabited by the Skyborne within the Elemental Plane. Sister islands known as Anvilas and Siroccas also drifted across Skywall, but communications between them ceased after the elementals vanished. In recent times, refugees from these crumbling neighboring landmasses have managed to reach Zephras seeking safety, bearing grim tidings that the other islands are disintegrating outright beneath their feet.

With their own landmass in slow decay, the Skyborne of Zephras have begun looking beyond the boundaries of Skywall toward Azeroth. From the skydocks of Valanaar, airships now venture forth to establish rare lifelines to the mortal realm. These voyages connect the airy domain directly to points on Azeroth, including the outskirts of Dalaran in the Alterac Mountains and the Skywatcher Plateau in Mulgore.
